commands.label: Load Actions…
commands.params: {"path":".atn file"?,"data":base64 bytes?,"set":name? (override the file's set name),"replace":bool=true (replace the actions of a set of the same name),"encoding":"auto"|label="auto" (the encoding of 8-bit step names: shift_jis, gbk, big5, euc-kr, windows-1252, macintosh…; auto works it out)} → {set, actions:[names], steps, unsupported:[{action, step, event, name}], functionKeys:[{action, key}], warnings, encoding}. Photoshop steps PhotoCraft cannot play become actions.photoshopStep steps (kept for Save Actions; they fail at playback with the step's name); tool selections and other steps with no document effect are imported switched off. Layer references by name replay in any document.

commands.label: Save Actions…
commands.params: {"path":".atn file"? (else the bytes come back as base64 `data`),"set":name? (that set's actions, none for an empty New Set set; default: every action, as the set "PhotoCraft Actions"),"action":name|index? (one action),"skipUnsupported":bool=false (leave out steps with no Photoshop equivalent instead of failing)} → {set, actions:[names], steps, bytes, skipped:[{action, step, id}], path|data}

commands.label: Stop
commands.params: {"message":str,"allowContinue":bool=false} (Photoshop's Insert Stop: a step that shows the message; headless playback continues when allowContinue is set and otherwise stops the action with the message)

commands.label: Menu Item
commands.params: {"id":menu command,"eventKind":"name"|"code"="name"} (a descriptor-free Image Size or unambiguous mapped filter menu event; desktop playback asks for settings when needed, headless playback only runs stateless menu items)

commands.label: Photoshop Step
commands.params: {"event":id,"name":str,"descriptor":base64?} (a step from a .atn file PhotoCraft has no command for: fails at playback, written back by actions.save)

commands.label: Insert Menu Item…
commands.params: {"action":name|index,"id":menu command,"at":index?,"eventKind":"name"|"code"="name"} → {action,step,id,steps}. Records an unambiguous supported menu event without settings. Image Size and mapped filter menu events are supported. Desktop playback opens the existing editor when settings are needed; no-settings items run immediately.

commands.label: Insert Path
commands.params: {"action":name|index,"name":"work"|"layer"|saved path name,"at":index?} → {action,step,id,steps}. Snapshot exactly the selected path as a path.set work-path step, preserving cubic handles and path options. No fallback from a missing Work Path to a layer path. The measured Work Path ATN descriptor supports absolute coordinates, cubic handles, even-odd subpaths and Add/Subtract/XOR. Paths outside that measured form still play natively and are reported as unsupported by ATN export.

commands.label: Allow Tool Recording
commands.params: {"enabled":bool?=toggle} → {enabled:bool}. Opt in to recording painting-tool strokes (off initially). Existing pending steps are committed under the previous mode. Painting, history and the journal are unchanged. actions.list reports toolRecording.

commands.label: Record Again
commands.params: {"action":name|index,"step":index,"params":{new settings},"revision":u64?} → {action,step,id,result}. Replays the selected command and stores its new settings only after success, preserving its enabled/dialog flags. The panel opens the command's editor at the recorded settings. Stop recording or playback first; revision optionally rejects stale library state.

commands.label: Duplicate Action
commands.params: {"action":name|index,"step":index?} or {"set":name} → {action?,index?,step?,steps?,set?,actions?}. Copy an action, step or named set below the source. Copies retain settings and flags, and leave shortcuts with the originals.

commands.label: Insert Step
commands.params: {"action":name|index, "id":command id, "params":{}?, "at":index?=end} → {action, step, id, steps}. Inserts a step at the 0-based position (the reference application's Insert Stop… with id actions.stopMessage, its dialog toggle on; Insert Menu Item… with any command). Pending recorded steps count; flags of the steps after it follow them.

commands.label: Toggle Step Dialog
commands.params: {"action":name|index, "step":index?, "enabled":bool?} → {action, dialogs:[step…]}. The Actions panel's dialog toggle: the desktop shell shows the step's dialog, seeded with its recorded params, and resumes playback when it is confirmed; headless playback runs the recorded params. Omitted enabled flips it; without step, every step: on unless all already are, or as enabled says.

commands.label: Conditional
commands.params: {"if":condition, "then":action name|null, "else":action name|null} → {if, holds, played, ran?, failed?}. Photoshop's Insert Conditional: conditions always|never|isOpen|landscape|square|portrait|modeIsRGB|modeIsCMYK|modeIsGrayscale|modeIsLab|modeIsBitmap|modeIsIndexed|modeIsDuotone|modeIsMultichannel|depth8|depth16|depth32|unsaved|hasSelection|hasLayers|hasAlphaChannels|isBackground|isPixelLayer|isAdjustmentLayer|isShapeLayer|isTypeLayer|isSmartObject|isLayerGroup|isLocked|isVisible|hasPixelMask|hasVectorMask|hasEffects (layer conditions test the active layer). The branch plays as actions.play does; its failure stops the calling action.

commands.label: Move to Set
commands.params: {"action":name|index, "set":name|null} → {action, set}. The set folder the Actions panel shows the action under (what Load Actions fills and Save Actions writes); null takes it out of any set.

commands.label: New Set
commands.params: {"name":str? (default "Set N")} → {set}. An empty set folder in the Actions panel, as Photoshop's New Set… makes; New Action records into the selected set (actions.record's `set`). Save Actions… (actions.save's `set`) writes it even while empty; it is remembered between sessions once it holds an action.

commands.label: History Options…
commands.params: {"automaticallyCreateFirstSnapshot":bool?,"automaticallyCreateNewSnapshotWhenSaving":bool?,"allowNonLinearHistory":bool?,"showNewSnapshotDialogByDefault":bool?,"makeLayerVisibilityChangesUndoable":bool?} → all five values (no params: report them). Automatically Create First Snapshot: a new or opened document starts with a snapshot of itself, named after it (default on). Automatically Create New Snapshot When Saving: each save of the document (not a copy) adds a snapshot named with the time of the save (default off). Allow Non-Linear History: an edit after stepping back keeps the later states and is appended at the end; deleting a state deletes only it (default off). Show New Snapshot Dialog by Default: a click on the History panel's camera button opens New Snapshot, not only ⌥-click (default off). Make Layer Visibility Changes Undoable: showing or hiding a layer is a history state (default on). Also `prefs.set historyOptions.*`

commands.params: {"id":text,"params":json} (plug-in parameters under "params" or at the top level; see plugin.list)

commands.label: Expand/Collapse Group
commands.params: {"layer":id?,"expanded":bool?,"all":bool?} (no expanded: toggle; all: every group; not an undo step)

commands.label: Expand/Collapse Effects
commands.params: {"layer":id?,"expanded":bool?,"all":bool?} (no expanded: toggle; all: every layer with effects or smart filters; view state, not an undo step)

commands.label: Show/Hide Effects
commands.params: {"layer":id?,"index":n?,"visible":bool?} (no index: all of the layer's effects, the "Effects" row; index: the effect at that position in the layer's list; no visible: toggle)

commands.label: View Layer Mask
commands.params: {"layer":id?,"mode":"off"|"gray"|"overlay"|"toggleGray"|"toggleOverlay"="toggleGray","mask":"layer"|"filter"="layer" (filter: a smart object's filter mask)} (gray: the mask alone, ⌥-click its thumbnail; overlay: red rubylith over the composite, ⇧⌥-click or `\`; view state, not an undo step; painting while shown paints the mask)

commands.label: Toggle Layer Mask Overlay
commands.params: {"layer":id?} (shows or hides the active layer's mask as a rubylith over the composite, the `\` key; red at 50% unless Layer Mask Display Options, channel.options {"channel":"mask"}, set it; view state, not an undo step; painting while shown paints the mask)

commands.label: Edit Layer Mask
commands.params: {"layer":id? (default active),"document":id? (reject a stale dialog),"density":0..100?,"feather":0..1000? (pixels)} → {layer,density,feather}; at least one property required; mask pixels are preserved

commands.label: Set Actions History
commands.params: {"singleState":bool} → {singleState}. Persist Create a single history state (default true). Playback Options can use this setting without changing its performance mode.

commands.label: Playback Options
commands.params: {"performance":"accelerated"|"step"|"pause"?, "seconds":1..60?, "singleState":bool?} → {performance, seconds, singleState}. The Actions panel menu's Playback Options, saved in preferences (`actions.performance`, `actions.pauseSeconds`, `actions.createSingleHistoryState`). Step by Step and Pause For pace a person's Play in the app, about one second between steps plus Pause For's whole seconds; actions.play from agents, the CLI and Batch always runs at once. Omitted keys keep their value; {} reads them. Every value is checked before any is stored.

commands.label: Move Action or Step
commands.params: {"action":name|index, "step":index?, "to":index}. Move a step within its action, or the action itself. to is the final zero-based index. Pending recorded steps can be moved.

commands.label: List Actions
commands.params: {} → {actions:[{name, steps:count, set:name|null}], sets:[name…] (every set in panel order, empty ones too), recording:name|null, toolRecording:bool}

commands.label: Get Action
commands.params: {"action":name|index} → {name, steps:[[id, params]…], disabled:[step…], dialogs:[step…], set:name|null, color:str} (steps is the shape file.automate.batch and droplets take; disabled lists the 0-based steps playback skips; dialogs the steps whose dialog Photoshop would show; set the action set from Load Actions; color is the Button Mode swatch, or empty)

commands.label: Record Action
commands.params: {"name":str? (new action, default "Action N"),"set":name? (the set it goes in, as New Action records into the selected set)} or {"action":name|index} (append) → {action, index}

commands.label: Stop Recording
commands.params: {} → {action, steps:count} (steps recorded since actions.record, queries and action-editing commands omitted)

commands.label: Play Action
commands.params: {"action":name|index, "from":step?} → {action, ran, failed?:{step, id, error}}. step and from are 0-based; steps switched off with actions.toggle are skipped. Stops at the first error (the command still returns ok, with failed set) and groups document edits in one Action: <name> history entry by default; actions.setHistory can retain per-step history. Nested calls are supported up to 16 levels; cycles are rejected. Recording stores a named call rather than its expanded commands. Each step is checked with Session::authorize when one is installed.

commands.label: Delete Action
commands.params: {"action":name|index, "step":index?} → {deleted:name} or {action, deletedStep, steps:count}. step is 0-based, including pending recorded steps. Whole-action deletion is refused while recording.

commands.label: Toggle Action Steps
commands.params: {"action":name|index, "step":index?, "enabled":bool?} → {action, disabled:[step…]}. Switch one 0-based step (including pending recorded steps) on or off for playback, Batch and droplets; omitted enabled flips it. Without step, switch every step: on unless all already are, or as enabled says.

commands.label: Rename Action
commands.params: {"action":name|index, "name":str} → {action, index}. The name must not be empty or whitespace-only and must be unique. Nested Play Action steps and the action's function key follow the rename.

commands.label: Set Action Color
commands.params: {"action":name|index, "color":""|"red"|"orange"|"yellow"|"green"|"blue"|"violet"|"gray"} → {action, color}. The Button Mode colour. Empty clears it.

commands.label: New…
commands.params: {preset?: a name from file.newPresets (start from it; the other params change it), name?|title?: document name (default Untitled-N), width?: pt=612|"210 mm", height?: pt=792, units?: "Pixels"|"Points"|"Picas"|"Inches"|"Millimeters"|"Centimeters"|"Feet"|"Yards"|"Meters"|"Feet & Inches" (default: prefs unitsGeneral, as print presets; screen presets: Pixels), orientation?: "portrait"|"landscape" (swaps width and height to match), artboards?: n (1–1000), artboardLayout?: {layout?: "gridByRow"|"gridByColumn"|"row"|"column", columns?: n (default: all in one row), spacing?: pt=20, rightToLeft?: bool}, bleed?: pt|[top, bottom, left, right]|{top?, …} (0–72 pt), backgroundContents?: "transparent"|"white" (a white artboard background, not an object), colorMode?: "rgb"|"cmyk" (a CMYK document starts with CMYK swatches and stores the colours applied to it as CMYK), rasterEffectsPpi?: 72|150|300 (1–2400), previewMode?: "default"|"pixel"|"overprint" (overprint turns Overprint Preview on, pixel Pixel Preview in the app; default leaves both), created?: Unix seconds|null (File Info's created date; default now, recorded in the journal so a replay matches), size?: a preset's size label (a preset file.newPresets lists can be passed back; ignored)} → {index, previewMode}; the size is remembered in file.newPresets' Recent

commands.label: Close
commands.params: {index?}

commands.label: Activate Document
commands.params: {index}

commands.label: Move Document
commands.params: {from?: index (default: the current document), to: index (0 = the first tab; past the last document = the last tab)} → {index}: moves the document to tab `to`, as dragging its tab along the tab strip does; the documents between shift by one, the order Window › Next/Previous Document steps through follows, and the current document stays the current one

commands.label: Inspect Document
commands.params: {depth?, childLimit?, ids?: [id…] (list just these nodes, of any level, in this order, under `nodes` in place of `layers`; an unknown id is an error; at most 10000), kind?: panel label such as Layer; Group; Path; Type or Image (exact, ignoring case; list every such node under `nodes`, each with `path`, its ancestor ids with the layer first, searching the subtrees of `ids` when given), limit?: at most this many entries of the list, offset?: entries skipped first (default 0; with `ids`, `kind`, `limit` or `offset` the reply adds `total`, the entries before paging)} → layer tree (each node: id, name, kind, visible, locked, bounds, opacity (0–1) and opacityPct (0–100 %, the scale object.setProps takes) when below 1, blend when not Normal, fill, stroke and strokeWidth of objects and compound paths; a compound path's members have compoundMember: true instead of paint, which is the compound's), artboards, selection, history (a sliced tree reports childCount); without the scope options the reply is the whole layer tree

commands.label: Inspect Object
commands.params: {id, summary?: compact summary, depth?: child levels in the summary (default all), childLimit?: children shown per node (default all; a level that shows fewer reports childCount)} → one object

commands.label: Find Objects
commands.params: {name?: substring of the Layers panel name, kind?: panel label such as Group; Path; Type or Image (exact), text?: substring of type content, within?: [x, y, width, height] (an object's geometric bounds inside this rectangle, edges included; document points as document.inspect's bounds; layers never match this or the size filters), intersects?: [x, y, width, height] (bounds touching or overlapping it), minWidth?, maxWidth?, minHeight?, maxHeight?: pt (the bounds' size), minThickness?, maxThickness?: pt (the smaller of the bounds' width and height), minArea?, maxArea?: pt² (the bounds' width × height), minAnchors?, maxAnchors?: anchor points of a path (a compound path's members together; other objects never match), select?: bool (also select the matches, leaving out hidden and locked ones, those inside another match, and a compound path's members unless the compound path is isolated; Select > Reselect repeats it), limit?: max matches listed (default 100, 0 counts only)} → {matches: [{id, name, kind, path}], total, selected (with select: the count selected)}; at least one filter, all of them matching

commands.label: Document JSON
commands.params: {} → complete document model

commands.label: Units
commands.params: {units: "Points"|"Picas"|"Inches"|"Millimeters"|"Centimeters"|"Pixels"|"Feet & Inches"|"Meters"|"Yards"|"Feet"} the document's units: every length the UI shows and reads (General)

commands.label: Switch Units
commands.params: {} the document's units become the next of Points, Picas, Inches, Millimeters, Centimeters, Pixels, Feet & Inches, Meters, Yards and Feet (the order a right-click on a ruler lists them), Feet going back to Points; one undo step → {units}

commands.label: Ruler Origin
commands.params: {artboard?: index=0 (the active artboard, which artboard rulers measure from)} → {x, y} the rulers' zero point, in absolute document points

commands.label: Ruler Origin
commands.params: {x, y, artboard?: index=0} set the rulers' zero point in absolute document points: the document's with global rulers, that artboard's with artboard rulers (it moves with the artboard); art, guides and command coordinates stay in place

commands.label: Reset Ruler Origin
commands.params: {artboard?: index=0} reset the rulers' zero point to that artboard's top-left corner (with artboard rulers, that artboard's own zero point)

commands.label: Change to Global Rulers
commands.params: {global?: bool (default: toggle)} global rulers measure the whole document from one zero point; artboard rulers (a new document's) from the active artboard's top-left corner, or the zero point set for it. Saved with the document → {global}

commands.label: Drop Artwork
commands.params: {sourceDocument: uid, ids: [id…], grab: [x,y], at: [x,y]} copy 1–10000 editable source objects from an open document to the active document, preserving the grab point and clipboard, as one undo step

commands.label: Clear History
commands.params: {} remove every undo and redo step of the active document (the History panel menu's Clear History): the document stays as it is, and clearing is not an undo step → {cleared: the number of steps removed}

commands.label: New Document from State
commands.params: {index?: a row of the History panel (0: the oldest state kept; default: the current state), created?: Unix seconds|null (File Info's created date; default now, recorded in the journal so a replay matches)} make a new document holding the art as it was at that state, and make it the active document (the History panel's New Document from State button). The new document is named with the next Untitled-N, has nothing selected and no steps to undo or redo, is marked unsaved and links to the same files. It is out of symbol, opacity-mask and pattern editing, with the art drawn in a pattern's tile stored in the pattern as object.pattern.done stores it. The source document and its steps stay as they are, except that typing or a drag in progress is first kept as a step, as edit.undo keeps it; `index` names the row as it was listed before that. An index that names no state is an error and changes nothing → {index: the new document's, title}

commands.label: Begin Undo Group
commands.params: {label?: string} until edit.undoGroup.end, the edits made in the document active at the begin, and in each document opened or created before then (also when no document is open; the edits of a command that opens a document and edits it stay that command's undo step), are one undo step in that document, named `label` (else after its first edit); in a document that was open before the begin and is switched to (document.activate), each edit stays its own undo step: for automation, such as MCP command_batch with `atomic` (#1163)

commands.label: End Undo Group
commands.params: {cancel?: bool} close the undo group: its edits stay one undo step or, with `cancel`, are undone

commands.label: Cut
commands.params: {lockedAndHidden?: bool (the Artboard tool chosen, as artboard.cut)} (selected ruler guides go too; the Artboard tool chosen: artboard.cut)

commands.label: Copy
commands.params: {lockedAndHidden?: bool (the Artboard tool chosen, as artboard.copy)} the selection with what it uses, and the selected ruler guides (pasted on the layer new art goes to, moved as the objects are; alone, where they were); the Artboard tool chosen: artboard.copy → {copied, guides}

commands.label: Paste
commands.params: {center?: [x, y], artboardsAt?: [x, y], dx?, dy?, swatchConflict?} paste centred on `center` (the app passes the view centre), else offset by dx/dy (default: the Paste Offset preference). Pasting brings the image blobs, symbols, patterns, global and spot swatches (with the tint swatches of the tints used), gradient swatches, graphic styles, character and paragraph styles and brushes the objects use; one of the same name that differs comes in renamed. swatchConflict, for a swatch whose name the document gives another colour (clipboard.conflicts): "merge" (default: the objects take the document's swatch) | "add" (the pasted swatch comes in renamed) | {name: "merge"|"add"}. With Paste Remembers Layers on (layer.pasteRemembersLayers), objects go back into the layers they came from (by name; made when missing). Artboards copied with artboard.copy come with their art, together right of the last artboard as they lay, or centered on `artboardsAt` (the Artboard tool's canvas menu passes the right-click point; a value that is not [x, y] is an error) (the other paste commands but Paste on All Artboards: where they were), their art back in the layers it came from, and the Artboard tool, when chosen, selects them. In Draw Inside (view.drawMode) the objects go inside the object drawn into, as new art does, and Paste Remembers Layers doesn't apply; edit.pasteInPlace and edit.pasteOnAllArtboards do the same, and in Draw Behind they go behind the selection as edit.pasteInBack puts them; edit.pasteInFront and edit.pasteInBack ignore the drawing mode → {ids, artboard: the first new artboard's index or null, artboards: the new artboards' indices, added: resources added, merged: conflicts merged, renamed: [{kind, from, to}]}

commands.label: Paste in Front
commands.params: {swatchConflict?, artboard?: index (the active artboard: the objects go where they were on the artboard they were copied from, on this one)} paste in place just above the top selected object, or on top of the current layer when nothing is selected (resources and layers as edit.paste) → {ids, added, merged, renamed}

commands.label: Paste in Back
commands.params: {swatchConflict?, artboard?: index (as edit.pasteInFront)} paste in place just below the bottom selected object, or at the bottom of the current layer when nothing is selected (resources and layers as edit.paste) → {ids, added, merged, renamed}

commands.label: Paste in Place
commands.params: {swatchConflict?, artboard?: index (as edit.pasteInFront)} paste where the objects were copied (resources, layers and drawing modes as edit.paste) → {ids, added, merged, renamed}

commands.label: Paste on All Artboards
commands.params: {swatchConflict?} paste a copy on every artboard at the offset the objects had to the artboard they were copied from (resources, layers and drawing modes as edit.paste) → {ids, added, merged, renamed}

commands.label: Clear
commands.params: {ids?, guides?: bool (with ids: also delete the selected ruler guides)} delete the objects `ids`, else the selection (fully selected objects and direct-selected anchors together, else ruler guides)

commands.label: Duplicate
commands.params: {ids?: [id…] (selected first; default: the selection), dx?, dy?} duplicate the selection in place (offset optional)

commands.label: Clipboard as SVG
commands.params: {} → {svg} the copied objects as standalone SVG (null when the clipboard is empty)

commands.label: Load SVG into Clipboard
commands.params: {svg | dataBase64 (SVG or SVGZ bytes), center?: [x, y]} replace the clipboard with the SVG's objects (and the images, patterns and symbols they use), centred on `center` (default: the first artboard) → {count}; then run edit.pasteInPlace

commands.label: Swatch Conflicts
commands.params: {} → {swatches: [{name, document, clipboard, spot}]} the global or spot swatches the copied objects use whose name the active document gives another colour (`document`/`clipboard`: #rrggbb): Paste asks Merge or Add for each (pass the answer as edit.paste* {swatchConflict}). Pasting back into the document the objects came from raises none

commands.label: Clipboard as PNG
commands.params: {scale?: 1 (pixels per point, up to 64)} → {dataBase64, width, height (px), warnings} the copied objects cropped to their visual bounds, transparent around them (dataBase64 null when the clipboard is empty); warnings as for document.export (an image that couldn't be decoded, type in the fallback font or that doesn't fit its frame)

commands.label: Clipboard as PDF
commands.params: {} → {dataBase64, warnings} a one-page PDF of the copied objects, the page their visual bounds (dataBase64 null when the clipboard is empty); warnings as for document.export

commands.label: Clipboard as Text
commands.params: {} → {text} the copied type objects' text, one object per line (null unless every copied object is type, or a group of type)

commands.label: Clipboard Formats
commands.params: {} → {flavours: [mime…]} what Copy offers other apps for the current clipboard, best first, by the Clipboard Handling preferences: text/plain (a type-only copy's text, else the SVG markup with copyAsSvg when the images it embeds total at most 1 MiB), image/svg+xml (copyAsSvg), application/pdf (copyAsPdf), image/png (always; PDF and PNG only for objects with an area); the app publishes them on Copy and Cut

commands.label: Load Image into Clipboard
commands.params: {dataBase64 (PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, TIFF or BMP bytes), mime?: the type the system clipboard gave (an image/… type; the format is read from the bytes), center?: [x, y]} replace the clipboard with the image, embedded at 100% of its physical size (its resolution, else 72 ppi), centred on `center` (default: the first artboard) → {count, width, height (pt), pixelWidth, pixelHeight}; then run edit.paste. A PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP image whose pixels can't be read (a file cut short) is an error

commands.label: Load Text into Clipboard
commands.params: {text, center?: [x, y], table?: true} replace the clipboard with point text of `text` (one paragraph per line; trailing line breaks dropped) in the default type style, centred on `center` (default: the first artboard) → {count}; then run edit.paste. Cells copied from a spreadsheet (tab-separated, at least two columns, every row with the same number of cells, cells in double quotes may hold tabs and line breaks; at most 1000 rows, 256 columns and 20,000 cells) become a group "Table": point type for each cell that holds text, in columns as wide as their widest cell and rows as tall as their tallest, over a group "Gridlines" of 0.5 pt black lines around every cell → {count, rows, columns}; table: false pastes them as plain text

commands.label: Load PDF into Clipboard
commands.params: {dataBase64, page?: 1, password? (an encrypted PDF), editingData?: false (true: the data is a .ai or .ait file, read as document.open reads it; when document.open would use its editing data, every object of that data comes in, each layer's objects in stacking order and a hidden layer's objects hidden; else page `page`), center?: [x, y]} replace the clipboard with the objects of one PDF page, or of a .ai file's editing data (with the images, patterns and swatches they use; a .ai saved without PDF compatibility: every object of its editing data, as document.open reads it, with or without editingData), centred on `center` (default: the first artboard) → {count, warnings}; then run edit.paste

commands.label: Load Metafile into Clipboard
commands.params: {dataBase64 (EMF or WMF bytes), center?: [x, y]} replace the clipboard with the picture's objects (paths, clipping groups, images, point type; the images they use), centred on `center` (default: the first artboard) → {count, warnings}; records VectorCraft doesn't read are skipped with one warning; then run edit.paste

commands.label: Load EPS into Clipboard
commands.params: {dataBase64 (EPS or other PostScript bytes), center?: [x, y]} replace the clipboard with the picture's objects as document.open reads an EPS (editable paths, type and images, with the images, patterns and swatches they use; a hidden layer's objects hidden), centred on `center` (default: the first artboard) → {count, warnings}; then run edit.paste

commands.label: Artwork Colors
commands.params: {ids?: object ids (default: the selection, or with nothing selected the objects select.all takes, without the hidden and locked objects inside them)} → {colors: [{key: colour identity ("rgb 255 0 0", "cmyk 0 100 100 0", "gray 40", "lab 55 60 -40"), hex, count, swatch?: the global swatch it is linked to}]} unique colours used by the objects (fills, strokes, gradient stops, text, mesh points and the tiles of pattern fills and strokes), most used first

commands.label: Recolor Artwork
commands.params: {map: rows [{from: [colour keys (recolor.colors) or "#rrggbb" (every colour shown as that hex)], to: colour (hex, key, {c,m,y,k} or {l,a,b}) | null (in from, to and groupColors, #rrggbbaa and #rgba are refused), exclude?: false (the row's colours are kept), tint?: 100 (percent; with limitTo, art linked to the global or spot swatch the new color is takes this share of its tint)}] | {"key or #rrggbb": colour, …} (one row per colour), method?: "exact" (default)|"preserveTints"|"scaleTints"|"tintsShades"|"hueShift" (how a row's colours take its new colour, relative to the row's darkest, average or most saturated colour), limitTo?: swatch library id or name; or "document" (the document's swatches): new colours snap to its nearest colour, group?: colour group to rewrite, groupColors?: [colour] (what `group` is rewritten with; default: the rows' new colours, in order, excluded rows left out), rename?: the group's new name, includeImages?: true, includePatterns?: true, globalAdjust?: {saturation?: 0, brightness?: 0, temperature?: 0, luminosity?: 0} (Global Adjust: percent from -100 to 100, 0 changes nothing; every colour a row that isn't excluded recolours, and the group's new colours, take the same change after the row's new colour: saturation scales HSB saturation by 1 + saturation/100, brightness moves HSB brightness that share of the way to full or to black, temperature adds 0.2 × temperature/100 to red and takes it from blue, luminosity moves Lab lightness that share of the way to 100 or 0 keeping a and b; with limitTo each row's new colour takes the change before it snaps to the library)} recolour the selection (gradients, text, meshes, image pixels and pattern tiles included; each new colour keeps the model of the one it replaces (model?: "keep" default | "new" (the new colour's own model, so a CMYK colour replacing RGB art gives CMYK art) | "document" (the document's colour mode)), except a library swatch's with limitTo: art takes the swatch itself, linked to a global or spot colour at its tints, and the swatch joins the document's swatches; art linked to a global swatch of `group` that is rewritten with its row's new color stays linked to it, at its tint, unless the row converts the color into the art's model; other recolored art, and art in a row linked to a global swatch of `group` that is rewritten with another color, keeps its row's new color and loses its swatch link) and the group, as one undo step → {changed, swatches: [names added to the document's swatches], relinked?: with group, the other paints linked to its global swatches that took their new colors, note?: set when a colour kept a model other than its new colour's (see model)}

commands.label: Reduce Colors
commands.params: {colors?: n (rows; default: one per colour, with the tints of a global swatch in its row), method?: as recolor.apply; default scaleTints (picks each row's colour), preserve?: {white?: true, black?: true, grays?: false} (left out of the rows), limitTo?: as recolor.apply (new colours snap to it), ids?: as recolor.colors} group the colors of the objects (default: as recolor.colors) into rows of similar colours (k-means in Lab, weighted by use) → {map: [{from: [keys, the row's colour first], to: key}], preserved: [keys], method}

commands.label: Randomize Colors
commands.params: {map: rows as recolor.apply, order?: true (shuffle the new colours among the rows that aren't excluded), saturationBrightness?: false (random saturation and brightness, hue kept), seed?: 0} → {map: the rows with their new colours as keys}

commands.label: Open Document
commands.params: {path | name | dataBase64 (a file's path, or its name with its bytes), pages?: "2-3, 5" (PDF/.ai: 1-based, default all; one artboard each) | page?: n, cropTo?: bounding|art|crop (default)|trim|bleed|media (the box each artboard gets; bounding: the art's bounds; trim: the bleed box round it becomes the document's bleed; a PDF-compatible .ai or a PDF saved with its editing data opens on its trim boxes for crop), password? (encrypted PDFs; see document.pdfInfo), textAs?: text (default: point type per line, lines wrapped in a frame as area type where they lay out the same, in the file's fonts by name; missing ones are listed in warnings) | outlines (glyph paths), layers?: true (default: optional content groups become layers with their visibility, print state and lock — art that is off comes in as a hidden layer; other art goes to a layer per page) | false (one layer per page, without the art that is off; Save then asks for a name), editingData?: true (default: an EPS, .ai or PDF that carries its editor's own copy of the art opens from it, with its layers, hidden objects, guides, artboards and the art outside them; a .ai or PDF whose type shows opens from its PDF part with textAs: outlines) | "always" (as true, and a .ai's editing copy is used even where it draws differently from its PDF part, which can be older; the warnings say so) | false (only what its page or PDF part prints, for print pipelines; a .ai saved without PDF compatibility then can't be opened), colorMode?: rgb|cmyk (the mode the document opens in, its colours converted as file.documentColorMode does, grays? as there; default: the file's — a PDF keeps CMYK, Gray and spot inks (spot swatches at a tint) and opens in CMYK when painted mostly in CMYK), grays?: as file.documentColorMode, dxf?: {layout?: "Model" (default) | a paper layout's name (document.dxfInfo lists them), unit?, scale? (the ratio: 1 unit of the art = scale drawing units; default: the drawing at 1:1 in its own unit), fit?: false (scale to fit an artboard of fitTo?: [612, 792], turned to the art's orientation), scaleLineweights?: false (lineweights scale with the art), center?: true (false: the drawing's origin on the artboard's bottom-left corner; fitted art's bottom-left corner), mergeLayers?: false (all art on one layer)} (DXF), crop?: as cropTo (its older name)} → {index, title, format, warnings, restored, missingLinks, modifiedLinks, updatedLinks: [{name, path, ids}]}; any readable format (see document.formats): .vectorcraft/.drawcraft, .svg/.svgz, .pdf/.ai, .ait, ASCII .dxf (each DXF layer with art a layer; blocks symbols; what can't come in is listed in warnings), PNG/JPEG/GIF/WebP/TIFF/BMP (an image opens as a document of its size at the resolution it declares, as file.place sizes it; 72 ppi, 1 px = 1 pt, when it declares none), .emf/.wmf (one artboard, the picture's frame; records VectorCraft doesn't read are skipped with one warning), .eps and PostScript .ai (one artboard, the bounding box: an EPS file VectorCraft wrote restores the document it carries, restored: true; other files are read by a PostScript interpreter — paths, colours and spot inks, clips, gradients, images, type in the fonts named — and come in as their TIFF preview, with a warning, when their PostScript can't be read). A PDF/.ai/.ait or SVG saved with Preserve Editing restores the native document it carries (restored: true; a PDF only when no pages are picked), unless the file was changed elsewhere since or the data can't be read: then its artwork is imported and the first warning says why. Templates (native templates, .ait) open as a new untitled document; a restored .ai keeps its path (Save writes .ai again) and opens on the artboard its editing copy names as active. Linked images are read from their files (looked for at their path, then relative to the document): missing ones show their saved preview (links.relink), modified ones are read again only with Preferences › Update Links: Automatically (else links.update). An SVG's <image> files (relative links from the SVG's folder) stay linked, SVG files become art, missing ones a placeholder in their box (a warning and missingLinks)

commands.label: List Folder

commands.params: {ids?|id?} raise each selected stroke's weight by one step of Units › Stroke (a quarter unit below one unit, then whole units; up to 1000 pt), each from its own weight: the selected objects' active or top stroke, type's stroked characters; objects without a stroke are left alone. With nothing selected (and no ids), the weight of the next object drawn → {objects}

commands.label: Stroke Weight Down
commands.params: {ids?|id?} lower each selected stroke's weight by one step, as stroke.weightUp raises it, down to a quarter unit (a thinner weight is kept) → {objects}

commands.label: Stroke Options
commands.params: {arrowScale?: [start %, end %], swapArrows?: bool, flipProfile?: "along"|"across", brush?: name|null, item?: stroke item index|null, ids?|id?, target?: "object"|"contents"} Stroke panel extras (with nothing selected, all but brush set up the next object drawn)

commands.label: Add to Profiles
commands.params: {name?} save the selected stroke's variable width to the Profile list (kept with the preferences) under `name` (default "Width Profile N"; unique, not a built-in's) → {name}

commands.label: Delete Profile
commands.params: {name?} remove a saved profile from the Profile list (default: the selected stroke's); built-in profiles can't be deleted, and strokes keep their widths → {deleted}

commands.label: Reset Profiles
commands.params: {} remove every saved profile, leaving the built-ins → {removed: count}

commands.label: Width Profiles
commands.params: {} → {profiles: [{id (stroke.set `profile`), label, builtIn, points: [[t, left, right]…]}], current: the selected stroke's profile id or name (nothing selected: the next object drawn's), "custom" when it isn't listed, null without a stroke}

commands.label: Add New Fill
commands.params: {ids?|id?, target?: "object"|"contents"} add a fill on top of each selected object's own stack, on an image right below its Contents row, with its top fill's paint (type without one: its characters' fill; else the default fill). With a fill row active (appearance.setActiveItem), no `ids`, no `id` and no `target: "contents"`, the new fill takes that row's paint, goes right above it, and becomes the active row; appearance.duplicateItem copies a whole row. On a path directly in a graph series, the graph also stores the paint, weight and opacity of the topmost visible fill and stroke (exceptions: docs/mcp.md)

commands.label: Add New Stroke
commands.params: {ids?|id?, target?} add a stroke on top of each selected object's own stack, on an image right below its Contents row, with its top stroke's paint (else the default stroke) and that stroke's weight when it has paint, at least 1 pt. On a path directly in a graph series, the graph also stores the paint, weight and opacity of the topmost visible fill and stroke (exceptions: docs/mcp.md)

commands.label: Clear Appearance
commands.params: {ids?|id?, target?} leave each object one empty fill and stroke (None; a group none of its own) and reset its opacity and blend mode. On a path directly in a graph series, the graph also stores the paint, weight and opacity of the topmost visible fill and stroke (exceptions: docs/mcp.md)

commands.label: Reduce to Basic Appearance
commands.params: {ids?|id?, target?} keep only one visible fill and stroke (without ids: the Appearance panel's active row in place of the topmost one of its kind; else the topmost), without their own opacity, blend mode or effects (a group keeps no rows it lacked), and drop the object's effects. On a path directly in a graph series, the graph also stores the paint, weight and opacity of the topmost visible fill and stroke (exceptions: docs/mcp.md)

commands.label: Appearance Item
commands.params: {index: paint-order item index, ids?|id? (default: the selection), target?: "object"|"contents", opacity?: 0..100, blend?: name, visible?: bool, weight?: pt (strokes), color?|none?|swatch?|gradient? (as paint.setFill), tint?: 0..100, keepModel?: bool (both as paint.setFill), aligned?: bool (index and item are rows of the first target's stack: each other target edits its equal one, as the Appearance panel does for a mixed selection)} edit one fill/stroke of each target object's own appearance stack. On a path directly in a graph series, the graph also stores the paint, weight and opacity of the topmost visible fill and stroke (exceptions: docs/mcp.md)

commands.label: Remove Item
commands.params: {index | indices: [..] (paint-order item indices), ids?|id?, target?, aligned?: bool (index and item are rows of the first target's stack: each other target edits its equal one, as the Appearance panel does for a mixed selection)} remove those fills/strokes from each target object's own stack. On a path directly in a graph series, the graph also stores the paint, weight and opacity of the topmost visible fill and stroke (exceptions: docs/mcp.md)

commands.label: Add Effect
commands.params: {…as effect.apply} same as effect.apply (an alias): {effect: id, params?: {…}, item?: appearance item index|null, ids?, target?} → {ids, index, item}

commands.label: Duplicate Item
commands.params: {index | indices: [..] (paint-order item indices), to?: paint-order index of the copy (with several, of the lowest copy: they land together in their order; default: each right above its item; not with aligned rows of a mixed selection), contents?: count (with `to`: how many items paint below the Contents (Characters) row afterwards; default: it stays between the same items), ids?|id?, target?, aligned?: bool (index and item are rows of the first target's stack: each other target edits its equal one, as the Appearance panel does for a mixed selection)} copy fills/strokes with their effects, as Alt-dragging rows places them. On a path directly in a graph series, the graph also stores the paint, weight and opacity of the topmost visible fill and stroke (exceptions: docs/mcp.md)

commands.label: Reorder Appearance Item
commands.params: {from: paint-order item index | "contents", indices?: [..] (several items instead of from: they move as one block in their order, the lowest landing at `to`; a block landing next to the Contents row keeps its lowest item's side), to, contents?: count, ids?|id?, target?, aligned?: bool (refused when the targets' appearances differ)} move fill/stroke `from` to paint-order index `to`; on a group, layer or type the Contents (Characters) row stays between the same items (a moved item landing next to it keeps its side) unless `contents` says how many items paint below it afterwards. from "contents": move that row so `to` items paint below the members (characters) and the rest above. On a path directly in a graph series, the graph also stores the paint, weight and opacity of the topmost visible fill and stroke (exceptions: docs/mcp.md) → {index: where the item landed | contents: the row's slot}

commands.label: Eyedropper
commands.params: {source: id, ids?, pickUp?, apply? (trees as eyedropper.setOptions, merged over the Eyedropper Options for this call), reverse?: bool, append?: bool, defaultsOnly?: bool} copy the attributes both picked up and applied (by default the whole appearance stack, opacity and blend mode, and from type to type the character and paragraph attributes) from `source` to ids (default: highlighted characters while editing type, after Select All in a frame of threaded text the text of the story's frames, leaving out `source`, otherwise the object selection; highlighted characters reject enabled non-neutral object transparency), the fill, stroke and weight also to the paint defaults; `defaultsOnly` updates only paint defaults and cannot be combined with ids, reverse or append; `reverse` (Alt-click) copies from the first selected object (or ids) onto `source` instead, or with nothing selected what the Eyedropper picked up last (a click without Alt); `append` (Shift+Alt-click) adds the source's fills, strokes and effects on top of each target's stack; placed gradients land at the same place relative to each target's bounds (defaults: fitted to new art). On a path directly in a graph series, the graph also stores the paint, weight and opacity of the topmost visible fill and stroke (exceptions: docs/mcp.md) → {ids}

commands.label: Select Appearance Item
commands.params: {index: paint-order item index in the first selected object's stack | null} make that fill/stroke row the target of the paint.setFill/setStroke, stroke.set/setAdvanced, paint.editGradient/setGradientGeom, transparency.set and effect.* calls that omit `item` (a fill row brings the Fill proxy forward, a stroke row the Stroke proxy); null or any selection change clears it → {index}

commands.label: Show All Hidden Attributes
commands.params: {ids?|id?, target?} make every hidden fill, stroke and effect (the object's and each item's) of each selected object visible again; errors when nothing is hidden. On a path directly in a graph series, the graph also stores the paint, weight and opacity of the topmost visible fill and stroke (exceptions: docs/mcp.md) → {ids}

commands.label: Target Contents
commands.params: {ids?|id?, target?: "object"|"contents"} select the members of the selected groups and layers (or `ids`), as double-clicking the Appearance panel's Contents row does: the panel then lists, and appearance edits change, their own appearance; errors when none has members → {ids}

commands.label: Move Appearance
commands.params: {source: id, target: id, copy?: bool} give `target` (a layer, group or object) the appearance (fills, strokes, effects) and transparency (opacity, blend mode, isolation, knockout) of `source`, as dragging a target circle onto another in the Layers panel does; the source is left with a cleared appearance (as appearance.clear) unless `copy` (Alt-drag). Opacity masks stay; placed gradients keep their place relative to each object's bounds. On a path directly in a graph series, the graph also stores the paint, weight and opacity of the topmost visible fill and stroke (exceptions: docs/mcp.md) → {source, target}

commands.label: Apply Graphic Style
commands.params: {name, add?: bool, ids?|id? (layers too), target?: "object"|"contents"} give the objects (default: the selection; a group or layer itself, its fills and strokes painting its members and its effects applying to them as one piece; target contents: the objects inside instead) the style's appearance, opacity, blend mode, isolate and knockout, and link them to it (placed gradients land at the same place relative to each object's bounds); add: true (Alt-click) adds its fills, strokes and effects on top of the existing appearance instead and unlinks. With nothing selected (and no ids) the next object drawn takes the style instead (see appearance.newArt) → {newArt: true}

commands.label: New Graphic Style
commands.params: {name?, id?} a style from object `id` or the first selected object: its appearance, opacity, blend mode, isolate and knockout (a group without fills or strokes of its own lends its topmost object's, type its characters'; placed gradients are kept relative to its bounds); links the object. Names are made unique → {name}

commands.label: Delete Graphic Style
commands.params: {name} | {names: [name…]} delete styles; their objects keep their look but are unlinked

commands.label: Duplicate Graphic Style
commands.params: {name} → {name}

commands.label: List Graphic Styles
commands.params: {} → {styles: [{id, name, fill, stroke, strokeWidth, fills, strokes, effects: [effect id…], opacity: 0..100, blend, isolate, knockout: "on"|"off"|"neutral", linked: [object ids]}], selected: the style the first selected object is linked to, or null, overrideCharColor}

commands.label: Redefine Graphic Style
commands.params: {name?, id?} replace the style (default: the one the object was last linked to) with the look of object `id` or the first selected object; the objects still linked to it update, and that object becomes linked → {name}

commands.label: Break Link to Graphic Style
commands.params: {ids?|id?, target?: "object"|"contents"} unlink the objects (default: the selection) from their graphic style; they keep their look

commands.label: Rename Graphic Style
commands.params: {name, to} (Graphic Style Options; names are unique and linked objects stay linked) → {name}

commands.label: Select All Unused
commands.params: {} → {names: [the styles no object is linked to]} (the panel selects them)

commands.label: Sort by Name
commands.params: {} sort the styles by name (the Default Graphic Style stays first)

commands.label: Merge Graphic Styles
commands.params: {names: [name…] (two or more), name?} add a style combining the styles' fills, strokes and effects (each style's on top of the ones before it) with the first one's opacity, blend mode, isolate and knockout → {name}

commands.label: Move Graphic Style
commands.params: {name, to: index} move the style to position `to` of the list (0 = first, clamped), as dragging it in the Graphic Styles panel does

commands.label: Graphic Styles Options
commands.params: {overrideCharColor?: bool} Override Character Color (the preference `overrideCharColor`, on by default): applying a style to type replaces its characters' fill and stroke with the style's fills and strokes → {overrideCharColor}

commands.label: New Swatch
commands.params: {name?, color? | colors?: [colour] (one swatch each, in one undo step; #rrggbbaa and #rgba are refused) | swatch? | gradient? | pattern?: name (default: the current fill), tint?: 0..100 (% of the global or spot `swatch`, or of the one the current fill links to), mode?: "gray"|"rgb"|"hsb"|"lab"|"cmyk"|"web" (convert the colour; lab: CIE L*a*b*, how spot colours are usually defined), global?, spot? (a spot colour, always global), group?: colour group name (solid colours only; default: ungrouped), none?: true (the None paint), paint?: paint.setFill params, keepModel?: bool (as paint.setFill)} save a colour, gradient or pattern as a swatch. A tint of a global or spot colour (below 100%, without mode, global or spot) becomes a tint swatch, "Name 40%", linked to its base: it follows edits to the base and applies as that tint of it. Names are unique ("Sky 2"); a colour's default name is its values ("C=10 M=20 Y=30 K=0", "R=255 G=128 B=0", "Gray K=40", "L=55 a=60 b=40") → {name, names: [every new swatch]}

commands.label: Delete Swatch
commands.params: {name? | names?: [swatch or colour group names] (a group goes with its swatches), unlink?: true (art using a deleted global swatch keeps its colour, unlinked; false keeps the stale link)} delete in one undo step → {deleted, unlinked: paints unlinked}

commands.label: New Color Group
commands.params: {name?, swatches?: [names] (solid colours move into the group; gradients, patterns and None stay), colors?: [colour] (added as new swatches; #rrggbbaa and #rgba are refused), keepModel?: bool (as paint.setFill), fromArtwork?: false (add the unique colours of the selected art: fills, strokes, text, gradient stops and mesh points; a colour linked to a global swatch moves that swatch into the group), toGlobal?: true (with fromArtwork: the new swatches are global and the selected art's matching unlinked colours link to them), includeTints?: false (with fromArtwork: tints of global swatches also get swatches of their own)} → {name, swatches: [names in the group], linked: paints linked}

commands.label: Duplicate Swatch
commands.params: {name}

commands.label: Swatch Options
commands.params: {name, newName?, color? (e.g. {l, a, b} for a Lab colour; #rrggbbaa and #rgba are refused), keepModel?: bool (as paint.setFill; the swatch's own color and a color given with mode keep their model), mode?: "gray"|"rgb"|"hsb"|"lab"|"cmyk"|"web" (convert the colour), global?, spot? (spot colours are always global), paint?: paint.setFill params ({color}, {gradient}, {swatch} or {pattern}) replacing the swatch's colour; gradient or pattern with one of the same kind} edit a swatch in any colour group, as one undo step. Fills, strokes, text, gradient stops and tint swatches linked to a global swatch take its new colour (at their own tint) and name; turning Global off unlinks them (they keep their colour). Colour, mode and spot apply to solid colours only; a tint swatch only takes a new name (edit its base) → {name, relinked: paints changed}

commands.label: Swatches
commands.params: {group?: name (only that colour group's swatches)} → {swatches: [{name, kind: "none"|"color"|"gradient"|"pattern", group, global, spot, color?, hex?, tintOf?: base swatch of a tint swatch, tint?: its %, gradient?, pattern?}] (the built-in [Registration] after None: it prints on every plate and can't be edited, moved or deleted), groups: [{name, swatches: [names]}]}

commands.label: Move Swatch
commands.params: {name? | names?: [swatch names, in order; or colour group names to reorder the groups], to?: index in the destination (they go before the swatch or group now there; default: the end), group?: destination colour group (default: the ungrouped swatches; groups hold solid colours only)} reorder swatches or move them into or out of colour groups, as one undo step → {moved}

commands.label: Add Used Colors
commands.params: {selection?: false (only the selected art's colours; default: all the art's), global?: false (the new swatches are global and the matching unlinked colours in that art link to them)} add a swatch for each colour used (fills, strokes, text, gradient stops, mesh points) that no solid swatch has yet, as one undo step → {added: [names], linked}

commands.label: Select All Unused
commands.params: {} → {names: [the swatches nothing uses, in panel order]}: a colour is used when a paint links to it or an unlinked paint, gradient stop or mesh point has its colour; a gradient when a gradient links to it or has its stops; a pattern when it fills or strokes anything (art, symbols, pattern tiles and graphic styles count). None is never listed

commands.label: Merge Swatches
commands.params: {names: [two or more solid-colour swatches], name?: the merged swatch's name (one swatch kept)} keep the first (its name and colour) and delete the others; paints linked to them take its colour and link to it (or unlink when it isn't global), as one undo step → {name, merged: [deleted names], relinked}

commands.label: Ungroup Color Group
commands.params: {name: colour group} move its swatches to the end of the ungrouped swatches and remove the group, as one undo step → {swatches: [names]}

commands.label: Sort by Kind
commands.params: {} order the swatches of each list by kind (None first, then process colours, spot colours, gradients, patterns; colour groups stay after them), keeping their order within a kind, as one undo step

commands.label: Spot Colors
commands.params: {useLab?: bool (omitted: unchanged)} the document's Spot Colors options: spot colours defined in Lab show, print and export from their Lab values (true, the default: PDF Separation spaces get a Lab alternate) or from their working-CMYK equivalents (false: a DeviceCMYK alternate, matching older files). Art, gradient stops and tint swatches linked to Lab spot swatches take the chosen colour at their tint, as one undo step → {useLab, relinked: paints changed}

commands.label: Edit Color Group
commands.params: {group: colour group, colors: [colour] (hex, key, {c,m,y,k} or {l,a,b}; #rrggbbaa and #rgba are refused; the group's swatches take them in order, extra colours become new swatches, swatches past the end are removed; built-in swatches can't change; a color the swatch already has keeps its model), keepModel?: bool (as paint.setFill), rename?: new group name} rewrite a colour group as one undo step; art linked to its global swatches takes their new colours (and keeps its colour, unlinked, when its swatch goes) → {name, swatches: [names], relinked}

commands.label: Gradient
commands.params: {stroke?: bool (default: the targeted item's kind, else the active proxy), kind?: linear|radial|freeform (freeform places points on each object, coloured along the stops), mode?: points|lines (freeform: how the Gradient tool adds points), method?: classic|perceptual (how the colours between the stops mix: in display RGB, or perceptually (OKLab) so the steps look even; SVG exports draw a Perceptual gradient as an image, and PDF exports do too unless it is linear or radial, has spot color stops, every other stop is paper white or written in CMYK or gray (an export that converts colors to a CMYK destination profile writes RGB and Lab stops in CMYK, and so does a CMYK document unless the export converts colors to an RGB destination profile), it is not a dithered fill and its curve does not have too many stops: then PDF writes tints of one spot ink as a Separation shading in that ink, and spot inks mixed with other spot, CMYK or gray inks as a DeviceN shading; freeform gradients mix their own way), stops?: [{offset 0..1, color? (needed without swatch; #rrggbbaa and #rgba are refused), opacity? 0..1 (or 0..100), midpoint? 0.13..0.87, swatch?: colour swatch name (a global or spot colour or tint swatch links the stop, so swatch edits recolour it and a spot stop prints on its plate; a process colour just gives its colour), tint?: 0..100 (% of the linked swatch; default 100, or a tint swatch's own)}] (at least 2; a freeform gradient's points are recoloured along them), keepModel?: bool (as paint.setFill; a stop color the gradient already has keeps its model), angle?: deg, aspect?: %, reverse?: bool, dither?: bool (fills only: a linear or radial gradient fill is drawn with fine noise that hides banding, and as pixels in SVG and PDF exports), item?: fill/stroke item index|null (omitted: the Appearance panel's active item when it is of the edited kind), ids?|id?, strokeMode?: within|along|across (strokes only: the gradient lies on the page and shows through the stroke, runs from the start of each subpath to its end, or runs from the stroke's left edge to its right all along it; with nothing selected, for the next object drawn; type characters' own strokes always paint within), target?: "object"|"contents"} edit the gradient in place (keeps its placement); solid/none paints become the default gradient

commands.label: Gradient Vector
commands.params: {start?: [x,y], end?: [x,y] (document coordinates; both or neither: omitted, the vector stays), aspect?: % (radial: the extent ellipse's height / width; default: kept), focal?: [x,y] (document coordinates) | null (radial: the focal point, where the first stop sits, pulled inside the extent ellipse; null centres it; default: it keeps its place in the ellipse), ids?|id?, stroke?: bool (default: the targeted item's kind, else the active proxy), item?: fill/stroke item index|null (alias: index; omitted: the Appearance panel's active item when it is of the edited kind), target?: "object"|"contents", index?: appearance item index (as item)} set the gradient vector, aspect ratio and focal point (solid paints become the default gradient; type objects set it on their runs, in text space)

commands.label: Select Gradient Stop
commands.params: {index: stop index (0 = the start) | null to clear} select a stop of the gradient behind the active proxy (the first selected object's, else the default paint): the stop the Gradient tool's annotator, the Gradient and Color panels and Delete/arrow keys act on → {index}

commands.label: Gradient Presets
commands.params: {} → {presets: [{name, library: the built-in library (theme) it comes from, null for a saved one, builtIn, gradient: {kind, stops, method?, dither?} (as paint.setFill's `gradient`)}]} the Gradient panel's presets: the built-in ones by library, then the saved ones; names are unique

commands.label: Apply Gradient Preset
commands.params: {name: a preset's name (gradient.presets.list), stroke?, item?, ids?|id?, target? (as paint.editGradient)} give the gradient behind the active proxy (or the targeted fill or stroke) the preset's type, stops and method, and a fill its dither, keeping its placement; a solid or no paint becomes the gradient. One undo step, as paint.editGradient → {name, ids: the objects painted (none: only the default changed)}

commands.disabled_reason: the active paint is not a gradient
commands.label: Save Gradient Preset
commands.params: {name?: (default: a new "Gradient Preset N"; unique, any case, and not a built-in preset's)} save the gradient behind the active proxy (paint.toggleActive picks Fill or Stroke) as a preset, kept with the preferences: its type, stops, method and dither (stops linked to a swatch keep their colour, unlinked) → {name}

commands.label: Delete Gradient Preset
commands.params: {name?: a saved preset (default: the saved preset the active proxy's gradient is)} remove a saved preset; built-in presets can't be deleted, and painted art keeps its gradient → {deleted}

commands.label: Make Opacity Mask
commands.params: {ids?, clip?, invert?} the topmost of the selected objects (or of `ids`) becomes the mask of the others (grouped if several; a layer among several stands for its art, so the topmost object of a layer on top is the mask; an object in `ids` that is hidden, locked or on a locked artboard is refused). One object gets an empty mask and enters mask editing: draw the mask, then transparency.stopEditingOpacityMask; one target (an object or a layer) is refused in isolation mode and in pattern editing mode → {id, editing}

commands.label: Release Opacity Mask
commands.params: {id?|ids?} put the mask art back above each masked object (default: the selection, or the object whose mask is being edited, which leaves mask editing)

commands.label: Disable Opacity Mask
commands.params: {id?|ids?} keep the mask but stop applying it

commands.label: Enable Opacity Mask
commands.params: {id?|ids?}

commands.label: Unlink Opacity Mask
commands.params: {id?|ids?} the object moves without its mask

commands.label: Link Opacity Mask
commands.params: {id?|ids?}

commands.label: Opacity Mask Options
commands.params: {id?|ids?, clip?, invert?, disabled?, linked?} change the opacity masks of `ids`, the selection, or the object whose mask is being edited

commands.label: New Opacity Masks Are Clipping
commands.params: {value?} → {value}

commands.label: New Opacity Masks Are Inverted
commands.params: {value?} → {value}

commands.label: Opacity Mask Info
commands.params: {id?|ids?} → [{id, clip, invert, disabled, linked, art}] the opacity masks of `ids`, the selection, or the object whose mask is being edited

commands.label: Transparency Info
commands.params: {id?|ids?} → {ids, opacity: 0..100, blend, isolate, knockout: "on"|"off"|"neutral", knockoutShape, editingMask, pageIsolatedBlending, pageKnockoutGroup} the Transparency panel's values for `ids`, the selection, or the object whose mask is being edited. A value is null where those objects differ (or there are none); editingMask is the id of the object whose mask is being edited, or null; the page values are the document's

commands.label: Page Isolated Blending
commands.params: {value?} make the page an isolated group (default: toggle): blend modes of top-level objects don't blend with what lies under the page; saved with the document and written to PDF → {value}

commands.label: Page Knockout Group
commands.params: {value?} make the page a knockout group (default: toggle): its layers (the contents of neutral layers) hide what they cover instead of showing it through their transparency; saved with the document and written to PDF → {value}

commands.label: New Layer…
commands.params: {name?, top?: bool, below?: bool, color?, template?, locked?, visible?, printable?, preview?, dimImages?} a layer directly above the current layer, at its level (a sublayer beside a current sublayer); `top`: above all layers (Ctrl/Cmd-click the button); `below`: directly below the current layer, at its level (Ctrl/Cmd+Alt-click the button), not with `top`. Options as layer.setProps; refused while an opacity mask is edited (the Layers panel lists only the mask) → {id}

commands.label: New Sublayer…
commands.params: {parent?: layer id (default: the highlighted row's layer, else the current layer), bottom?: bool, name?, …options as layer.new} a sublayer on top of the parent's contents; `bottom`: under the parent's contents, above a clipping layer's clipping path (Ctrl/Cmd+Alt-click the button); refused while an opacity mask is edited → {id}

commands.label: Delete Selection
commands.params: {ids?|id?} delete rows: layers, sublayers, groups or objects with what they hold (default: the highlighted rows, else the current layer). The last layer stays → {deleted}

commands.label: Duplicate Selection
commands.params: {ids?|id?} copy rows (default: the highlighted rows, else the current layer), each just above its original; a layer's copy is named `<name> copy`. The copies are highlighted → {ids}

commands.label: Set Current Layer
commands.params: {id} click a row: it alone is highlighted, and the layer it is (or the layer it is in) becomes the current layer, where new art goes. Not an undo step → {id, layer}

commands.label: Highlight Rows
commands.params: {ids, mode?: "set"|"add"|"toggle"} highlight Layers panel rows (Shift-click: a range, Ctrl-click: toggle one); the last one's layer becomes current. Not an undo step → {rows}

commands.label: Layer Options…
commands.params: {ids?|id? (default: the highlighted rows, else the current layer), name? (with prefs.identifyObjectsBy xmlId: a valid XML ID, stored as the object name), visible?, locked?, template?, printable?, preview?, dimImages?: 0..100|false, color?: index 0..26|"#rrggbb"|preset name (a hex color with an alpha part, #rrggbbaa or #rgba, is an error)} Layer Options; rows that are not layers take name, visible and locked. Template on also locks the layer and dims its images to 50% (unless given); off unlocks it and stops dimming. One undo step

commands.label: Collect in New Layer
commands.params: {ids?} move rows (default: the highlighted rows, else the selected objects) into a new layer where the topmost of them was (a sublayer when they are in a layer), deselecting every selected object left hidden or locked (the key object too) → {id}

commands.label: Select Art
commands.params: {id, add?: bool} the Layers panel's selection column: select the visible, unlocked art of a layer (its sublayers' too), or the object itself; `add` (Shift-click) adds it to the selection, or removes it when it is all selected already → {selected: [..]}

commands.label: Move Rows
commands.params: {ids|id, target, place?: "above"|"below"|"inside" (default inside), copy?: bool} drag rows in the Layers panel: above or below the target row (beside it, in its layer or group), or inside a layer or group (on top of its contents). Layers go only in layers or at the top level, objects in layers and groups; an object placed beside a top-level layer goes inside it. A row never goes into itself; a locked layer or group takes nothing. `copy` (Alt-drag) moves copies. Every selected object left hidden or locked, such as one moved into a hidden layer or group, is deselected (the key object too). One undo step → {ids}

commands.label: Reorder
commands.params: {id, parent?: id (null = top level), index} put a row at `index` (0 = bottom) of `parent` (layers only at the top level or in layers), deselecting every selected object left hidden or locked (the key object too)

commands.label: New Artboard
commands.params: {x?, y?, width?, height?, name?, color?: color (its background color, as artboard.setProps takes it, #rrggbbaa and #rgba refused; default: none), showCenterMark?: bool, showCrossHairs?: bool, showVideoSafeAreas?: bool (as artboard.setProps takes them; default false), videoRulerPixelAspectRatio?: number 0.1–10 (as artboard.setProps takes it; default 1)} (default place: right of the last)

commands.label: Delete Artboard
commands.params: {index | indices: [index…]} delete artboards (with their guides) in one step; one is always left, and a locked one is an error

commands.label: Delete Empty Artboards
commands.params: {} delete every artboard with no artwork on it (no object, hidden, locked and template art included, whose visual bounds meet or touch it, clip groups and clipping layers by their members inside the clip; guides don't count), with its guides, in one step; locked artboards stay; when every artboard is empty and none is locked, artboard 1 stays (with a locked one left, artboard 1 can go) → {deleted: [index…]} (the indices before deleting)

commands.label: Artboard Options…
commands.params: {index | artboards: [{index, name?, color?, locked?, showCenterMark?, showCrossHairs?, showVideoSafeAreas?, videoRulerPixelAspectRatio?, x?, y?, width?, height?}…] (several artboards in one undo step, each with its own fields; the art inside each before any of them changes goes with it, and an object inside several goes with the first listed that moves or scales its art), name?, color?: color ("#rrggbb", {c,m,y,k}, … as the paint commands take, #rrggbbaa and #rgba refused: the background color the canvas draws the artboard's paper in, multiplied with the Simulate Colored Paper color while that is on; exports and print leave it out) | null (no background color), locked?: bool (the Artboards panel's lock column: a locked artboard keeps its rectangle (a new x, y, width or height is an error unless locked is false), can't be moved, deleted or cut, and Rearrange and Fit to Artwork Bounds leave it as it is; the art on it (each object of a layer or sublayer whose bounds with strokes overlap it, a group as one object) acts as locked art until it is unlocked: clicks, marquees, select.set, select.all and the tools pass over it (art drawn or pasted onto it stays selected and editable until a selection leaves it out or it is moved off the locked artboards), it is deselected, and when another artboard moves or scales it stays unless lockedAndHidden), showCenterMark?: bool (Artboard Options' Show Center Mark: the canvas draws a mark at the artboard's center), showCrossHairs?: bool (Show Cross Hairs: the canvas draws a line from the middle of each side through the center), showVideoSafeAreas?: bool (Show Video Safe Areas: the canvas draws the action-safe area 3.5% and the title-safe area 5% in from each edge, as EBU R 95 sets them; the three are screen-only, as the artboard's edges are: exports and print leave them out), videoRulerPixelAspectRatio?: number 0.1–10 (Video Ruler Pixel Aspect Ratio: the width of one video pixel over its height, which View › Rulers › Show Video Rulers counts the artboard in; default 1, square pixels), x?, y?, width?, height?, moveArt?: bool (default false; a position-only change moves the contained art with its artboard), scaleArt?: bool (Scale Artwork with Artboard: resized, the artboard takes the art fully inside it (locked and hidden art only with lockedAndHidden?: bool, default prefs moveLockedWithArtboard) and its guides from its old rectangle onto the new one, each side by its own ratio; strokes/corners/patterns as object.scale), strokes?: bool, corners?: bool, patterns?: bool (the three as object.scale, for art that moves or scales with the artboard), lockedAndHidden?: bool (locked and hidden art moves along; default: the preference; recorded in the journal so a replay matches)} → null, or with scaleArt {scaled: the art scaled}

commands.label: Fit to Artwork Bounds
commands.params: {index?: n | indices?: [n…] (0-based; the app passes the selected artboards: the Artboard tool's, else the active one; default: the first)} each artboard fits the art on it that shows (with its strokes and effects; hidden objects and layers, guides and template layers don't count), in one undo step (none when every artboard already fits): an object counts for every artboard its bounds overlap, and a group or clipping layer counts as one object; an artboard with no art, or a locked one, stays as it is, and the command fails when every artboard it names is locked or none has art

commands.label: Fit to Selected Art
commands.params: {index?: n (0-based; the app passes the active artboard; default: the first)} the artboard fits the selected art (with its strokes); a locked artboard stays as it is (an error when the fit would change it)

commands.label: Make/Release Clipping Mask
commands.params: {id?: layer or group (default: the one highlighted layer or group row, else the one selected group, else the current layer)} make: its top object (a path, compound path or text, which loses its paint) clips the rest and moves to the bottom (new art added on top is clipped); release: it stops clipping, the clipping path stays unpainted → {clip}

commands.label: Target
commands.params: {id, add?: bool (Shift-click: the item joins the selection, or leaves it when all selected; nothing is targeted)} target a layer, group or object as clicking its target circle in the Layers panel does: a layer gets its visible, unlocked art (its sublayers' too) selected and becomes the current layer, and appearance.*, effect.*, transparency.* and the opacity-mask commands without `ids` then act on the layer itself; anything else is selected. Any other selection change ends the targeting (`document.inspect` → target) → {id, selected: [..]}

commands.label: Paste Remembers Layers
commands.params: {on?} (default: toggle) the document option: on, the Paste commands put objects back into the layers they were copied from (by name; a missing one is made on top), off into the current layer; one undo step when it changes (document.inspect → pasteRemembersLayers) → {on}

commands.label: Merge Selected
commands.params: {ids?|id?} (default: the highlighted rows) merge two or more rows into the layer listed (highlighted) last: the other layers' contents and the other rows move into it, keeping their stacking order, and the emptied layers go. Every selected object left hidden or locked, such as one merged into a hidden or locked layer, is deselected (the key object too). One undo step → {id}

commands.label: Flatten Artwork
commands.params: {id?} (default: the highlighted row's top-level layer, else the current one's) move the art of every other visible top-level layer into this one, keeping the stacking order; hidden layers and their art are deleted, template layers stay. Every selected object left hidden or locked, such as one flattened into a locked layer, is deselected (the key object too). One undo step → {id, discarded}

commands.label: Release to Layers (Sequence)
commands.params: {id?: layer or group (default: the highlighted row, else the current layer), build?: bool} each object in it goes into a new sublayer of its own, in stacking order (a group's objects go into sublayers of its layer, where the group was). `build`: Release to Layers (Build), each new sublayer holds copies of the objects up to its own, so the layers add up. One undo step → {ids}

commands.label: Release to Layers (Build)
commands.params: {id?} layer.releaseToLayers with build: true → {ids}

commands.label: Reverse Order
commands.params: {ids?|id?} (default: the highlighted rows) reverse the stacking order of two or more rows that share a layer or group; each keeps the places the others held. One undo step

commands.label: Template
commands.params: {ids?|id?, on?: bool (default: toggle the first)} make layers templates (locked, dimmed, left out of print and export) or ordinary layers again (layer.setProps template) → {on}

commands.label: Hide Others
commands.params: {ids?|id?} hide every top-level layer but those holding the highlighted rows (else the current layer), which show. One undo step → {count}

commands.label: Show All Layers
commands.params: {} show every layer and sublayer → {count}

commands.label: Outline Others
commands.params: {ids?|id?} turn Preview off (outline view) for every top-level layer but those holding the highlighted rows (else the current layer), which preview → {count}

commands.label: Preview All Layers
commands.params: {} turn Preview on for every layer and sublayer → {count}

commands.label: Lock Others
commands.params: {ids?|id?} lock every top-level layer but those holding the highlighted rows (else the current layer), which unlock → {count}

commands.label: Unlock All Layers
commands.params: {} unlock every layer and sublayer → {count}

commands.label: Locate Object
commands.params: {id?} (default: the last selected object) highlight the object's row; the Layers panel opens the layers around it and scrolls to it → {id, ancestry: [layer…, id]}

commands.label: Pencil
commands.params: {points: [[x,y]…] or [[x,y,pressure]…] or [[x,y,pressure,tiltX,tiltY,rotation]…] (pen pressure 0..1: the stroke keeps it, for Calligraphic and Scatter brushes with Pressure variation; a point without one presses fully. Pen tilt in degrees, each −90..90, x positive leaning right and y leaning down the page, and barrel rotation in degrees clockwise: the stroke keeps how far the pen leaned, which way and how far its barrel turned, for brushes with Tilt, Bearing and Rotation variation; null for what a point lacks), fidelity?: pt (1.5), fit?: bool (true; false: the points are joined by straight segments, as the Pencil previews a stroke with Live curve fitting off), closed?, style?: "pencil"|"brush", fill?: bool, keepSelected?: bool (true: the drawn or continued path is selected; false: a new path leaves nothing selected, and a continued or redrawn one is deselected while the rest of the selection stays), extend?: {id, end: "start"|"end"}, connect?: {id, end: "start"|"end"}, redraw?: {id, within?: pt (12)}} fit a freehand stroke → {id}. extend continues the path from that end; with connect, the stroke ends on that end of another path's last open subpath and joins it on, in one path with the extended path's appearance (the other path is removed when nothing of it is left); redraw (Edit Selected Paths) replaces the section of the path between where the stroke starts and ends, each within `within` of one subpath (the shorter way round a closed one), and draws a new path when the stroke doesn't end on it

commands.label: Curvature
commands.params: {points: [{x, y, corner?}], closed?, id?} create (or with id: replace) a path curving through the points → {id}

commands.label: Curvature
