commands.params: {id, subpath?, op: "move"|"insert"|"extend"|"close", anchor?, segment?, t?, end?: "start"|"end", from?: "keep"|"smooth"|"corner", corner?, x?, y?} edit a path as the Curvature tool does, its shape kept elsewhere; the anchor edited becomes the direct-selected one → {anchor}. move: anchor to x, y, re-curving only its two segments (a smooth anchor takes the Curvature tool's handles, along the circle through it and its neighbours); insert: a smooth anchor at t on segment, the shape unchanged (with x, y: then moved there); extend: an open subpath goes on from its end (default) or start to a new end at x, y, curving into it unless corner is true; close: an open subpath closes from that end. The old end bends into the new segment as from says: keep its curve (default), smooth through its neighbours, or a corner

commands.label: Delete Anchor Point
commands.params: {id, subpath?, anchor, curvature?} remove one anchor, re-fitting the curve (with curvature: true, the curve where it was follows the remaining anchors, as the Curvature tool curves its points)

commands.label: Remove Anchor Points
commands.params: {} remove the direct-selected anchors without opening their paths, refitting the curve round each; the anchor after each removed one is selected, so running it again goes on along the path → {removedObjects}

commands.label: Convert Anchor Point
commands.params: {id, subpath?, anchor, to: "corner"|"smooth", x?, y?} (smooth with x/y: out handle there, in handle mirrored; without: as the Curvature tool curves a point, along the circle through it and its neighbours, or at an open end one handle into the curve)

commands.label: Reshape Segment
commands.params: {id, subpath?, segment, t, dx, dy, perpendicular?: bool} bend a segment so the point at t moves by (dx, dy); with perpendicular (Shift), both handles stand at right angles to the line between its anchors at one length, and the point at t lies as far from that line as the moved point does

commands.label: Split Path
commands.params: {id, subpath?, segment, t} or {id, subpath?, anchor}: closed paths open there, open paths become two → {ids}

commands.label: Knife
commands.params: {points: [[x,y]…]} cut closed shapes (selected, or all when nothing is selected) along the polyline → {ids}

commands.label: Eraser
commands.params: {points: [[x,y]…] or [[x,y,pressure]…] (pen pressure 0..1), size?: pt (10), sizeMode?: "fixed" (default) | "pressure" (Eraser Tool Options' Size set to Pressure: the tip is size − sizeVariation across where the pen presses lightest and size + sizeVariation where it presses hardest, as path.blob), sizeVariation?: pt (0), angle?: ° (0), roundness?: % (100, kept within 1–100)} erase the stroke of an elliptical tip from paths (selected, or all) → {ids}. The tip is `size` across its long axis, which runs at `angle` counter-clockwise from horizontal; its short axis is `roundness` percent of the long one

commands.label: Path Eraser
commands.params: {points: [[x,y]…], width?: pt (8)} erase the parts of selected paths under the drag → {ids}

commands.label: Smooth
commands.params: {points: [[x,y]…], radius?: pt (12), fidelity?: pt (2.5)} smooth selected paths near the drag → {ids, before, after}

commands.label: Join
commands.params: {points: [[x,y]…], tolerance?: pt (12)} join the open-path endpoints scrubbed over, or trim two crossing open paths whose overhanging ends are scrubbed and join them at the crossing → {id}

commands.label: Blob Brush
commands.params: {points: [[x,y]…] or [[x,y,pressure]…] (pen pressure 0..1), size?: pt (10), sizeMode?: "fixed" (default) | "pressure" (Blob Brush Tool Options' Size set to Pressure: the brush is size − sizeVariation wide at the lightest pen pressure and size + sizeVariation at the heaviest, at least 0.1 pt; a stroke without pressure keeps the size), sizeVariation?: pt (0), angle?: ° (0, kept within −180–180: the tip's long axis counter-clockwise from horizontal, kept on the page along the stroke), roundness?: % (100, kept within 0–100: the tip's short axis in percent of its long one, 100 round; 0 is drawn as 0.1), fidelity?: pt (0.01–100; the brush follows the stroke fitted at this tolerance as path.freehand fits a Pencil stroke, and a higher value gives a smoother shape; without it the brush follows every point), merge?: true, mergeOnlySelection?: bool (false: merge with any touching same-color blob; true: only with selected ones), keepSelected?: bool (false: the drawn or merged path is not selected, and the rest of the selection stays; true: it is selected)} filled brush shape, merged with the topmost touching same-color blob and the touching ones next to it in stacking order in its group or layer → {id}

commands.label: Free Distort
commands.params: {corners: [[x,y]×4] (TL, TR, BR, BL), from?: [x0,y0,x1,y1] (default: selection bounds), ids?} projective warp of anchors and handles

commands.label: Sample Color
commands.params: {color (#rrggbbaa and #rgba are refused), stroke?: bool (default: whichever proxy is active), ids?, stop?: index, clearStroke?: bool} sample a color into the active fill/stroke (and the selection; `ids: []` changes only the paint default); `clearStroke: true` requires `stroke: false`, `ids: []` and no `stop`, and clears the default stroke after sampling an image into the fill; with `stop`, recolor that stop of the gradient behind the proxy instead (paint.editGradient); in a CMYK document an RGB color is stored as CMYK through the color settings, as paint.setFill stores it

commands.label: Eyedropper Options
commands.params: {sampleSize?: 1|3|5 (pixels square averaged when sampling an image: point, 3×3, 5×5), pickUp?, apply?: {appearance?: {transparency?, fill?: {color?, transparency?, overprint?}, stroke?: {color?, transparency?, overprint?, weight?, cap?, join?, miter?, dash?}}, character?, paragraph?} (bools; a bool for a branch sets all of it)} Eyedropper Options, kept in the preferences: what appearance.copyFrom picks up from the clicked object and applies (only attributes in both trees are copied; every fill and stroke attribute copies the whole appearance stack); {} reads them → the options

commands.label: Move Artboard
commands.params: {index | indices: [index…], dx, dy, moveArt?: bool, copy?: bool, patterns?: bool (Transform Patterns: pattern fills and strokes transform with the art; default: prefs transformPatternTiles), lockedAndHidden?: bool (default: prefs moveLockedWithArtboard)} move artboards (and the art fully inside them; locked and hidden art, and art also on another locked artboard, only with lockedAndHidden), several in one step (an error when one is locked); `copy` (Alt-drag) leaves them and moves copies, which start unlocked → {index (the first), indices: the artboards moved or the copies, moved: the art moved or the copies}

commands.label: Apply Effect
commands.params: {effect: id (see effect.list, e.g. "stylize.dropShadow", "distort.roughen", "warp.arc", or "plugin.<id>" for an installed effect plug-in), params?: {…} (missing keys take the dialog defaults), item?: appearance item index|null (apply to that fill/stroke only; omitted: the Appearance panel's active item, else the whole object), ids?|id?: [..] (layers too), target?: "object"|"contents" (contents: the objects inside groups and layers)} append a live effect to each selected object's appearance (a group's or layer's apply to its members as one piece: one combined shadow; a Pathfinder effect, which combines a group's contents, groups several loose selected objects first, in the same undo step) → {ids, index, item, grouped?}

commands.label: Effects
commands.params: {ids?|id?: object ids (default: the selection), target?: "object"|"contents"} → {catalog: [{id, label, menu, params, defaults, raster, lengths: {always, absolute (while relative is false)} (distance params Scale Strokes & Effects scales)}] (installed effect plug-ins last: id plugin.<plug-in id>, menu Effect › Plug-ins), applied: [{id, effects, items: [{index, kind: fill|stroke, effects}]}], activeItem} for the selection

commands.label: Remove Effect
commands.params: {index: int (position in the effect list), indices?: [int] (several positions in the same list instead of index, removed in one undo step; every one must exist), item?: appearance item index|null (that fill/stroke's effects; omitted: the active item, else the object's), ids?|id?: [..], target?: "object"|"contents", aligned?: bool (index and item are rows of the first target's stack: each other target edits its equal one, as the Appearance panel does for a mixed selection)} → {ids}

commands.label: Effect Options
commands.params: {index: int, params?: {…} (merged into the current parameters), warpStyle?: string (an existing Warp style suffix, e.g. arc or flag; changes only an applied Warp in place), threeDType?: plane|extrude|revolve|inflate (the 3D and Materials panel's object type: changes only an applied 3D effect in place into Rotate, Extrude & Bevel, Revolve or Inflate; the settings the new effect also takes keep their values, rotation angles wrapped into -180..180 outside Revolve, and the others start at its defaults; params then merge into the new effect's; the type the effect already has, with nothing else given, changes nothing and records no undo step), visible?: bool, item?: appearance item index|null (as effect.remove), ids?|id?: [..], target?: "object"|"contents", aligned?: bool (index and item are rows of the first target's stack: each other target edits its equal one, as the Appearance panel does for a mixed selection)} → {ids}

commands.label: 3D Lighting Preset
commands.params: {index: int, preset: standard|diffuse|topLeft|right, item?: appearance item index|null (omitted: the active item, else the object's), ids?|id?: [..], target?: object|contents, aligned?: bool (index and item are rows of the first target's stack: each other target edits its equal one, as the Appearance panel does for a mixed selection)} replace an applied 3D effect's light rig and ambient with an original lighting preset; preserve shading, geometry and view; all targets must have a 3D effect at index; one undo step → {ids}

commands.label: Expand Appearance
commands.params: {ids?|id?: [..], target?} turn each object's appearance into objects: every fill and stroke becomes an object of its own (a stroke stays a stroke, with its weight, dashes, arrowheads and width profile, on its own copy of the path, which object.expand or object.path.outlineStroke outline; brushed strokes become their brush art) grouped in paint order under the object's id and transparency, geometry effects are baked, raster effects become an embedded image (shadows and outer glows below the art; blur, feather and inner glow replace it; an object whose only raster effect is its own Rasterize becomes the image object.rasterize makes with the effect's options), type with effects or fills of its own is outlined; Crop Marks become a group of the object and its marks; Vector Halftone (addon.color.halftone) becomes a group of its dot paths, one per ink; a group's or layer's own fills and strokes become objects among its members, which are expanded too. An outlined frame of threaded text leaves its thread with the text it shows, and a frame kept as type in a group stays in its thread. A dimension whose art it changes, or one selected with the art it measures when that art is replaced, becomes a plain group of its art. Hidden fills, strokes and effects are dropped. Enabled when a selected or targeted object's appearance isn't basic (`ids` then pick which objects) → {ids, warning? (an image in the art couldn't be decoded, as object.rasterize says)}

commands.label: Duplicate Effect
commands.params: {index: int, indices?: [int] (several positions in the same list instead of index; every one must exist), item?: appearance item index|null (as effect.remove), ids?|id?: [..], target?: "object"|"contents", aligned?: bool (index and item are rows of the first target's stack: each other target edits its equal one, as the Appearance panel does for a mixed selection)} insert a copy of each effect right after it, in one undo step → {ids}

commands.label: Move Effect
commands.params: {from: int|[int] (position in the source list; a list moves several effects of that list, which keep their order and land together), to: int (the position of the (first) moved effect in the destination list afterwards), fromItem?: appearance item index|null (the source list: that fill/stroke's effects, null the object's; omitted: the active item, else the object's), toItem?: item index|null (the destination list; default: the source list), copy?: bool (copy instead of move, as Alt-dragging the row), ids?|id?: [..], target?: "object"|"contents", aligned?: bool (refused when the targets' appearances differ)} reorder an effect or move it between the object and its fills/strokes, as one undo step → {ids, index, item}

commands.label: Unite
commands.params: {ids?: [id…] (selected first; default: the selection), precision?: pt 0.001..10, removeRedundantPoints?: bool, removeUnpainted?: bool (default: the Pathfinder Options, see object.pathfinder.options; the values used join the journal entry)} operate on the selected objects (back → front) → {ids}

commands.label: Minus Front
commands.params: {ids?: [id…] (selected first; default: the selection), precision?: pt 0.001..10, removeRedundantPoints?: bool, removeUnpainted?: bool (default: the Pathfinder Options, see object.pathfinder.options; the values used join the journal entry)} operate on the selected objects (back → front) → {ids}

commands.label: Intersect
commands.params: {ids?: [id…] (selected first; default: the selection), precision?: pt 0.001..10, removeRedundantPoints?: bool, removeUnpainted?: bool (default: the Pathfinder Options, see object.pathfinder.options; the values used join the journal entry)} operate on the selected objects (back → front) → {ids}

commands.label: Exclude
commands.params: {ids?: [id…] (selected first; default: the selection), precision?: pt 0.001..10, removeRedundantPoints?: bool, removeUnpainted?: bool (default: the Pathfinder Options, see object.pathfinder.options; the values used join the journal entry)} operate on the selected objects (back → front) → {ids}

commands.label: Divide
commands.params: {ids?: [id…] (selected first; default: the selection), precision?: pt 0.001..10, removeRedundantPoints?: bool, removeUnpainted?: bool (default: the Pathfinder Options, see object.pathfinder.options; the values used join the journal entry)} operate on the selected objects (back → front) → {ids}

commands.label: Trim
commands.params: {ids?: [id…] (selected first; default: the selection), precision?: pt 0.001..10, removeRedundantPoints?: bool, removeUnpainted?: bool (default: the Pathfinder Options, see object.pathfinder.options; the values used join the journal entry)} operate on the selected objects (back → front) → {ids}

commands.label: Merge
commands.params: {ids?: [id…] (selected first; default: the selection), precision?: pt 0.001..10, removeRedundantPoints?: bool, removeUnpainted?: bool (default: the Pathfinder Options, see object.pathfinder.options; the values used join the journal entry)} operate on the selected objects (back → front) → {ids}

commands.label: Crop
commands.params: {ids?: [id…] (selected first; default: the selection), precision?: pt 0.001..10, removeRedundantPoints?: bool, removeUnpainted?: bool (default: the Pathfinder Options, see object.pathfinder.options; the values used join the journal entry)} operate on the selected objects (back → front) → {ids}

commands.label: Outline
commands.params: {ids?: [id…] (selected first; default: the selection), precision?: pt 0.001..10, removeRedundantPoints?: bool, removeUnpainted?: bool (default: the Pathfinder Options, see object.pathfinder.options; the values used join the journal entry)} operate on the selected objects (back → front) → {ids}

commands.label: Minus Back
commands.params: {ids?: [id…] (selected first; default: the selection), precision?: pt 0.001..10, removeRedundantPoints?: bool, removeUnpainted?: bool (default: the Pathfinder Options, see object.pathfinder.options; the values used join the journal entry)} operate on the selected objects (back → front) → {ids}

commands.label: Trap…
commands.params: {ids?: [id…] (selected first; default: the selection), thickness?: pt 0.01..5000 (0.25; how far the lighter colour reaches into the darker one across vertical edges), heightWidth?: % 1..1000 (100; the reach across horizontal edges as a percentage of the vertical one), tintReduction?: % 0..100 (40; the trap paints the lighter colour at this percentage of its tint), trapsWithProcessColor?: bool (false; a swatch (spot) colour's trap is painted with its CMYK process equivalent), reverseTraps?: bool (false; the darker colour spreads into the lighter one, except a rich black)} adds overprinting traps where the selected objects' visible areas of different solid colours meet, grouped directly above the topmost selected object and selected; the objects stay as they are → {ids}

commands.label: Pathfinder Options…
commands.params: {precision?: pt 0.001..10 (0.01; how closely the Pathfinder operations follow the paths: results are refit to within it and pieces thinner than it are dropped), removeRedundantPoints?: bool (false; the results lose the anchors that don't change their shape), removeUnpainted?: bool (false; Divide and Outline leave out the pieces of objects with no fill)} Pathfinder Options, kept in the preferences and used by every later Shape Mode and Pathfinder operation (not Trap); {} reads them → the options

commands.label: Outline Stroke
commands.params: {} replace stroked paths with filled outlines; a dimension whose lines are outlined, or selected with the art it measures when that art is outlined, becomes a plain group of its art → {ids}

commands.label: Offset Path…
commands.params: {offset: pt (negative insets), joins?: "miter"|"round"|"bevel", miterLimit?: 4} → {ids} (new objects above the originals)

commands.label: Simplify…
commands.params: {tolerance?: pt (1), level?: 0..100 (the Simplify slider, in place of tolerance: 0 fewest anchor points, 50 is 1 pt, every 10 levels halves or doubles it), auto?: bool (Auto-Simplify: the lowest level whose tolerance is at most 1/400 of the selection's longer side, or 100 when that side is under 12.5 pt), cornerAngle?: deg (30), straightLines?: bool, wholePaths?: bool (false: a path with segments direct-selected, or between direct-selected anchors, simplifies only each run of them between its end anchors, which stay as they are, and keeps the runs selected; true simplifies those paths whole)} → {ids, before, after} anchor counts, and the level used with level or auto

commands.label: Smooth…
commands.params: {level?: 0..100 (50; the Smooth slider: 0 minimum smoothing, the path staying within 0.1% of its longer side, 100 maximum: smoothed along its length by up to 5% of it and refitted with curves within up to 2.5% of it, corners kept only where the path turns back, never with more anchor points), auto?: bool (Auto-Smooth: level 50), ids?: [id…] (default: the selection)} smooth each path under the objects, compound path members included, as one undo step; without ids, a path with anchor points or segments direct-selected smooths only the sections between them, which stay selected → {ids, before, after} anchor counts, and the level used

commands.label: Divide Objects Below
commands.params: {} cut the objects below with the selected path (which is removed) → {ids}

commands.label: Split Into Grid…
commands.params: {rows?: 2, columns?: 2, gutter?: pt (12; rowGutter?, columnGutter?: one of the two), totalHeight?, totalWidth?: pt (the grid's size; the selected paths' when left out), height?, width?: pt (each row's and column's size, which then sets the total), addGuides?: false (ruler guides along the row and column edges)} one grid of rectangles over the selected paths replaces them, painted as the topmost one → {ids, guides: count}

commands.label: Clean Up…
commands.params: {strayPoints?: true, unpaintedObjects?: true, emptyTextPaths?: true} → {removed}

commands.label: Make Compound Shape
commands.params: {ids?: [id…] (selected first; default: the selection), mode?: "add"|"subtract"|"intersect"|"exclude" (default add; Alt-clicking a Shape Mode button gives its mode)} the two or more selected objects (paths, compound paths, groups, compound shapes, type, blends, envelopes) become the members of one compound shape, each with the shape mode, in their stacking order where the frontmost was: it draws as the area they make from the backmost up (open paths closed; a blend as its steps, an envelope as its distorted art, an object with a warp or other geometry effect as it draws), painted with the appearance and transparency of the topmost member in Add, Intersect or Exclude mode (with every member in Subtract, the backmost), and the members stay editable (Direct Selection, Layers panel, isolation mode) → {id}

commands.label: Shape Mode
commands.params: {mode: "add"|"subtract"|"intersect"|"exclude", ids?: [id…] (selected first; default: the selection)} the members of compound shapes that the selected objects are or are in take the shape mode (what clicking a Shape Mode button does with members selected); the backmost member's mode doesn't change the shape → {ids}

commands.label: Release Compound Shape
commands.params: {ids?: [id…] (selected first; default: the selection)} the selected compound shapes (and those holding the selected objects) become their members again, as they were before Make Compound Shape, selected → {ids}

commands.label: Expand Compound Shape
commands.params: {ids?: [id…] (selected first; default: the selection)} the selected compound shapes (and those holding the selected objects) become the path, or compound path, of the area they draw, painted as they are, selected → {ids}

commands.label: Vertical
commands.params: {ids?|id?} set vertical writing

commands.label: Horizontal
commands.params: {ids?|id?} set horizontal writing

commands.label: Create Outlines
commands.params: {} convert the selected text to groups of compound paths (one per glyph); a frame of threaded text leaves its thread with the text it shows; a dimension whose label is outlined becomes a plain group of its art → {ids}

commands.label: Scale Text Attributes
commands.params: {ids?|id?} bake each selected type object's transform scale into its character sizes (leading, baseline shift and horizontal scale included), leaving rotation and position in the affine → {ids, changed}

commands.label: Optical Margin Alignment
commands.params: {ids?|id?, on?: bool} turn Optical Margin Alignment on or off for the selected type and every frame of its threads (on omitted: the opposite of the first object's setting): in every paragraph of point and area type, quotation marks, hyphens, full stops and commas at a line's start or end hang wholly outside the margin there; asterisks, tildes, ellipses, en and em dashes, colons and semicolons hang by half; and A, V, W, Y, v, w and y hang by a tenth of their advance; a left-aligned line hangs at its left margin, a right-aligned line hangs at its right margin, and centered and justified lines hang at both; Auto aligns a right-to-left line at its right; type on a path hangs at the start bracket when its line is placed there, hangs at the end bracket when the line is placed there, and hangs at both when it is centered → {on, ids}

commands.label: System Layout
commands.params: {on?: bool} turn System Layout on or off for the document (on omitted: the opposite of the document's setting) and every text object in it. On, each character that takes any space advances by a whole number of points, at least one, so small type does not run together; a character with no width stays at none. Off (the default, and what a document from before it reads as), spacing uses fractions of a point. New point, area and path type inherits the document's setting → {on}

commands.label: Fractional Widths
commands.params: {ids?|id?, on?: bool} turn Fractional Widths on or off for the selected type and every frame of its threads (on omitted: the opposite of the first object's setting). On (the default, and what a document from before it reads as), spacing between characters uses fractions of a point. Off, each character that takes any space advances by a whole number of points, at least one, so small type does not run together; a character with no width stays at none. The setting is the whole type object, not a range of characters → {on, ids}

commands.label: Set Text
commands.params: {id?|ids?, text} replace the contents of text objects (keeps the first run's style) → {ids, overflow?: [id…] (area type and type on a path whose text no longer fits; left out when all fits)}

commands.label: Area Type Options…
commands.params: {ids?|id?, width?: pt, height?: pt, rows?, columns?, gutter?: pt (between rows and columns), rowGutter?: pt|null (between rows when it differs from gutter, which is then between columns; gutter given alone sets both; the reply gives the rows' gutter either way), inset?: pt, firstBaseline?: ascent|capHeight|xHeight|leading|fixed, firstBaselineMin?: pt, verticalAlign?: top|center|bottom|justify, flow?: columns|rows (Text Flow: down each column's rows, then across, the default; or across each row's columns, then down), fit?: none|autoHeight|shrinkText, fitMinPercent?: 10..100, …the keys of its own reply (it can be passed back; the values it only reports are ignored)} set the selected area type's options (each frame takes the options given over its own and keeps the rest; fit resolves against each frame's own; options that change nothing add no undo step); width and height size the type area from its top-left corner, along the type's own axes, and the text reflows at its size (with fit autoHeight, Auto Size, the frame's height follows the text after every edit and height is ignored; setting the height by hand turns it off); fit shrinkText scales overflowing text down (size, leading, baseline shift) by the largest factor down to fitMinPercent % (default 50) that makes it fit (none given: query) → the first object's options, plus overflow (the text doesn't fit its frame) and fitScale (Shrink Text's factor, 1 unshrunk)

commands.label: Reshape Type Area
commands.params: {id, anchors: [[subpath, anchor]…], dx, dy} or {items: [{id, anchors}…], dx, dy} move anchors of area type's frame (the type area) by dx, dy points, with their handles; the text reflows at its size, through its thread too (what Direct Selection does dragging a frame corner or edge, or the frame anchors its marquee selected, and the arrow keys nudging those); with items, every listed frame moves in one step

commands.label: Reshape Type Path
commands.params: {id, anchors: [[subpath, anchor]…], dx, dy} move anchors of type on a path's path by dx, dy points, with their handles; the start and end brackets keep their fractions of the path and the text reflows along it (what Direct Selection does dragging an anchor of the path)

commands.label: Fit Headline
commands.params: {ids?|id?} track the first line of area type so it fills the frame width → {tracking}

commands.label: Character
commands.params: {ids?|id?, font?, style? (font alone: the style is kept when the new family has it, else its closest), size?: pt, leading?: pt|"auto", tracking?: 1/1000 em, justify?: "auto" (the start of each paragraph's direction)|"left"|"center"|"right"|"justifyAll", fill?: colour|"none", stroke?: colour|"none" (characters without a stroke weight get 1 pt; #rrggbbaa and #rgba are refused in both), keepModel?: bool (fill and stroke, as paint.setFill), strokeWidth?: pt (the character stroke's weight, in document points as stroke.set), features?: ["dlig", "-liga", …] OpenType, featureChanges?: ["tnum", "-onum", …] (OpenType features turned on, or with - off, on top of each character's own; its other features are kept), start?: byte, end?: byte} (size/leading are document points after object scaling; with a range: the character attributes style that range and justify the paragraphs it touches; without: all the text) → {ids, overflow?: [id…] (area type and type on a path whose text no longer fits; left out when all fits), warning?: text (the font or style set isn't available: its type is drawn in the fallback font or the family's closest style)}

commands.label: Ruby…
commands.params: {ids?|id?, start?: byte, end?: byte, text?: reading, position?: above|below (vertical type: right|left), align?: start|center|end, size?: 1–100 (percent of the base text's size, default 50), overhang?: bool (default true), remove?: bool} set the ruby (furigana) over the selected text's bytes in `start..end` (without them: all its text): the reading over the base characters, above them in horizontal type and right of them in vertical type; `remove` takes the ruby off the range instead → {ids, ruby: [{start, end, text, position, align, sizePercent, overhang}…] (the first object's ruby)}

commands.label: All Artwork Above
commands.params: {} lock objects in the same layer that are above and overlap the selection, deselecting every selected object left locked or hidden (the key object too); in isolation mode, lock the selected objects and the objects above them inside the isolated object → {count}

commands.label: Other Layers
commands.params: {} lock every layer that holds no selected object; in isolation mode, change nothing and return a count of 0 → {count}

commands.label: Unselected Artwork
commands.params: {} lock unselected artwork in one undo step, including unselected members of partly selected groups, clipping groups and compound paths, and guides while Lock Guides is on; hidden art and art on locked layers stay unlocked; a selected layer's art counts as selected; in isolation, only art inside the isolated object is affected; object.unlockAll unlocks locked art document-wide, or inside the isolated object in isolation mode → {count}

commands.label: All Artwork Above
commands.params: {} hide objects in the same layer that are above and overlap the selection, deselecting every selected object left hidden or locked (the key object too); in isolation mode, hide the selected objects and the objects above them inside the isolated object → {count}

commands.label: Other Layers
commands.params: {} hide every layer that holds no selected object; in isolation mode, change nothing and return a count of 0 → {count}

commands.label: Unselected Artwork
commands.params: {} hide, in one undo step, every object select.all takes that is not selected and holds no selected object; in a group that holds one it hides the other members one by one, and a clip group, compound path or other object that holds one stays as it is; the objects of a selected layer count as selected; while Lock Guides is on, guide paths count as selected and stay as they are; in isolation mode, only art inside the isolated object is affected; object.showAll shows them again → {count}

commands.label: Transform Each…
commands.params: {scaleH?: % (100), scaleV?: % (100), relative?: bool (true: scaleH and scaleV are percentages of each object's size, as the dialog's Relative; false: Absolute, scaleH and scaleV are the width and height in pt each object becomes, measured on its own bounds, and a side left out keeps its size), moveH?: pt, moveV?: pt (down = +), rotate?: deg (counter-clockwise), reflectX?: bool (flip left-right, as Reflect X in the Transform Each dialog), reflectY?: bool (flip top-bottom, as Reflect Y), random?: bool, seed?: n, reference?: 0..8 (9-point grid, 4 = centre), copy?: bool, strokes?: bool (Scale Strokes & Effects), corners?: bool (Scale Corners; both default to the preferences), objects?: bool (Transform Objects, default true; false: the art stays and, with patterns, only its pattern tiles transform), patterns?: bool (Transform Patterns; default: prefs transformPatternTiles)} transform every selected object about the reference point of its own box, along its own axes → {ids}

commands.label: Reset Bounding Box
commands.params: {} square the bounding box of the selected objects, and of every object inside them (the children of groups, compound paths, clip groups, blends, envelopes, repeats and intertwines, and the art of linked opacity masks), to the page again after a rotation (their geometry stays; one undo step, none when no box is rotated) → {changed: objects reset, the objects inside included}

commands.label: Rasterize…
commands.params: {ppi?, background?: transparent|white|black|"#rrggbb" (#rrggbbaa and #rgba are refused), antiAlias?: none|art|type (text snapped to pixels)|bool, padding?|addAround?: pt (0–1000), colorModel?: "rgb"|"cmyk"|"grayscale"|"bitmap", clippingMask?: bool (a clip group with the art's outline)} replace the selection with an embedded image (PNG; in a CMYK document with its own colour model, a CMYK image of the art's inks, its transparency as its opacity mask); each defaults to document.rasterEffectsSettings; a frame of threaded text that is rasterized leaves its thread with the text it shows → {id (the image, or its clip group), width, height, warning?: "an image couldn't be decoded and is missing from the picture" (as raster exports say)}

commands.label: Create Object Mosaic…
commands.params: {columns=10, rows=10 (whole numbers, kept within 1..1000), width?, height? (new size in pt; default the image's), spacingX=0, spacingY=0 (pt between tiles), gray?: bool, deleteRaster?: bool} a group of rectangles coloured by the selected image's average tile colours → {id, tiles}

commands.label: Crop Image
commands.params: {rect?: [x, y, width, height] | trim?: true (to the pixels that aren't fully transparent, pixel for pixel; an image with none to cut is left as it is, trimmed: false)} crop the selected image (default: to the artboard it sits on) → {id, width, height, trimmed? (with trim), warning? (without trim: the image couldn't be decoded, as object.rasterize says)}

commands.label: Mask
commands.params: {} clip the selected image with a rectangle around it (its own outline, rotated with it) and select that clipping path, whose handles then crop it; one undo step → {id: the clip group, path: the clipping path}

commands.label: Create Trim Marks
commands.params: {style?: "roman"|"japanese" (default: the japaneseCropMarks preference; japanese: double lines at the trim and bleed edges plus centre marks), allArtboards?: bool (default: true when nothing is selected), offset?: pt (9, roman), length?: pt (18), bleed?: pt (8.5, japanese), weight?: pt (0.3)} trim marks stroked in [Registration] (printing on every plate) around the selection, or around every artboard, one group each, as one undo step → {id: the first group, ids}

commands.label: Convert to Shape
commands.params: {} turn paths that are rectangles (any rotation) or axis-aligned ellipses into live shapes → {converted}

commands.label: Convert to Artboards
commands.params: {} turn each selected object's bounds into a new artboard (the objects are removed) → {artboards}

commands.label: Rearrange All Artboards…
commands.params: {layout?: gridByRow|gridByColumn|row|column (gridByRow; byColumn?: true is gridByColumn), order?: leftToRight|rightToLeft (leftToRight: right-to-left mirrors the order along the rows), columns?: n (2; the rows for gridByColumn; row and column ignore it), spacing?: pt (20), moveArtwork?: true (each object of a layer or sublayer moves with the artboard its center is on; locked and hidden art, and art on a locked artboard, only with lockedAndHidden), patterns?: bool (Transform Patterns: pattern fills and strokes transform with the art; default: prefs transformPatternTiles), lockedAndHidden?: bool (default: prefs moveLockedWithArtboard), byColumn?: bool (an older way to ask for layout gridByColumn)} lay the artboards out in their order, the grid's top-left at the first artboard's; a locked artboard stays where it is → {artboards, rows, columns}

commands.label: Make
commands.params: {ids?, steps?: n | distance?: pt | smooth?: bool, orientation?: page|path (default: the Blend Options set with nothing selected, else smooth colour and page), starts?: [anchor index | null, …] (per object of `ids`, else of the selection in paint order: the anchor of its first subpath the blend starts from; an open path's last anchor runs it the other way), spacing?: smooth|steps|distance (with value), value?: n, easingType?: easeIn|easeOut|easeInOut|easeOutIn, ramp?: pct (0..100), colorShift?: pct (-100..100; 0: even)} blend the selected objects (paint order) into a live blend; a blend among them takes the others in as more key objects (keeping its options, name and transparency) instead of nesting → {id}

commands.label: Release
commands.params: {} release the selected blends: the key objects come back and the spine stays as a path with no fill or stroke, below them; a blend with a name, opacity, blend mode, isolation, opacity mask or appearance of its own comes back as a group keeping them (and its knockout) → {ids (the keys), spines: [ids], groups: [ids]}

commands.label: Blend Options…
commands.params: {spacing?: smooth|steps|distance, value?: n, steps?: n, distance?: pt, orientation?: page|path, smooth?: bool, easingType?: easeIn|easeOut|easeInOut|easeOutIn, ramp?: pct, colorShift?: pct} set the options of the selected blends; easingType chooses the distribution, ramp sets its strength (0..100; 0 = even), colorShift (-100..100; 0 = even) shifts colours independently of shape/position easing (omitted ones keep their value; out of range is an error); with no blend selected, the options new blends start with (spacing and orientation only; a tool setting, not an undo step) → {defaults?: true}

commands.label: Expand
commands.params: {} replace the selected blends by groups of their keys and steps, each keeping the blend's id, name, transparency (knockout and isolation included), opacity mask and appearance → {ids}

commands.label: Replace Spine
commands.params: {} use the selected path as the spine of the selected blend (the path is consumed)

commands.label: Reverse Spine
commands.params: {} reverse the order of the key objects along the spine

commands.label: Blend Info
commands.params: {} the options of the first selected blend, else those new blends start with → {target: blend|defaults, id?, spacing: smooth|steps|distance, steps, distance, orientation: page|path, easingType?: easeIn|easeOut|easeInOut|easeOutIn, ramp?: pct, colorShift?: pct, keys?: [ids], starts?: [anchor|null], spine?: {anchors: [{x, y, in: [x, y], out: [x, y]}], closed, keyAnchors: [anchor each key sits on] | null (keys spread evenly: a spine from Replace Spine), explicit: false for the straight lines between the key centres}}

commands.label: Move Spine Point
commands.params: {id? (default: the selected blend), anchor: index, x, y, with?: [index…], handle?: in|out, independent?: bool} move a point of the blend's spine (its handles along), and the points `with` names by as much, or with `handle` place that handle's end at (x, y) (a smooth point keeps the other handle in line unless `independent`). A key object sitting on a moved point moves with it. The first edit turns the straight spine into a path

commands.label: Convert Anchor Point
commands.params: {id? (default: the selected blend), anchor: index, to: smooth|corner, x?, y?} convert a blend spine point: dragging a corner creates symmetric smooth handles, clicking a point with handles retracts both. Without x/y, smooth uses the neighbouring spine points

commands.label: Reshape Spine Segment
commands.params: {id? (default: the selected blend), segment: index, t: 0..1, dx, dy, perpendicular?: bool} bend a segment of the blend's spine so its point at t moves by (dx, dy), as path.reshapeSegment bends a path's (perpendicular too): a straight spine turns into a curve (#1111)

commands.label: Add Spine Point
commands.params: {id? (default: the selected blend), x, y} add a point to the blend's spine where it passes nearest (x, y) → {anchor}

commands.label: Delete Spine Point
commands.params: {id? (default: the selected blend), anchor: index} delete a point of the blend's spine that no key object sits on

commands.label: Reverse Front to Back
commands.params: {} reverse the stacking order of the selected blends

commands.label: Make with Warp…
commands.params: {ids?, style?: arc|arcLower|arcUpper|arch|bulge|shellLower|shellUpper|flag|wave|fish|rise|fisheye|inflate|squeeze|twist (arc), bend?: % -100..100 (50), h?: horizontal distortion % -100..100 (0), v?: vertical distortion % (0), horizontal?: bool (true) | orientation?: horizontal|vertical, horizontalDistortion?: as h, verticalDistortion?: as v} envelope the selected objects with a warp (Envelope Options from object.envelope.options with nothing selected; type maps from its glyph outline bounds) → {id}

commands.label: Make with Mesh…
commands.params: {ids?, rows?: 1..50 (4), cols?: 1..50 (4), columns?: as cols} envelope the selected objects with a mesh of rows × cols patches over their bounds (type measured by its glyph outlines) → {id}

commands.label: Make with Top Object
commands.params: {ids?} the topmost selected path becomes the envelope of the others (type maps from its glyph outline bounds) → {id}

commands.label: Reset with Warp…
commands.params: {style?, bend?, h?, v?, horizontal? | orientation? (as makeWithWarp; unset: the envelope's current warp, else arc 50 %), horizontalDistortion?: as h, verticalDistortion?: as v} make the selected envelopes warp envelopes, keeping their content

commands.label: Reset with Mesh…
commands.params: {rows?: 1..50, cols?: 1..50 (unset: a mesh envelope's own, else 4), maintainShape?: bool (true: the mesh follows the current envelope shape; false: a flat grid over the content, type measured by its glyph outlines), columns?: as cols} make the selected envelopes mesh envelopes, keeping their content

commands.label: Envelope Info
commands.params: {} the selected envelope's settings, or with none selected the defaults new envelopes get → {id: n|null, type: warp|mesh|topObject, style, bend, h, v, horizontal, rows, cols, fidelity, antiAlias, preserveShape: clippingMask|transparency, distortAppearance, distortLinearGradients, distortPatternFills, boundsMargin?: [top, bottom, left, right] (shares of the content's height and width, reported only when not zero: with distortAppearance, how far the box the content maps from reaches past its geometric bounds), editing}

commands.label: Release
commands.params: {} release the selected envelopes into their content and their shape (a grey gradient mesh for warp and mesh envelopes, the path for a top-object envelope; the content keeps the envelope's opacity, blend mode and opacity mask) → {ids}

commands.label: Envelope Options…
commands.params: {fidelity?: 0..100, antiAlias?: bool, preserveShape?: clippingMask|transparency, distortAppearance?: bool, distortLinearGradients?: bool, distortPatternFills?: bool (the last two work with distortAppearance; on an envelope with boundsMargin, distortAppearance also switches the content between the box with the margins and its geometric box), style?, bend?, h?, v?, horizontal? (warp envelopes), horizontalDistortion?: as h, verticalDistortion?: as v, orientation?: horizontal|vertical} set the selected envelopes' options; with no envelope selected, the options new envelopes get (see object.envelope.info)

commands.label: Expand
commands.params: {} replace the selected envelopes by groups of their distorted content (type outlined), keeping name, opacity, blend mode, isolation, knockout and opacity mask → {ids}

commands.label: Edit Contents
commands.params: {editing?: bool} toggle Edit Contents / Edit Envelope; leaving Edit Contents measures an envelope's boundsMargin again when the content's strokes reach differently than when Edit Contents began → {editing}

commands.label: Move Envelope Mesh Point
commands.params: {id, index, x, y, handle?: 0 right|1 left|2 down|3 up} move a point of a mesh envelope (its handles follow), or with `handle` place that handle end at (x, y); object.mesh.movePoint, addLine and deletePoint edit mesh envelopes too

commands.label: Create Gradient Mesh…
commands.params: {ids?, rows?: n (4), cols?: n (4), appearance?: flat|center|edge, highlight?: % (100), at?: [x,y], tolerance?: pt (0), columns?: as cols} convert filled paths into gradient meshes in their fill colour (a gradient fill: the colour it paints at each point), lightened per `appearance` (with `at`: 1×1 mesh plus lines through that point, or through the nearest point of the edge when `at` is outside within `tolerance`); an embedded image becomes a mesh over its rectangle (its transform kept) whose points take the average colour and opacity of the picture around them (a linked image is refused: embed it first) → {ids, index?}

commands.label: Set Mesh Point Color
commands.params: {id, index | points: [index…] | items: [{id, index | points}…], color? (#rrggbbaa and #rgba are refused), keepModel?: bool (as paint.setFill), opacity?: 0..1} colour and/or opacity of gradient mesh points (one undo step; an index out of range changes nothing)

commands.label: Move Mesh Point
commands.params: {id, index, x, y, handle?: 0 right|1 left|2 down|3 up} move a point of a gradient mesh or mesh envelope (its handles follow), or with `handle` place that handle end at (x, y)

commands.label: Move Mesh Points
commands.params: {id, points: [index…] | items: [{id, index | points}…], dx, dy} move points of gradient meshes or mesh envelopes by (dx, dy), their handles with them (one undo step; an index out of range changes nothing)

commands.label: Add Mesh Line
commands.params: {id, x, y, color? (#rrggbbaa and #rgba are refused), keepModel?: bool (as paint.setFill), tolerance?: pt (0)} add a row and a column through (x, y) to a gradient mesh (new point in `color`) or a mesh envelope; a point outside within `tolerance` of the edge adds them through the nearest point of the edge → {index}

commands.label: Delete Mesh Point
commands.params: {id, index} delete the mesh lines through a point of a gradient mesh or mesh envelope

commands.label: Expand Gradient Mesh
commands.params: {} replace the selected meshes by groups of flat-coloured pieces → {ids}

commands.label: Invert Colors
commands.params: {fill?: true, stroke?: true, includeImages?: true, includePatterns?: true, ids?} replace each colour by its RGB inverse (keeps the colour model) in fills, strokes, text, gradient meshes (with fills), colorized image fills (their pixels stay unchanged), other embedded images (a recoloured copy) and pattern tiles (a new pattern swatch; the original stays), as one undo step → {changed}

commands.label: Convert to CMYK
commands.params: {fill?, stroke?, includeImages?, includePatterns?, ids?} (as edit.colors.invert) → {changed}

commands.label: Convert to Grayscale
commands.params: {fill?, stroke?, includeImages?, includePatterns?, ids?} (as edit.colors.invert) → {changed}

commands.label: Convert to RGB
commands.params: {fill?, stroke?, includeImages?, includePatterns?, ids?} (as edit.colors.invert) → {changed}

commands.label: Saturate…
commands.params: {intensity: -100..100 (%; a number outside the range counts as its nearest end), fill?, stroke?, includeImages?, includePatterns?, ids?} scale saturation by (1 + intensity/100), reaching what edit.colors.invert does → {changed}

commands.label: Adjust Color Balance…
commands.params: {mode?: "rgb"|"cmyk"|"gray"|"global" (default: from the channels given), r?, g?, b? | c?, m?, y?, k? | gray? | tint?: -100..100 (% added per channel, default 0; `tint` is global mode: it shifts the tints of colours and gradient stops linked to global and spot swatches, which stay linked, and leaves other colours and images alone), convert?: false (true: the results stay in the adjusted model; false: each colour keeps its own), fill?, stroke?, includeImages?, includePatterns?, ids?} reaching what edit.colors.invert does → {changed}

commands.label: Blend Front to Back
commands.params: {} ≥3 filled objects (solid fills or gradient meshes, which keep their shading): intermediate fills graded between the frontmost and backmost fill → {changed}

commands.label: Blend Horizontally
commands.params: {} ≥3 filled objects or meshes: fills graded between the leftmost and rightmost → {changed}

commands.label: Blend Vertically
commands.params: {} ≥3 filled objects or meshes: fills graded between the topmost and bottommost → {changed}

commands.label: Color Guide
commands.params: {color (#rrggbbaa and #rgba are refused), rule: complementary|complementary2|splitComplementary|leftComplement|rightComplement|analogous|analogous2|monochromatic|shades|triad|triad2|triad3|tetrad|tetrad2|tetrad3|compound|compound2|highContrast|highContrast2|highContrast3|pentagram (or its label), steps?: 1..20 (4), variation?: "tintsShades"|"warmCool"|"vividMuted", amount?: 0..100 (50; how far the outermost steps go), limitTo?: swatch library id or name; or "document" (the document's swatches): every colour snaps to its nearest colour there (ΔE 2000)} the Color Guide for a base colour → {rule, colors: ["#rrggbb", the base first], grid: [per colour, 2·steps+1 variations from shades/cool/muted to tints/warm/vivid with the colour itself in the centre]}

commands.label: Color Settings…
commands.params: {rgb?: profile, cmyk?: profile, intent?: "perceptual"|"relative"|"saturation"|"absolute", bpc?: bool} set the working spaces → {rgb, cmyk, intent, bpc, profiles: [{name, kind, builtin}]}

commands.label: Load Color Profile…
commands.params: {path: .icc/.icm file of at most 32 MB} register an ICC profile (native only). The desktop app and vectorcraft-cli keep a copy of the file in the `Color Profiles` folder next to the preferences and register it again at every start (not with VECTORCRAFT_NO_PREFS, or in a confined `mcp --automation-*-root` server: there it lasts until the process ends) → {name, kind, remembered: whether a copy was kept}

commands.label: Remove Color Profile…
commands.params: {name} forget a profile color.loadProfile loaded, and the copy kept of it (built-in profiles and the working spaces stay) → {removed: name}

commands.label: Assign Profile…
commands.params: {rgb?: profile|null, cmyk?: profile|null} tag the document with profiles (colour numbers are kept) → {rgb, cmyk}

commands.label: Convert Document Color Mode
commands.params: {…as file.documentColorMode} same as file.documentColorMode: {mode: "cmyk"|"rgb", convert?: true, intent?, grays?} → {changed} (an alias kept for older scripts; the command palette leaves it out)

commands.label: Edit Text

commands.label: Bullets and Numbering

" or "1) " (a numbered list in 1, 2, 3), "A. " or "A) " (a numbered list in A, B, C), or "* ", "# ", "> " or "+ " (a bulleted list with the filled dot), and the paragraph is in no list, those characters are removed and the paragraph joins that list as one undo step (left and first-line indents of 0 become 18 and -18, as text.setFormat sets them); otherwise nothing changes → {id, started: bool, caret: byte (the paragraph's start when started, else `at`)}

commands.label: Character

(default: the one selected type object), start?: byte, end?: byte (default: all text), story?: bool = false (all the text of every frame of the threaded story `id` is a frame of, in one undo step; no `start` or `end`), font?, style?, size?: pt, leading?: pt|"auto", tracking?, kerning?: 1/1000 em|"auto"|"optical", baselineShift?: pt, hScale?: %, vScale?: %, rotation?: deg, fill?: colour|"none", stroke?: colour|"none" (#rrggbbaa and #rgba are refused in both), keepModel?: bool (fill and stroke, as paint.setFill), strokeWidth?: pt, strokeOptions?: {weight?, cap?, join?, miterLimit?, align?, dash?, dashOffset?, alignDashes?} (as stroke.set: the character stroke), underline?, strikethrough?, allCaps?: bool, smallCaps?: bool, position?: "normal"|"superscript"|"subscript" (sizes from Document Setup), features?: ["dlig", "-liga", …], featureChanges?: ["tnum", "-onum", …] (OpenType features turned on, or with - off, on top of each character's own; its other features are kept), charAlign?: "romanBaseline"|"emBoxTop"|"emBoxCenter"|"emBoxBottom"|"icfTop"|"icfBottom", proportionalMetrics?: bool (full-width glyphs on the font's proportional widths: `palt` in horizontal type, `vpal` in vertical type), tateChuYoko?: bool (Character panel menu › Tate-chu-yoko, with Show East Asian Options: in vertical type those characters stand side by side across one em of the column; kept on the characters and ignored in horizontal type), tcyUpDown?, tcyLeftRight?: pt -1296..1296 (Character panel menu › Tate-chu-yoko Settings: in vertical type a block of tate-chu-yoko characters moves up by a positive Up/Down and down by a negative one, right by a positive Left/Right and left by a negative one, as one piece with the values of its first character; 0 by default; automatic digit blocks and horizontal type do not move; neither turns tateChuYoko on), standardVerticalRoman?: bool (Character panel menu › Standard Vertical Roman Alignment, with Show East Asian Options: in vertical type those half-width characters, such as Latin letters and digits, stand upright one below the other instead of being rotated; on by default), charDirection?: "default"|"leftToRight"|"rightToLeft" (Character panel menu › Character Direction: the characters are set left to right or right to left inside their paragraph, as a Unicode bidi embedding; default: as the bidi algorithm sets them), digits?: "default"|"arabic"|"hindi"|"farsi"|"devanagari"|"bengali"|"gurmukhi"|"gujarati"|"odia"|"tamil"|"telugu"|"kannada"|"malayalam" (Character panel menu › Digits: the numeral system every digit is drawn in, whatever was typed: Western, Arabic-Indic (hindi), Eastern Arabic-Indic (farsi) or an Indic script's own digits), fontHeightReference?: "emBox"|"capHeight"|"xHeight"|"icfBox" (Character panel › Set Font Height Reference: the height of the font that size measures, the em box by default; with a font that has no such height, or one outside 0.1 to 2 em, the em box), language?: name|tag (Character panel › Language: one of Document Setup's languages by name or BCP 47 tag, case-insensitive, such as "Turkish" or "tr"; the characters are shaped in it, so the font uses that language's forms (OpenType `locl`); saved as the tag, English: USA, the default, as none; new type takes the document's language), fontAxes?: {"wght": 650, …} (Character panel › Variable Font: the setting of each variation axis named, in the axis's units and clamped to its range; null: back to the style's own setting; other axes keep theirs; tags the font has no axis for are left out; a font or style change clears them; text.fontList {family, style} lists the axes)} style a character range (size/leading/baselineShift are document points and hScale includes the object transform; runs are split at the range ends) → {id, runs, warning?: text (the font or style set isn't available: its type is drawn in the fallback font or the family's closest style)}

commands.label: Touch Type
commands.params: {id, start: byte (a character of it), dx?: pt, dy?: pt, hScale?: %, vScale?: %, rotation?: deg} change one character (a ligature, one glyph for several characters, as a whole) as a Touch Type tool drag does, as one undo step: dx moves it along its line in reading order by changing the kerning of the character before it on the line and its own kerning, and the characters after it stay where they are (an error for the first logical character of a line or at a reading-direction boundary; supported in either reading direction; limited to what kerning from -1000 to 10000 can give); dy raises it (baseline shift, up from its line whatever its rotation, also for the first character of a line and a right-to-left character); dx and dy are document points; hScale (including the object transform), vScale and rotation set its scales and rotation as text.setRangeStyle does. The kerning of the two characters also keeps the character and the ones after it where they were along the line when the font kerned them with their neighbors; a wider or narrower character moves the ones after it by the change in its width → {id, start, end} (the character's bytes)

commands.label: Glyphs
commands.params: {id, start: byte (a character of it), gid: glyph id|null} draw that one character with another glyph of its font as one undo step, what a double-click in the Glyphs panel's Show › Alternates for Current Selection does: gid is one of the glyphs text.glyphAlternates lists for it; its own default glyph, or null, puts the default glyph back. The text keeps the character, and its other attributes do not change. The choice is saved with the character's style and names the face it was made in (PostScript name and version): set in another font or version, or after the font goes missing, the character takes its default glyph; typed characters take their default glyphs. Choosing the glyph the character already draws is not an edit. An error when the character's font is not available, the glyph is not one of its alternates, or the character's style does not draw it (All Caps, Small Caps, another numeral system) → {id, start, end (the character's bytes), gid (the glyph drawn)}

commands.label: Glyphs
commands.params: {id, start: byte (a character of it)} the alternate glyphs of that character in its font, what the Glyphs panel's Show › Alternates for Current Selection lists: from the font's OpenType GSUB table, the glyphs that single and alternate substitutions put in place of the character's default glyph, `aalt` first, then `salt`, `ss01` to `ss20`, `swsh`, `cv01` to `cv99`, `hist`, `jalt`, `nalt`, `ornm` and `titl`, each glyph once, the default glyph only when `aalt` lists it → {char, font: family, style: style, default: glyph id, chosen: glyph id (the glyph drawn now), alternates: [{gid, feature}]} (empty when the font has none for it; an error when the character's font is not available)

commands.label: Get Text Range
commands.params: {id, start?, end?, effective?: bool = false, story?: bool = false (the whole text of the threaded story `id` is a frame of, its frames in thread order; no `start` or `end`)} → {text, runs: [{text, style}], length}; effective uses document-point size/leading/baseline shift and transformed horizontal scale; default returns stored local styles for rich-text copying

commands.label: Area / Path Type
commands.params: {path: id, mode: "area"|"onPath", text?: "", vertical?: bool = false, at?: [x, y] (on-path start: nearest point), size?, font?, style?, color?, keepModel? (as text.create), fit?: none|autoHeight|shrinkText, fitMinPercent? The range of `id`, else the type objects in `ids`, else the text the Type tool has selected (at a caret: kerning steps the character before it, leading its paragraph), else every selected type object → {ids}

commands.label: Discard Empty Type

commands.params: {id?: text id (default: the text the Type tool edits), at?: byte offset (default: the Type tool's selection, which it replaces; clamped to the text), symbol?: symbol name (default: the Symbols panel's current symbol), scale?: art height ÷ font size = 1 (0 < scale ≤ 100), shift?: pt raise = 0} place a document symbol inline in the text as one character (U+FFFC) that flows like a glyph: its art is scaled to `scale` × the font size tall, its vertical centre on the middle of the cap height raised by `shift`. Typing, Backspace and Delete over it remove it whole → {id, caret}

A style that is the same as the style here of its name, or of its name with a number (`Body 2`), isn't added again; any other is added under a free name (`Body 2`). The file's Normal styles aren't loaded, and a style whose attributes don't read or are out of the range charStyle.new takes, or whose name is empty, is skipped → {added: [names here], existing: [names already here], skipped: [names in the file]} (textStyle.loadAll: {charStyles: {…}, paraStyles: {…}}); charStyle.load and paraStyle.load list only the styles of their own kind

commands.params: {name, to, attrs: {…}} replace name and sparse attributes in one undo step; users keep local overrides; changed numeric attrs: size 0.1..=1296 pt, explicit leading 0.1..=5000 pt, h/v scale 1..=10000%, baseline shift and Tate-chu-yoko offsets -1296..=1296 pt

The file's Normal styles aren't loaded, and a style whose attributes don't read or are out of the range charStyle.new takes, or whose name is empty, is skipped → {added: [names here], existing: [names already here], skipped: [names in the file]} (textStyle.loadAll: {charStyles: {…}, paraStyles: {…}}); charStyle.load and paraStyle.load list only the styles of their own kind

commands.label: Fonts in Document
commands.params: {selectionOnly?} (the type in the art of the symbols in scope included: all of the document's, or those the selected instances show) → [{family, style, runs, objects, missing, status: exact|substitute|missing, resolved: {family, style}, missingGlyphs, version?: the installed version the type names (when it names one)}] sorted by name. A font is found by any of its names (ヒラギノ角ゴシック = Hiragino Sans) among the loaded and installed fonts; substitute: the family is there but not the style (resolved names the stand-in); missing: the family is unknown (the fallback family stands in); missingGlyphs: characters of its text the resolved font lacks (drawn by a fallback font)

commands.label: Replace Font
commands.params: {from: {family, style?}, to: {family (any of its names; stored as the font's own family name), style?}, selectionOnly?} (style omitted: every style of the family / keep the closest style); the type in the art of the symbols in scope changes too (all of the document's, or those the selected instances show, so every instance of them follows); text that is hidden or locked, in a hidden or locked group or layer (or group of a symbol's art), or on a locked artboard keeps its font; when no run changes (text already set in the new font, or none to change), the document and its undo history stay as they are → {runs: the runs changed, skipped?: the text objects left in the font, warning?: text (some text was left in its font, or the style set isn't available: its type is drawn in the family's closest style)}

commands.label: Select Text by Font
commands.params: {family, style?} select the text objects using the font, and the instances of the symbols whose art uses it, that are not hidden or locked, in a hidden or locked group or layer, or on a locked artboard → {count}

commands.label: Font List
commands.params: {family?, style?} → {families: [names]} sorted: the bundled fonts, fonts added and the fonts installed on the system (none on the web), each the family's English (canonical) name for `text.setStyle` and documents (without the system's hidden families, whose names start with a dot; they still resolve by name). Preferences › Type › Show Font Names in English only changes the UI menu labels, not this list; with family: {family, styles: [names] (upright styles by weight, then italics; an error when the family isn't available), axes: [{tag, name, min, default, max, value, hidden}] (a variable font's variation axes, the Character panel's Variable Font sliders, with `value` the setting of `style`, else of the first style; empty for a static font; `hidden`: the font asks for the axis not to be shown)}

commands.label: Refresh Font List
commands.params: {} scan the system font folders again, for fonts installed or removed since the app started; text in a font that became available redraws in it, and text in a family that was removed redraws in the fallback font (no fonts are installed on the web) → {families, faces} (families listed, installed faces found)

commands.label: Missing Fonts
commands.params: {} → {fonts: [{family, style, status: missing|substitute, resolved: {family, style}}] (sorted by name; at most 1000), count, fontsNextToDocument?} the fonts the active document's type uses, in its layers and its symbols, that aren't available as named: missing (the family is unknown and the fallback family stands in) or substitute (the family is there but not the style; resolved names the stand-in), as text.fonts says. CSS generic families such as sans-serif and names longer than 256 bytes are left out. fontsNextToDocument: the Fonts folder next to the saved document (File › Package writes it), when there is one and a search may start there (not in another app's folders, such as a mail app's attachments)

commands.label: Find Font Files
commands.params: {folder?: an absolute path, fonts?: [{family, style?}] (1 to 1000; default: the active document's missing fonts, as text.missingFonts lists them), maxSeconds?: 60 (1 to 600), stop?: false (true: stop the last search)} with folder: look in it and its subfolders for font files that make the fonts available, on separate threads, and answer at once (state: searching); without folder: the last search's state, with the files found so far. A search reads the table directories and the name, fvar and OS/2 tables of .ttf, .otf, .ttc and .otc files of at most 256 MB and, on macOS, of suitcase fonts (files without an extension or with .suit, whose fonts are in a resource fork of at most 8 MB), and lists a file for a font when the file, added with text.addFontFiles, makes the font resolve exactly as text.fonts resolves it; fonts that resolve exactly already are left out. It doesn't enter app packages, folders named Program Files (also x86 and Arm), ProgramData, $Recycle.Bin or System Volume Information, the system's folders at the root of a volume, the Shared and Public folders in Users, a home folder's Library, AppData, Applications, snap and dot folders, a Library folder's app data folders or the folders the environment names for apps' data, and a search of a folder inside one of them fails; the walk also skips other hidden folders, folders whose contents are in the cloud and folders more than 64 levels deep, and follows no links (a picked path is resolved through its links); none on the web → {id (absent while idle), state: idle|searching|done|stopped|failed, folder?, fonts: [{family, style, status, files: [paths]}], searched?: {folders, files, fontFiles}, skipped?, unreadable?, stopped?: stop|time|limit, error?, seconds?}

A header that names no variable defines one, unbound: `#Name` defines a visibility variable, `@Name` defines an image variable, and a header without a prefix defines a text variable. A prefixed header whose name is a variable of another kind, and a `%` header that isn't a variable's exact name (graph data files), are refused, and so are two headers that name one variable and a header that would define a variable while the variables are locked. Every data set is deleted, and every variable of the document is deleted with its bindings and values except a text variable the library also declares, which keeps its bindings; then the library's other variables whose `trait` is `textcontent` are defined as text variables, unbound, and each data set takes a value for a variable from the `p` elements of the element named after it, one paragraph each. Variables of other kinds are left out and named in `skipped` and `warning`. Refused while the variables are locked when it would delete or define a variable → {variables, deleted, deletedDataSets, names, skipped, warning?}

Variables of other kinds are left out with their values and named in `skipped` and `warning`. Refused without a text variable, for a text variable whose name isn't an XML name (letters, digits, `-`, `_` and `.`, starting with a letter or `_`), for a data set name or value that holds a control character, for a data set name with white space at either end, for a name longer than 255 characters or used twice, and past variable.loadLibrary's caps (256 variables, 1,000 data sets, 8 MiB). Without path → {xml, variables, datasets, skipped, warning?}; with it → {path, variables, datasets, skipped, warning?}
