commands.params: {index?: n | indices?: [n…] (default: the artboards the Artboard tool has selected), selectedArtboards?: [n…] (the journal records that default here, for a replay), art?: bool (default: the Artboard tool's moveArt option), patterns?: bool (Transform Patterns: pattern fills and strokes transform with the art; default: prefs transformPatternTiles), lockedAndHidden?: bool (locked and hidden art goes too; default: prefs moveLockedWithArtboard)} a copy of each artboard, the copies placed together right of the last artboard as they lay, with copies of the art fully inside each when `art`, in one undo step → {index: the first copy's index, indices: the copies' indices, ids: the art's copies}

commands.label: Copy Artboard
commands.params: {index? | indices?, selectedArtboards?, art?, lockedAndHidden?} (defaults as artboard.duplicate) put the artboards, and the art fully inside each when `art`, on the clipboard: edit.paste adds a copy of each, together right of the last artboard as they lay, edit.pasteInPlace/InFront/InBack where they were, in this or another document (one undo step; edit.pasteOnAllArtboards pastes only the art); edit.copy runs this while the Artboard tool is chosen → {copied: objects}

commands.label: Cut Artboard
commands.params: {index? | indices?, selectedArtboards?, art?, lockedAndHidden?} artboard.copy, then delete the artboards and that art in one undo step (one artboard is always left: the cut fails when it names every artboard, or a locked one; art also on another locked artboard stays, and is left off the clipboard, unless lockedAndHidden); edit.cut runs this while the Artboard tool is chosen → {copied: objects}

commands.label: Rename Artboards
commands.params: {index? | indices?, selectedArtboards?: [n…] (as artboard.duplicate), name} (default: the artboards the Artboard tool has selected, else its active one) rename the artboards in one undo step: one takes `name` (trimmed), and several take it numbered in artboard order, `name-1`, `name-2` and so on; a locked artboard is renamed too. An empty name is an error, and when every artboard already has its new name nothing changes and no undo step is recorded → {renamed: [index…]}

commands.label: Switch Orientation
commands.params: {index? | indices?, selectedArtboards?: [n…] (as artboard.duplicate), scaleArt?: bool (default: the Artboard tool's Scale Artwork with Artboard option), patterns?, lockedAndHidden?: bool (as artboard.setProps)} (default: the artboards the Artboard tool has selected, else its active one) each artboard swaps its width and height and keeps its top-left corner, in one undo step; a square artboard and a locked one stay as they are, the call fails with `the artboard is locked` when every artboard it names is locked, and when nothing else changes no undo step is recorded → {switched: [index…]}

commands.label: Character / Paragraph
commands.params: {ids?|id?, kerning?: 1/1000 em|"auto"|"optical", baselineShift?: pt, hScale?: %, vScale?: %, rotation?: deg, underline?, strikethrough?, allCaps?, smallCaps?: bool, position?: "normal"|"superscript"|"subscript" (sizes from Document Setup), leftIndent?, rightIndent?, firstLineIndent?, spaceBefore?, spaceAfter?: pt (±1296), list?: "none"|"bullet"|"number", bullet?: "none"|"dot"|"dash"|"circle"|"square", number?: "none"|"arabic"|"upperLetters"|"lowerLetters"|"upperRoman"|"lowerRoman"|"twoDigits"|"threeDigits" (Paragraph panel › Bullets and Numbered List: each paragraph of a list starts with its marker, drawn in the font, size and color of the paragraph's first character, and its text starts at the next tab stop after the marker, the left indent counting as a stop; a bulleted list's marker is its bullet, and a numbered list's is the paragraph's number and a period: 1, 2, 3; A to Z, then AA, BB; a to z, then aa, bb; I, II, III; i, ii, iii; 01 to 99, then 100; 001 to 999, then 1000; letters and roman numerals past 3999 in Arabic digits; the numbers count the story's numbered paragraphs, its threaded frames included, from 1 after a paragraph in no list, and an empty or bulleted paragraph is not counted; list "bullet" keeps a list's bullet, else a dot, and list "number" keeps a numbered list's style, else arabic; without list, a number style makes a numbered list and a bullet makes a bulleted one; "none" in any of the three turns the list off; a paragraph that joins a list with left and first-line indents of 0 gets 18 and -18 unless the call sets an indent; a horizontal right-to-left list paragraph has its indents mirrored, measured from the right), hyphenate?: bool, wordsLongerThan?: letters 1..25 (5), afterFirst?, beforeLast?: letters 1..15 (3), hyphenLimit?: lines 0..25 (0: no limit), hyphenationZone?: pt 0..1296 (0; Single-line Composer only), hyphenateCapitalized?: bool (true) (Paragraph panel menu › Hyphenation…: only words longer than wordsLongerThan break, keeping afterFirst letters before the hyphen and beforeLast after it; at most hyphenLimit lines in a row end with a hyphen; a line whose text already ends within hyphenationZone of its right edge breaks before the next word instead of hyphenating it; the counts are rounded, and every value is clamped to its range), wordSpacing?: % 0..1000 (80, 100, 133), letterSpacing?: % of a word space -100..500 (0, 0, 0), glyphScaling?: % 50..200 (100, 100, 100): each [min, desired, max] or {min?, desired?, max?} (Paragraph panel menu › Justification…: Desired applies to every line, Minimum and Maximum bound what justified lines may use; values are clamped to their range, and Minimum ≤ Desired ≤ Maximum must hold afterwards or nothing changes), autoLeading?: % of the size 0..500 (120; the leading of characters whose leading is Auto), singleWordJustification?: "fullJustify"|"alignLeft"|"alignCenter"|"alignRight" (a justified line holding one word), mojikumi?: "none"|"lineEndHalf" (Japanese punctuation spacing), kinsoku?: "none"|"hard"|"soft" (Kinsoku Set: Soft lets 々, ー and small kana start a line), direction?: "auto"|"leftToRight"|"rightToLeft" (paragraph direction; auto: from each paragraph's first strong character), leadingModel?: "romanBaseline"|"emBoxTop" (leading measured baseline to baseline, or em box top to top), charAlign?: "romanBaseline"|"emBoxTop"|"emBoxCenter"|"emBoxBottom"|"icfTop"|"icfBottom" (where characters smaller than the largest on their line line up with it), proportionalMetrics?: bool (full-width glyphs on the font's proportional widths: `palt` in horizontal type, `vpal` in vertical type), tateChuYoko?: bool (Character panel menu › Tate-chu-yoko, with Show East Asian Options: in vertical type those characters stand side by side across one em of the column; kept on the characters and ignored in horizontal type), tcyUpDown?, tcyLeftRight?: pt -1296..1296 (Character panel menu › Tate-chu-yoko Settings, as text.setRangeStyle: a tate-chu-yoko block moves up or down, right or left), standardVerticalRoman?: bool (Character panel menu › Standard Vertical Roman Alignment, as text.setRangeStyle), noBreak?: bool (Character panel menu › No Break: these characters stay on one line, including across a space inside the run), kashidas?: bool (Character panel menu › Kashidas: selected characters allow insertion only when both joined neighbors have it on; on by default), charDirection?: "default"|"leftToRight"|"rightToLeft" (Character panel menu › Character Direction: the characters are set left to right or right to left inside their paragraph, as a Unicode bidi embedding; default: as the bidi algorithm sets them), digits?: "default"|"arabic"|"hindi"|"farsi"|"devanagari"|"bengali"|"gurmukhi"|"gujarati"|"odia"|"tamil"|"telugu"|"kannada"|"malayalam" (Character panel menu › Digits: the numeral system every digit is drawn in, whatever was typed: Western, Arabic-Indic (hindi), Eastern Arabic-Indic (farsi) or an Indic script's own digits), fontHeightReference?: "emBox"|"capHeight"|"xHeight"|"icfBox" (Character panel › Set Font Height Reference, as text.setRangeStyle: the height of the font that the size measures), language?: name|tag (Character panel › Language, as text.setRangeStyle), fontAxes?: {"wght": 650, …} (Character panel › Variable Font, as text.setRangeStyle: each axis named set in its units and clamped to its range, null back to the style's own setting), burasagari?: "none"|"standard"|"forced" (Paragraph panel menu › Burasagari None/Regular/Force: an East Asian comma or full stop ending an area type line hangs outside it: when it doesn't fit, or always; new type: "standard"), romanHangingPunctuation?: bool (Paragraph panel menu › Roman Hanging Punctuation: quotation marks, hyphens, full stops and commas starting or ending a line hang outside the margin, asterisks, tildes, ellipses, dashes, colons and semicolons by half; off by default), kashida?: "none"|"short"|"medium"|"long"|"stylistic" (Paragraph panel › Insert Kashidas: justified lines of horizontal area type lengthen each Arabic word with a kashida between its last pair of joined letters, at most a quarter, half or whole em long, or whole tatweels up to an em for stylistic, before they widen their word spaces; none by default), composer?: "singleLine"|"everyLine" (line breaking, Every-line by default), start?: byte, end?: byte} (baselineShift is in document points and hScale includes the object transform; groups include their text descendants; with a range: the character attributes style that range and the paragraph attributes apply to the paragraphs it touches; without: all the text)

commands.label: Convert to Text
commands.params: {ids?|id?, start?: byte, end?: byte} (Type › Bullets and Numbering › Convert to Text: the paragraphs of the selected type, or of `ids`, or those a start/end range touches; after Select All in a frame of threaded text, without `ids`, `id` or a range, every paragraph of the story's frames that are neither locked nor hidden; while the story is selected, its locked and hidden frames are not converted even when named, nor a paragraph whose text starts in one) the marker of each list paragraph becomes characters of its text: the bullet, or the number and its period as the paragraph showed it, then a tab, at the start of the paragraph in the marker's font, size and color; the list is turned off. When the marker's tab went to the left indent, the paragraph gets a left-aligned tab stop without a leader there, in place of any stop there, which keeps the text after the tab where it started; when it went to a tab stop and a stop there or past it has a leader or is not left-aligned, or a right, center or decimal stop lies between the marker and that place, the paragraph gets a left-aligned stop without a leader where the marker's tab ended, in place of any stop there and of those right, center and decimal stops before it (past the left indent only in a paragraph with no tab of its own). In threaded type the numbers are those counted through the story's frames, and a paragraph that continues into a later frame is converted where its text starts. An empty list paragraph has no marker and only leaves the list. A paragraph with no direction set gets the direction it ran in when the characters would change it (a letter or roman numeral before right-to-left text). With the Every-line Composer, a paragraph with a tab is broken line by line, so a converted paragraph can break its lines at other places. While the Type tool edits, its typing ends first and its anchor and caret move past the characters inserted at or before them (a whole story that Select All selected stays selected when the call converts all of it); in threaded type, when the caret's character moved to another frame, the tool edits that frame, which becomes the selection when it was not selected. One undo step → {ids, converted: paragraphs, inserted: [{id, at: byte before the change, length: bytes}]}

commands.label: Shape Builder
commands.params: {ids?|id?: [id…] (default: selection), points: [[x,y]…] (drag path; one point = click; may be left out with rect), rect?: [x, y, width, height] (Shift-drag marquee from where the drag started, x and y, to x+width and y+height; width and height may be negative: touches every region whose outline crosses the rectangle or has an anchor inside it and the region holding the whole rectangle, the region under x, y comes first and the one under the opposite corner comes next; with points, it also touches the regions along them; for pickColorFrom, x, y is the drag's first point and the opposite corner is its last), erase?: bool (erase mode, Alt: deletes the regions touched, and the pieces of open paths that cut regions and the edges (outline pieces between the points where paths meet; see shapeBuilder.regions) within tolerance, except that a point in a region no more than twice the tolerance across there touches the region; a deleted edge opens its path there, and edges bounding a deleted region go with it; what is left of each path keeps its look, with gradients fitted to its bounds kept where they were on it, its name, opacity mask and attributes, and its fill rule unless merged regions shaped it), splitStroke?: false (In Merge Mode, Clicking Stroke Splits the Path; not with erase or rect: when the one point of a click is within tolerance of a stroke, the path that stroke is on splits in two instead of a merge: the path keeps the rest of it, and a copy of the path holding the run of it from the anchor or crossing point before the click to the one after it, in the path's direction, goes directly above it; both keep the path's gradients where they were on it; the other objects stay as they are; with pickColorFrom "swatches" or fill, the run's stroke takes that paint; a path in a Live Paint group or a Shaper Group does not split, and nor does a path the run is all of, such as a lone line, or all but 0.05 pt or less of (a ten-thousandth of the larger side of a path over 500 pt)), tolerance?: pt (2, erase or splitStroke), gap?: pt (0–72; 0: Gap Detection off), openFilledAsClosed?: true (Consider Open Filled Paths as Closed: a filled open path bounds a region as if an invisible edge closed it; false: it cuts the regions it crosses like an unfilled one), pickColorFrom?: "artwork" (default: the merged shape takes the look of the front-most object under the first point, else under the last point, else of the front-most object) | "swatches" (the current fill, with the rest of the look of the front-most object over the first region the drag touches that an object covers, else of the front-most object), fill?: "#rrggbb" | {color|swatch|gradient|none} (overrides pickColorFrom)} replaces the paths it uses where they are; other selected objects (type, hidden or locked objects, clipping paths) stay, and a group goes only when it is left empty → {ids (selected after: each selected object still there, or what took its place), merged, regions, lines, edges (counts deleted, merged or split), split?: id (the run split off, after a split)}; after a split, ids are the roots, with the rest and the run in place of the path when it was one

commands.label: Shape Builder Regions
commands.params: {ids?|id?, gap?: pt (0–72; 0: Gap Detection off), openFilledAsClosed?: true (as shapeBuilder.merge)} → {regions: [{bounds: [x0,y0,x1,y1], area, sources: [id…]}], lines: [{bounds, source: id}], edges: [{bounds, source: id}]} faces of the planar arrangement (unfilled open paths cut them, and filled ones too with openFilledAsClosed false; sources is empty for an area only they enclose), the pieces of those open paths and the edges (the other paths' outlines cut where paths meet; source: the front-most path along it), which erasing deletes

commands.label: Make
commands.params: {ids?|id?} build a Live Paint group from the selected paths (paths, compound paths and groups of them; type, images and other objects are refused, nothing changes); each covered face starts with its front-most covering source's fill; with a Live Paint group among them, add the others to it as livePaint.merge does → {id, faces, edges}

commands.label: Merge
commands.params: {ids?|id?} add the other selected paths (compound paths, groups of paths and Live Paint groups too; type, images and other objects are refused, nothing changes) to the bottom-most Live Paint group, keeping its id, its paint and its own properties (name, lock, visibility, transparency, appearance, opacity mask, graphic style link) → {id, faces, edges}

commands.label: Release
commands.params: {id?, ids?: [id…] (instead of id)} replace Live Paint groups with their original paths → {ids}

commands.label: Expand
commands.params: {id?, ids?: [id…] (instead of id)} turn Live Paint groups into plain groups of their painted faces and edges → {ids}

commands.label: Gap Options
commands.params: {id?, ids?: [id…] (instead of id; default: the selected Live Paint groups), detect?: bool (Gap Detection: paint stops at gaps up to size wide), size?: "small" (3 pt) | "medium" (6 pt) | "large" (12 pt) | pt (custom, over 0 up to 72) (Paint Stops At), color?: #rrggbb or a layer color's name such as "Red" (Gap Preview Color; a hex color with an alpha part, #rrggbbaa or #rgba, is an error), closeGaps?: bool (add an unpainted path across each gap up to size wide to the group's paths)} set the Gap Options of Live Paint groups (what is not given stays as it was; a group starts with detect false, small and Red) and make their faces again, keeping their paint → {ids, faces, gaps: [[x0,y0,x1,y1]…] (the gaps up to size wide that no path closes, from a loose end of a path to where it closes to; detect closes them for paint), closed (paths added)}

commands.label: Live Paint Bucket
commands.params: {group?: id | ids?|id?: [id…] (paths to make live first, as livePaint.make does), point: [x,y], color?|swatch?|gradient?|none? (default: current fill; a color in #rrggbbaa or #rgba is refused), tint?: 0..100, keepModel?: bool (both as paint.setFill)} fill the face containing point, skipping hidden faces → {group, face}

commands.label: Live Paint Bucket (Stroke)
commands.params: {group: id, point: [x,y], color?|swatch?|none? (default: current stroke), width?: pt (default: current weight), tolerance?: pt (4), tint?: 0..100, keepModel?: bool (both as paint.setFill)} paint the edge nearest point → {group, edge}

commands.label: Live Paint Info
commands.params: {group, id?: object id (default: the selection)} → {faces: [{id, fill, bounds}], edges: [{id, stroke, width}], sources, gapOptions: {detect, size: "small"|"medium"|"large"|pt, points, color: #rrggbb} (as livePaint.gapOptions sets them), gaps: [[x0,y0,x1,y1]…] (as livePaint.gapOptions returns them)}

commands.label: Make
commands.params: {id?: image or Image Trace group (default: selection), preset?: name (imageTrace.presets), savedPreset?: {settings} (a saved preset's settings, which the journal records so a replay traces with them after the preset is changed, renamed or deleted; used in place of the saved preset `preset` names), enhanced?: false (the preset's enhanced version: with Auto Grouping, and with Shapes in all but High Fidelity Photo; Flat Logo has none and is traced as it is), params?: {mode: "blackAndWhite"|"grayscale"|"color"|"logo", threshold: 0-255, palette: "limited"|"fullTone"|"automatic"|"documentLibrary" (color mode; limited: the `colors` best colours, fullTone: as many as the tones need, more with colorDetail, automatic: flat art with its own colours, else fullTone, documentLibrary: at most `colors` of the library's colours, as they are), colors: 2-256, colorDetail: 0-100 (fullTone, automatic), library: "document" (the document's swatches) or a swatch library id or name (swatch.library.list; documentLibrary), colorGroup?: name (color mode, documentLibrary with library "document": the colors of that document color group instead of every swatch; "" is every swatch), paths: 0-100, corners: 0-100, noise: px, method: "abutting"|"overlapping", ignoreWhite (leave out white areas), ignoreColor?: "#rrggbb" (with ignoreWhite: the colour left out instead of white), snapCurvesToLines, shapes: false (filled outlines that are a circle, an ellipse, a rectangle or a regular polygon come out as that live shape), autoGrouping: false (each path that has others inside it is grouped with them), gradients: false (grayscale and color: an area whose colour changes evenly along one direction is one path with a linear gradient fill), fills: true, strokes: false (Create: lines up to strokeWidth wide become stroked centre lines; without fills, wider areas become stroked outlines), strokeWidth: px (10), logoColors?: ["#rrggbb"…] (mode logo: flat-colour logos only; colours found automatically or named here, white is always its own colour, at most ten; noise = areas under noise/10 px ignored; edges to a fraction of a pixel, sharp corners restored, lines and circles snapped; enclosed transparent areas are painted white unless ignoreWhite makes them holes; fills/strokes are ignored; gradients and photos are refused)}, view?: as imageTrace.setView (default: the traced object's own, else tracingResult), ids?: [id…] (instead of id)} → {id, paths, anchors, colors, warnings: [text…] (the image is over 1500 px on a side, so it traces more slowly; or it was traced scaled down; Flat Logo names only the size it traced a larger image at)}

commands.label: Make and Expand
commands.params: {…as imageTrace.make} same as imageTrace.make, then expand → {id, paths, anchors, colors}

commands.label: Release
commands.params: {id?, ids?: [id…] (instead of id)} put the source image back in place of Image Trace groups → {ids}

commands.label: Expand
commands.params: {id?, ids?: [id…] (instead of id)} keep only the traced paths (drop the source image) → {ids}

commands.label: Image Trace View
commands.params: {id?|ids?: Image Trace objects (default: selection), view: "tracingResult"|"tracingResultWithOutlines"|"outlines"|"outlinesWithSourceImage"|"sourceImage"} how they draw on screen; exports, printing and Expand keep the tracing result → {ids, view}

commands.label: Image Trace Presets
commands.params: {} → {presets: [{name, builtIn, params, enhanced: the params of the preset's enhanced version, null if it has none}], revision: grows each time the saved presets change} the built-in presets, then the saved ones (builtIn false, enhanced null); any of these names works as imageTrace.make's `preset`

commands.label: Save Image Trace Preset
commands.params: {name?: (default: a new "Tracing Preset N"), newName?: rename the saved preset `name`, preset?: the preset to start from (default: the saved preset `name`, else Default), enhanced?, params?: {settings, as imageTrace.make takes them, over the preset's}} create or change a saved tracing preset, kept with the preferences (built-in ones can't change) → {name, params, created, renamedFrom: the name before `newName` changed it, else null}

commands.label: Delete Image Trace Preset
commands.params: {name} delete a saved tracing preset (built-in ones stay) → {deleted: name}

commands.label: Shaper
commands.params: {points: [[x,y]…], ids?: [id…] (default: nearby art), tolerance?: pt (4)} interior scribbles remove fills; scribbles through several regions merge with the origin fill; ending outside removes fills and boundary strokes; outside scribbles erase stroke pieces. Originals remain editable → {id, regions, strokes}

commands.label: Select Shaper Face
commands.params: {point: [x,y], source?: bool} click selects a group, then a face; source enters construction isolation and selects an original (while an opacity mask or a pattern is edited, it selects the original and the editing layer stays isolated); while a group's originals are isolated, it selects one of that group's originals → {id}

commands.label: Release Shaper Group
commands.params: {id? (default: selection)} restore the original paths → {ids}

commands.label: Expand Shaper Group
commands.params: {id? (default: selection)} keep the visible result as ordinary paths → {id}

commands.label: Remove from Shaper Group
commands.params: {source: id, group?: id (default: the Shaper Group that holds `source`)} take one original shape out of its Shaper Group: it becomes a path just above the group, keeps its look and is selected, and Construction mode ends; the group's result is computed again from the shapes left, and a group left with none is removed. In Construction mode, a Selection-tool move that ends with an original shape wholly outside the bounds the group's original shapes had does the same in the move's undo step (object.transform's `releaseOutside`) → {id}

commands.label: Brushes
commands.params: {} → {brushes: [{name, type}], current}

commands.label: Brush Definition
commands.params: {name} → the brush definition (JSON)

commands.label: Brush Art
commands.params: {ids?|id?} → {art: the object brush.new takes as a new scatter or art brush's art and as a new pattern brush's side tile (several objects become one group), or null when nothing is selected or ids name no object}

commands.label: Apply Brush
commands.params: {name, ids?|id?} apply a brush to the strokes of the selected paths (adds a stroke if missing) and make it current → {ids}

commands.label: Remove Brush Stroke
commands.params: {ids?|id?} remove brushes from the selected strokes → {ids}

commands.label: Current Brush
commands.params: {name: string|null} the brush the Paintbrush tool paints with (not an undo step)

commands.label: New Brush…
commands.params: {type: calligraphic|scatter|art|pattern|bristle, name? (trimmed; blank: New <Type> Brush; a bristle brush name, with the number a taken name gets, has at most 31 characters), params?: {…definition fields}, ids?|id?} new brush; art/scatter/pattern brushes take the selected art (pattern: side tile) unless params give it → {name}

commands.label: Delete Brush
commands.params: {name} | {names: [name…]} delete brushes; strokes using them become plain strokes

commands.label: Move Brush
commands.params: {name? | names?: [brush names of one type, in order], to?: index among the brushes of that type in brush.list order (they go before the brush of that type now there that isn't moving; default: after the last one), type?: calligraphic|scatter|art|pattern|bristle (the type they go into; default: theirs)} reorder brushes within their type, as one undo step (none when the order stays as it was); brushes of different types, or a type that isn't theirs, are refused (brushes move only within their type) → {moved}

commands.label: Duplicate Brush
commands.params: {name, newName? (trimmed; blank: <name> copy)} | {names: [name…]} → {name} | {names}

commands.label: Select All Unused
commands.params: {} → {names: [the brushes no stroke paints with, in library order]} (the Brushes panel selects them): strokes in the art (opacity masks included), symbols, graph designs, pattern tiles (with the tiles that pattern editing's Cancel puts back) and graphic styles count, and so do strokes in the art of a brush that is used

commands.label: Brush Options…
commands.params: {name, params?: {…fields to change (brush.get shows them; values outside their ranges are clamped). calligraphic: angle −180..180°, roundness 0..100%, size 0..1296 pt, variation: [angle°, roundness%, size pt], modes: [fixed|random|pressure|tilt|bearing|rotation for angle, roundness, size] (pressure goes from value − variation at the lightest pen pressure to value + variation at the heaviest; tilt from value − variation with the pen lying flat to value + variation with it upright; bearing and rotation add variation × the pen's bearing (which way it leans, counter-clockwise from leaning right) or its barrel's counter-clockwise rotation over 180°; the angle turns on past ±180°). scatter: size [a, b] 1..10000%, spacing [a, b] 1..10000%, scatter [a, b] −1000..1000%, rotation [a, b] −180..180°, modes: [fixed|random|pressure|tilt|bearing|rotation for size, spacing, scatter, rotation] (fixed: a; random: between a and b; pressure: a at the lightest pen pressure to b at the heaviest; tilt: a with the pen lying flat to b upright; bearing and rotation: a at −180° to b at 180°), rotation_relative_to_path. art: width 1..1000%, width_mode: null (fixed)|pressure, width_max 1..1000% (pressure: width at the lightest pen pressure to width_max at the heaviest, half way on a stroke drawn without pressure), scale: {mode: proportional|stretch|betweenGuides, start, end: 0..1 of the art length}, direction: leftToRight|rightToLeft|topToBottom|bottomToTop, flip_along, flip_across, overlap. pattern: scale 1..10000%, spacing 0..10000%, fit: stretch|addSpace|approximate, flip_along, flip_across, outer_corner and inner_corner: corner tile art (drawn as the corner that joins a side tile on its right to one below it) or null, outer_source and inner_source: what that kind of corner draws without its art: none|autoCentered|autoBetween|autoSliced|autoOverlap (a tile made from the side tile), or null (the other kind of corner's art); side_tile, outer_corner_tile, inner_corner_tile, start_tile, end_tile: a document pattern name, original, or none (side refuses none); corner tiles also take autoCentered|autoBetween|autoSliced|autoOverlap. Each tile also accepts {pattern: name} to select a swatch whose name is a reserved choice. scatter, art and pattern: colorization: {method: none|tints|tintsAndShades|hueShift, key: colour (hueShift: the art colour that becomes the stroke colour; without a key: the solid color the art's fills and strokes use most, black when they use none)}; colorization and the art brush's scale change only the fields given}, newName? (trimmed; blank: the name is kept; a new bristle brush name has at most 31 characters, and a longer name the brush has is kept)} edit a brush definition (strokes using it update) → {name}

commands.label: Expand Brush Strokes
commands.params: {ids?|id?} replace brushed paths (in the selection) with groups of the brush art → {ids}

commands.label: Paintbrush
commands.params: {…params as path.freehand, brush} paint a freehand stroke with a brush → {id}

commands.label: Symbols
commands.params: {} → {symbols: [{name, instances, size: [w,h], registration: 0..8, exportType: movieClip|graphic, nineSlice, type: static|dynamic}], current}

commands.label: New Symbol…
commands.params: {name?, ids?|id?, registration?: 0..8 (9-point grid, 4 = centre; Symbol Options › Registration), exportType?: movieClip (default)|graphic, nineSlice?: bool, nineSliceGuides?: array, type?: static (default)|dynamic (Symbol Options › Symbol Type)} make a symbol from the selection and replace it with an instance; a frame of threaded text in the selection leaves its thread with the text it shows, which the symbol's art holds; nineSlice is Symbol Options › Enable Guides for 9-Slice Scaling, nineSliceGuides [left, top, right, bottom] as fractions 0..1 of the natural size (default a quarter each); an instance of a symbol with guides keeps its corners' size when scaled, its edges stretch along their length and its center in both directions → {name, id, registration, exportType, nineSlice, type}

commands.label: Symbol Options…
commands.params: {name?, newName?, registration?: 0..8, exportType?: movieClip|graphic, nineSlice?: bool, nineSliceGuides?: array, type?: static|dynamic} rename a symbol and/or set Symbol Options › Registration, Export Type, 9-slice guides (nineSliceGuides [left, top, right, bottom] fractions 0..1) and Symbol Type (a dynamic symbol's instances may change the appearance of objects in its art and stay linked; making it static drops those changes); default name: current → {name, registration, exportType, nineSlice, type}

commands.label: Place Symbol Instance
commands.params: {name?, x?, y?} place an instance so its registration point is at (x, y) (default: artboard centre; name default: current) → {id}

commands.label: Break Link to Symbol
commands.params: {ids?|id?} expand selected instances into plain art (with their appearance changes to a dynamic symbol), placed through the symbol's 9-slice guides when it has them, with the instance's opacity mask → {ids}

commands.label: Edit Symbol
commands.params: {id?, ids?: [id…] (instead of id), name?, x?, y?, artboard?: index=0 (the active artboard; the app passes it), viewCenter?: [x, y] (the app passes the view's center)} edit a symbol's art in symbol editing mode: the instance `id` (default: the selected instances, which must share one symbol) where it shows the art, else the symbol `name` (default: the current symbol) centered on (x, y) (default: the center of artboard `artboard`, or of the first artboard when there is no such artboard; in a document without artboards, viewCenter, else (0, 0)); every instance follows each edit and the instance stays linked (symbol.breakLink expands one); refused while a pattern or an opacity mask is edited → {name, layer, id?}

commands.label: Exit Symbol Editing Mode
commands.params: {} leave symbol editing mode; after an edit, select the instance it was entered from; leaving without having changed the art adds no undo step and restores the selection from before entry (object.exitIsolation also leaves it) → {name?}

commands.label: Redefine Symbol
commands.params: {name, ids?|id?} replace the symbol's art with the selection (instances update, keeping their appearance changes to the objects at paths the new art still has; the selection becomes an instance; a frame of threaded text in the selection leaves its thread with the text it shows, which the symbol's art holds) → {name, id}

commands.label: Delete Symbol
commands.params: {name | names: [name…], expandInstances?: true} delete a symbol (or several, in one undo step); its instances are expanded (or deleted with false)

commands.label: Duplicate Symbol
commands.params: {name, newName?} → {name}

commands.label: Replace Symbol
commands.params: {name, ids?|id?} swap the symbol of the selected instances (an instance given a different symbol drops its appearance changes; one given its own symbol keeps them) → {ids}

commands.label: Symbol Instance Appearance
commands.params: {id?|ids?: [one id] (default: the one selected object), path: [i…] (the object in the symbol's art: child indices in paint order from the art's root down through its groups; [] the root), fill?: "#rrggbb"|{…paint params of paint.setFill: color, none, swatch, tint, gradient, keepModel}|null (null: the symbol's own again), stroke?: as fill, opacity?: 0..100|null, blend?: name|null} change the appearance of one object of a dynamic symbol instance's art, for that instance only: it stays linked, so editing the symbol reshapes it and keeps the change; refused for a static symbol or a path naming no object → {id, overrides: how many objects the instance changes}

commands.label: Reset Symbol Instance
commands.params: {ids?|id?} drop the selected dynamic symbol instances' own appearance changes, so they show the symbol's appearance again → {ids: the instances that had changes}

commands.label: Reset Transformation
commands.params: {ids?|id?} give the selected symbol instances (in groups too) their symbol's own scale, without rotation, shear or reflection, keeping the center of each one's bounding box in place, as one undo step; other objects, instances in perspective and instances already at their symbol's scale are left as they are, and no undo step is added when nothing changes; an id naming no object, or no symbol instance among the objects, is an error → {ids: the instances changed}

commands.label: Current Symbol
commands.params: {name} the symbol the symbolism tools spray (not an undo step)

commands.label: Select All Unused
commands.params: {} → {names: [the symbols nothing places, in panel order]} (the Symbols panel selects them): instances in the art (opacity masks included), graph designs, pattern tiles (with the tiles that pattern editing's Cancel puts back) and brush art count, and so do instances in the art of a symbol that is used

commands.label: Select All Instances
commands.params: {name} select every instance of a symbol → {count}

commands.label: Symbol Sprayer
commands.params: {points: [[x,y]…], name?, radius?: 40, density?: 1..10 (5), scale?: 1, alt?: bool (remove instances)} spray instances into a symbol set → {id, count}

commands.label: Symbolism Tool
commands.params: {tool: shift|scrunch|size|spin|stain|screen|style, points: [[x,y]…], radius?: 40, intensity?: 1..10 (5), alt?: bool, color? (#rrggbbaa and #rgba are refused), keepModel?: bool (as paint.setFill), style?: name} adjust instances near the points (selection, else all) → {count}

commands.label: Make
commands.params: {ids?, name? (trimmed; blank: New Pattern N), tileType?: grid|brickByRow|brickByColumn|hexByColumn|hexByRow, brickOffset?: 0..1 (0.5), width?, height?, edit?: bool (true)} make a pattern swatch from the selection and enter pattern editing mode; refused while an opacity mask is edited → {name}

commands.label: Edit Pattern
commands.params: {name?} edit a pattern (default: the selected object's fill pattern) in pattern editing mode; refused while an opacity mask is edited

commands.label: Done
commands.params: {} leave pattern editing mode, saving the tile art into the pattern

commands.label: Cancel
commands.params: {} leave pattern editing mode, discarding changes

commands.label: Save a Copy
commands.params: {name? (trimmed; blank: <pattern> copy)} while editing, save the current tile as a new pattern swatch → {name}

commands.label: Pattern Options
commands.params: {name? (default: the pattern being edited), newName? (trimmed; blank: the name is kept), tileType?, brickOffset?, width?, height?, hSpacing?, vSpacing?, sizeTileToArt?: bool, overlap?: {h: left|right, v: top|bottom}, copies?: 3|5|7|9, dimCopies?: %, showTileEdge?: bool, showSwatchBounds?: bool (outline the part of the tiling the swatch repeats, dashed)}

commands.label: Delete Pattern
commands.params: {name} delete a pattern swatch (objects painted with it lose that paint)

commands.label: List Patterns
commands.params: {} → {patterns: [{name, tileType, width, height, ...}], editing?}

commands.label: Transform Patterns
commands.params: {ids?|id?, matrix: [a,b,c,d,e,f]} transform only the pattern placement of the objects' pattern paints (Transform Patterns)

commands.label: Radial
commands.params: {ids?, instances?: n (8), radius?: pt} radial repeat of the selection (or switch the selected repeat to radial) → {id}

commands.label: Grid
commands.params: {ids?, hSpacing?: pt, vSpacing?: pt (¼ of the art size), rows?: n (3), cols?: n (3)} grid repeat of the selection → {id}

commands.label: Mirror
commands.params: {ids?, angle?: deg (90 = vertical axis), offset?: pt (10)} mirror repeat of the selection → {id}

commands.label: Release
commands.params: {} release the selected repeats back to their source art → {ids}

commands.label: Options…
commands.params: {instances?, radius?, reverseOverlap?, startAngle?, endAngle?, center?: [x,y] | hSpacing?, vSpacing?, rows?, cols?, gridType?, flipRows?, flipCols? | angle?} set the options of the selected repeats

commands.label: Expand Repeat
commands.params: {} replace the selected repeats by groups of their instances → {ids}

commands.label: Make
commands.params: {ids?: two or more objects (default: the selection)} put the objects in an Intertwine group and choose the Intertwine tool, which arranges its overlap areas (object.intertwine.arrange) → {id}

commands.label: Edit
commands.params: {} choose the Intertwine tool for the selected Intertwine group (Esc or Enter goes back to the tool before)

commands.label: Release
commands.params: {} give the objects of the selected Intertwine groups back as they were made, dropping the arranged areas → {ids}

commands.label: Arrange Intertwine Area
commands.params: {id?: Intertwine group (default: the selected one), at?: [x,y] (the overlap area under this point, as a click picks it) | area?: [[x,y]…] (a closed polygon drawn around overlap areas: every area whose inside it encloses), order?: toggle|front|forward|backward|back (toggle: the object drawn right below the top comes to the front, so two objects swap; forward and backward move an object one place up or down among the objects in that area; the others keep their order there), member?: id (front, forward, backward and back: the object to move; default: front and forward move the object right below the top, back and backward the top one)} → {count: areas changed (an area already in that order is not changed, and with none changed there is no undo step), top: [id of the object now on top in each changed area]}

commands.label: Attach
commands.params: {path?: id of the path to attach to (without it: choose the Objects on Path tool, whose click on a path attaches the selection to it), ids?: the objects to attach (default: the selection; the path is left out of it), pivot?: 0-8 (the reference point of each object that attaches to the path, row by row from the top left; default: the Objects on Path tool's Pivot, 4, the center, until its options change it), rotate?: degrees counter-clockwise from upright on the path (default: the tool's Rotate, 0 until its options change it)} put the objects and the path in an Objects on Path group: the path at the bottom, the objects spread evenly along it from its first anchor (the last one at the end of an open path) in their order on the canvas, column by column from left to right and top to bottom in each column, each turned to follow the path; editing the path moves them → {id}

commands.label: Objects on Path Options
commands.params: {ids?: Objects on Path groups or objects in them (default: the selection), pivot?: 0-8 (the reference point of each object that attaches to the path, row by row from the top left; 4: the center), rotate?: degrees counter-clockwise from upright on the path, spacing?: points along the path from each object's attachment point to the next one's (0 or more, kept to what the path has room for; or "auto", the default: spread evenly with the last object at the end of an open path), start?: points along the path from its first anchor to the first object's attachment point (default 0)} set how the objects of the groups attach and are spaced → {ids}

commands.label: Expand
commands.params: {ids?: Objects on Path groups or objects in them (default: the selection)} make the groups plain groups of the path and the objects where they are → {ids}

commands.label: Get Preferences
commands.params: {key?} → the value of one preference (or preference group: eyedropper), or {prefs: {…all…}}

commands.label: Set Preference
commands.params: {key, value} or {values: {key: value, …}} set preferences (validated; see prefs.list; lengths in pt or strings with a unit; unitsGeneral also sets the active document's units, one undo step; the eyedropper group takes a partial object, as eyedropper.setOptions; a new recoveryFolder must be a folder that can be listed and written in, and a new pluginsFolder a folder that can be listed: otherwise an error, and nothing changes; an empty value is not checked)

commands.label: Reset Preferences
commands.params: {category?} reset one category (or everything) to defaults

commands.label: List Preferences
commands.params: {} → [{key, category, section, label, kind, value, …}] every preference

commands.label: Width Point
commands.params: {id, t: 0..1 (fraction of the path length), left, right: side widths in pt, index?: width point to edit or move, adjustAdjoining?: bool (the nearest points either side change their widths in proportion, using the sampled widths for a new point)} → {index}. Without index a point already at t is replaced; a point moved onto another one's t joins it as a discontinuous point (on the side it came from), so the width steps there. Creates a uniform profile first if needed

commands.label: Delete Width Point
commands.params: {id, index | indices: [..]} remove width points (removing the last one leaves a uniform stroke)

commands.label: Copy Width Point
commands.params: {id, index: the width point to copy, t: 0..1 where the copy goes} → {index} (Alt-drag with the Width tool). Landing on another point makes a discontinuous point, as a stroke.widthPoint.set move does

commands.label: Width Profile
commands.params: {ids?|id?, points: [[t, left, right]…] (width factors, 1 = the stroke weight) | null = uniform}

commands.label: Liquify
commands.params: {tool: warp|twirl|pucker|bloat|scallop|crystallize|wrinkle, points: [[x,y,pressure?]…] (the brush stroke; pen pressure 0..1, default 1), diameter?|width?, height? (pt, default 100), angle?, intensity? (0..1 or %), usePressure?: bool (each point's pressure is the intensity there), detail? (1..10), simplify?: 0..100, simplifyOn?: bool (default true; both for warp, twirl, pucker, bloat), rate? (twirl °), complexity? (0..15), horizontal?, vertical? (wrinkle, 0..1 or %), affectAnchors?, affectIn?, affectOut?: bool (scallop, crystallize, wrinkle; default true), ids?|id? (default: selection, else every path the brush touches)}

commands.label: Puppet Warp
commands.params: {id?|ids? (default: selection), pins: [[x,y]…] (current pin positions), moved: [[x,y]…] (targets, same length), angles?: [deg|null…] (same length: the turn the art takes around each pin, as Alt-dragging around a pin does; null leaves it free), expand?: pt, rest?: bool, auto?: bool (as object.puppetWarp.pins reports; ignored)} as-rigid-as-possible mesh warp of anchors and handles. rest: true = the Puppet Warp tool's pins: `pins` are points on the shape the pins started from (object.puppetWarp.pins), each must be on its mesh, the warp replaces the previous one instead of adding to it, and the pins are kept with the document for Undo (an empty list removes them all, leaving the art as it is)

commands.label: Puppet Warp Pins
commands.params: {id?|ids? (default: selection), expand?: pt} → {ids, pins, moved, angles, expand, rest: true, auto} the Puppet Warp pins on the art: pins = where each sits on the shape they started from, moved = where it is now, angles = the turn it holds (deg, null = free); auto: none placed yet (the tool's automatic pins: the centre and the end of each limb). Change moved/angles (or add/remove pins) and pass it back to object.puppetWarp

commands.label: Define Perspective Grid
commands.params: {kind?: 1|2|3, origin?: [x,y], horizon?, vpLeft?, vpRight?, vpVertical?: [x,y], distance?, cell?, extent?, height?, visible?, plane?, leftOffset?, rightOffset?, groundOffset?: pt (planes moved along their normals), reproject?: bool, …the other fields of the grid as its reply lists them} merge into the document's grid. Objects in perspective stay where they are, as in the reference app; with reproject they move with the grid (each keeps its place on its plane)

commands.label: Perspective Grid Preset
commands.params: {kind: 1|2|3 (its normal view) | name: a preset (see perspective.presets.list)} reset the grid to the preset fitted to the first artboard (and show it; attached objects stay attached)

commands.label: Show Perspective Grid
commands.params: {visible?: bool} (no param toggles). View state: not an undo step

commands.label: Active Perspective Plane
commands.params: {plane: left|right|ground|none} Plane Switching widget. View state: not an undo step

commands.label: Attach to Active Plane
commands.params: {ids?|id?, plane?: left|right|ground (default: the active plane)} project the objects onto the plane

commands.label: Release with Perspective
commands.params: {ids?|id?} detach from the grid (geometry unchanged)

commands.label: Move in Perspective
commands.params: {ids?|id?, from: [x,y], to: [x,y], plane?, copy?: bool (move copies, as Alt-dragging does), perpendicular?: bool (move along the plane's normal instead, as pressing 5 while dragging does), snap?: bool (default: View › Perspective Grid › Snap to Grid), constrain?: bool (default false; constrain each in-plane move to its plane's nearest axis or 45° diagonal)} slide objects within their own planes (unattached objects attach to `plane`/the active plane first); snapping pulls the nearer edge of the first plane's joint bounds toward a gridline within a quarter cell while preserving the constrained direction; Transform Again repeats it

commands.label: Draw in Perspective
commands.params: {command: shape.* id, params, plane?, snap?: bool (default: Snap to Grid), at?: [x, y] (a point of the plane the shape lies on, as the tool gives it)} run a shape command and attach the result to the plane (snapping its corners to gridlines within a quarter cell)

commands.label: Transform in Perspective
commands.params: {ids?|id?, matrix: [a,b,c,d,e,f] (affine map in plane coordinates, points: u along the plane, v up or away), depth?: pt to move along the plane's normal (default 0), copy?: bool, plane?} transform objects within their own planes (Perspective Selection tool handles; unattached objects attach to `plane`/the active plane first); Transform Again repeats it → {ids}

commands.label: Nudge in Perspective
commands.params: {dx, dy: arrow direction (-1, 0 or 1), big?: bool (×10), copy?: bool} move the selection in perspective by the keyboard increment, as the arrow keys do with the Perspective Selection tool → {ids}

commands.label: Move Plane
commands.params: {plane?: left|right|ground (default: the active plane), offset?: pt (where along its normal; 0 is its place in the grid's definition) | by?: pt, objects?: none|move|copy (default none: the objects on the plane stay; move: they move with it, as Shift-dragging a plane widget does; copy: copies of them do, as Alt-dragging does)} → {plane, offset, ids}

commands.label: Move Plane to Match Object
commands.params: {id? (default: the first selected object)} move the plane the object is attached to onto the object and make it the active plane → {plane, offset}

commands.label: Edit Text
commands.params: {id? (default: the selected type)} Object › Perspective › Edit Text: show type in perspective flat where it is drawn, in isolation mode, to edit it (text.* commands, the Type tool); exiting isolation (object.exitIsolation, Esc) projects it again; refused while an opacity mask is edited → {id}

commands.label: Invert
commands.params: {stroke?: bool (default: the active proxy), ids?|id?, item?: appearance item index|null, target?: "object"|"contents"} invert the active proxy's colours of the selection (or ids; groups recolour their contents) keeping each colour's model, as edit.colors.invert does; the Appearance panel's active fill/stroke item (appearance.setActiveItem) is inverted instead when it is of that kind and no ids are given; with nothing selected, invert the default → {changed}

commands.label: Complement
commands.params: {stroke?: bool (default: the active proxy), ids?|id?, item?: appearance item index|null, target?: "object"|"contents"} replace the active proxy's colours by their complements ((highest + lowest) − each component, over RGB or CMY; grey unchanged) keeping each colour's model; honours the Appearance panel's active item as paint.invert does; with nothing selected, the default → {changed}

commands.label: Apply Last Color
commands.params: {stroke?: bool (default: the active proxy), ids?|id?, item?: appearance item index|null, target?: "object"|"contents"} apply the last solid colour used (paint.recent lastColor) to the active proxy of the selection and the default → {objects} (as paint.setFill)

commands.label: Apply Last Gradient
commands.params: {stroke?: bool (default: the active proxy), ids?|id?, item?: appearance item index|null, target?: "object"|"contents"} apply the last gradient used (paint.recent lastGradient), fitted to each object, to the active proxy of the selection and the default → {objects} (as paint.setFill)

commands.label: Recent Colors
commands.params: {} → {colors: [{hex, color}] newest first, at most 30, each once, kept across documents for the session (fed by every paint command and the eyedropper), lastColor: {hex, color}, lastGradient: gradient paint}

commands.label: Fill and Stroke
commands.params: {} → {fill, stroke: the paints the Fill/Stroke proxies show (the Appearance panel's active item for the proxy of its kind, else the first selected object's, a group's first painted object's, type: its first run's; else the defaults for new art), fillActive, fillMixed, strokeMixed: the selected objects' (or a selected group's contents') fills (strokes) differ, shown as a "?" proxy}

commands.label: Overprint
commands.params: {fill?: bool, stroke?: bool, item?: appearance item index|null, ids?|id?, target?: "object"|"contents"} make fills and/or strokes overprint (Overprint Preview, Separations Preview) or knock out: item's, else every fill or stroke of the painted objects (groups: their contents; type: its characters too). Without item and ids, the Appearance panel's active item stands in when it is of that kind → {changed: objects}

commands.label: Attributes
commands.params: {ids?|id?, item?, target?: "object"|"contents"} → {ids, overprintFill, overprintStroke, showCenter, imageMap: "none"|"rectangle"|"polygon", url, note, fillRule: "nonZero"|"evenOdd" (of the paths and compound paths in them), reversed (their subpaths run counter-clockwise on screen: Reverse Path Direction On), recentUrls: [newest first]} the Attributes panel's values for `ids` or the selection, overprint aimed as object.setOverprint aims; a value is null where they differ (or nothing has a fill, stroke or path)

commands.label: Swatch Libraries
commands.params: {} → {libraries: [{id, name, category: "builtIn"|"gradients"|"patterns"|"user" (User Defined: the library files in the user library folder, rescanned now)|"loaded" (swatch.library.load), count, path?}], userFolder} every library the library panel opens, in menu order

commands.label: Swatch Library
commands.params: {library: id or name} → {id, name, category, swatches: [{name, kind, group, global, spot, color?, hex?, gradient?, pattern?}] (as swatch.list), groups: [{name, swatches: [names]}]}

commands.label: Add to Swatches
commands.params: {library: id or name, names?: [swatch or colour group names in the library] (default: all of it; a group comes as a colour group, a single swatch ungrouped), apply?: "fill"|"stroke" (also apply the first one to the selection and the defaults, as paint.setFill / paint.setStroke), focus?: true (with apply: false keeps the active proxy)} copy library swatches into the document as one undo step. A swatch the document already has (same name and paint) isn't added again; a name taken by another swatch gets a number ("Clay 1 2"). A pattern swatch brings its pattern, as pasting art painted with it does: the same pattern the document has is used, and a name another pattern or swatch has gets a number → {library, added: [names in the document], existing: [names already there], applied?: name}

commands.label: Default Swatches
commands.params: {replace?: false} bring back the default swatches and colour groups of the document's colour mode that are missing (by name), as one undo step; replace: true makes the swatches exactly the defaults (art linked to a removed global swatch keeps its colour, unlinked) → {added: [names]}

commands.label: Save Swatch Library…
commands.params: {path?, format?: "vcswatches" (lossless JSON: colour models, global, spot, gradients, groups) | "gpl" (8-bit RGB palette; groups as `# Group:` comments) | "ase" (swatch exchange, binary: solid colors in their own model (RGB, CMYK, Lab, Gray) as global, spot or process colors, and color groups; gradients are left out, and a tint swatch is saved as the color it shows) | "css" (custom properties on :root) (default: the path's extension, else vcswatches), names?: [swatch or colour group names] (default: all; None and patterns are never saved), name?: library name (default: the document's), user?: false (save into the user library folder, listed under User Defined)} save the document's swatches as a library → {path, format, count: the swatches written (gpl and ase hold solid colors only, and css leaves freeform gradients out), library?: id when saved to the user folder}; without path or user → {data: the file's text, format, count}, or {dataBase64, format, count} for ase

commands.label: Other Library…
commands.params: {path? | data?: file text | dataBase64?, name?: file name (default: the path's)} load a .vcswatches, .gpl, .ase (swatch exchange) or .acb (color book, read only) library, or the swatches of any document VectorCraft opens (see document.formats), for the library panel (Window → Swatch Libraries lists it until the app quits; a file of the user library folder, or a file with the same extension and bytes as one there, opens as that User Defined library) → {library: id, name, count}

commands.label: Copy to User Defined
commands.params: {library: id or name of a loaded library (category "loaded", swatch.library.load)} copy it into the user library folder of the desktop app, whose libraries VectorCraft lists as User Defined every time it starts (a loaded library is listed until the app quits): a library file as it is, the swatches of a document or a library loaded from data as a .vcswatches file. A name the folder already has gets a number ("Brand 2.ase") and no file is replaced; when the folder already holds the same file, that file is used. The library is then listed as User Defined only, and until the app quits commands given its loaded id use the copy; a User Defined library comes back as it is → {library: its User Defined id, name, count, path, copied: false when nothing was written}

commands.label: Add Freeform Point
commands.params: {at: [x,y] (document coordinates), color? (default: the gradient's colour there; #rrggbbaa and #rgba are refused), keepModel?: bool (as paint.setFill), opacity?: 0..1 (or 0..100), spread?: 0..1 (or 0..100 %; the radius of pure colour around the point, a fraction of half the object's larger side; default 0), line?: true (join it to the selected point: extends the line ending there, else starts one), ids?|id?, stroke?: bool (default: the targeted item's kind, else the active proxy), item?: fill/stroke item index|null (omitted: the Appearance panel's active item when it is of the edited kind), target?: "object"|"contents"} add a point to the freeform gradient (an unplaced one keeps its automatic points first) and select it → {index}

commands.label: Edit Freeform Point
commands.params: {index? (default: the selected point), at?: [x,y] (document coordinates), color? (#rrggbbaa and #rgba are refused), keepModel?: bool (as paint.setFill), opacity?: 0..1 (or 0..100), spread?: 0..1 (or 0..100 %), ids?|id?, stroke?: bool (default: the targeted item's kind, else the active proxy), item?: fill/stroke item index|null (omitted: the Appearance panel's active item when it is of the edited kind), target?: "object"|"contents"} move or recolour a point of the freeform gradient → {index}

commands.label: Delete Freeform Point
commands.params: {index? (default: the selected point), ids?|id?, stroke?: bool (default: the targeted item's kind, else the active proxy), item?: fill/stroke item index|null (omitted: the Appearance panel's active item when it is of the edited kind), target?: "object"|"contents"} remove a point (never the last one); lines through it close up around it and lines left with one point go → {index}

commands.label: Add Freeform Line
commands.params: {points: [index, …] (at least two), ids?|id?, stroke?: bool (default: the targeted item's kind, else the active proxy), item?: fill/stroke item index|null (omitted: the Appearance panel's active item when it is of the edited kind), target?: "object"|"contents"} join points with a smooth line through them, in order → {line}

commands.label: Split Freeform Line
commands.params: {line: line index, segment: the segment from the line's point `segment` to the next, t?: 0..1 along it (default 0.5), ids?|id?, stroke?: bool (default: the targeted item's kind, else the active proxy), item?: fill/stroke item index|null (omitted: the Appearance panel's active item when it is of the edited kind), target?: "object"|"contents"} add a point on a line there (colour, opacity and spread between the segment's ends) and select it → {index}

commands.label: Select Freeform Point
commands.params: {index: point index | null to clear} select a point of the freeform gradient behind the active proxy (the first selected object's): the point the Gradient tool, the Gradient and Color panels and Delete act on → {index}

commands.label: Freeform Gradient
commands.params: {stroke?: bool (default: the active proxy)} the freeform gradient behind the proxy of the first selected object → {mode: points|lines, points: [{at: [x,y] (document coordinates), color, opacity, spread}], lines: [[index, …]], selected: index|null}

commands.label: Flatten Transparency…
commands.params: {preset?: "high"|"medium"|"low" or a saved preset's name (see flattener.presets.list; default medium), balance?: 0..100 (raster/vector balance; 0 rasterizes everything), lineArtPpi?: 1..2400, gradientPpi?: 1..2400 (areas only gradients and meshes reach), textToOutlines?, strokesToOutlines?, clipComplexRegions? (clip images to the region outlines, else rectangles), antiAlias?, preserveAlpha? (composite over nothing instead of white), preserveOverprints? (areas showing one paint keep its colour and overprint; false clears overprints), options?: {the same keys}, ids?|id?} overlapping transparent objects become one group of flat-colour regions (CMYK colours composited ink by ink in CMYK documents), plus an image where gradients, patterns, images, masks or raster effects reach; objects without transparency stay; a frame of threaded text that is outlined or flattened leaves its thread with the text it shows → {ids, rasterized: images made, vector: regions made, options, warning? (an image in the art couldn't be decoded, as object.rasterize says)}

commands.label: Transparency Flattener Presets
commands.params: {} → {presets: [{name, builtIn, options}]} the built-in presets (High, Medium and Low Resolution), then the saved ones; any of these names works as `preset` wherever flattener options are taken

commands.label: Save Transparency Flattener Preset
commands.params: {name?: (default: a new "Flattener Preset N"), newName?: rename it, preset?: the preset to start from (default: the saved preset `name`, else medium), …options (the keys of object.flattenTransparency, at the top level or in `options`)} create or change a saved preset (built-in ones can't change) → {name, options, created}

commands.label: Delete Transparency Flattener Preset
commands.params: {name} delete a saved preset (built-in ones stay) → {deleted: name}

commands.label: Import Transparency Flattener Presets
commands.params: {path? | data?: file text | dataBase64?, replace?: false (replace saved presets of the same names; else the imported ones get a number)} add the presets of a .vcflattener file (as flattener.presets.export writes) to the saved ones → {imported: [names]}

commands.label: Export Transparency Flattener Presets

commands.label: Flattener Preview

commands.label: Graphic Style Libraries
commands.params: {} → {libraries: [{id, name, category: "builtIn"|"user" (User Defined: the .vcstyles files in the user library folder, rescanned now)|"loaded" (graphicStyle.loadLibrary), count, path?}], userFolder} every graphic style library the library panel opens, in menu order

commands.label: Graphic Style Library
commands.params: {library: id or name} → {id, name, category, styles: [{name, fill, stroke, strokeWidth, fills, strokes, effects: [effect id…], opacity, blend, isolate, knockout}] (as graphicStyle.list)}

commands.label: Add to Graphic Styles
commands.params: {library: id or name, name? | names?: [style names in the library] (default: all of it), apply?: false (also apply the first one to `ids` or the selection, if any, as graphicStyle.apply), add?: false (with apply: add its appearance on top, as Alt-click), ids?} copy library styles into the document's Graphic Styles as one undo step (with the apply). A style the document already has (same name and look) isn't added again; a name taken by another style gets a number ("Halo 2"). The patterns they paint with come along (a name taken by another pattern or swatch gets a number) → {library, added: [names in the document], existing: [names already there], applied?: name}

commands.label: Save Graphic Style Library…
commands.params: {path?, names?: [style names] (default: all), name?: library name (default: the document's), user?: false (save into the user library folder, listed under User Defined)} save the document's graphic styles as a .vcstyles library (JSON: the styles, unlinked from swatches, and the patterns they paint with) → {path, count, library?: id when saved to the user folder}; without path or user → {data: the file's text, count}

commands.label: Other Library…
commands.params: {path? | data?: file text | dataBase64?, name?: file name (default: the path's)} load a .vcstyles library, or the graphic styles of any document VectorCraft opens (see document.formats), for the library panel (Window → Graphic Style Libraries lists it until the app quits; a file of the user library folder, or a file with the same extension and bytes as one there, opens as that User Defined library) → {library: id, name, count}

commands.label: Symbol Libraries

(as edit.paste)} copy library symbols into the document's Symbols as one undo step (with the place), with their Symbol Options and the resources they use (the symbols they nest, patterns, swatches, brushes, graphic styles, images). commands.label: Save Symbol Library…
commands.params: {path?, names?: [symbol names] (default: all), name?: library name (default: the document's), user?: false (save into the user library folder, listed under User Defined)} save the document's symbols, with their Symbol Options and the resources they use, as a symbol library: a .vectorcraft document holding only them → {path, count, library?: id when saved to the user folder}; without path or user → {dataBase64: the file's bytes, count}

commands.label: Other Library…
commands.params: {path? | data?: file text | dataBase64?, name?: file name (default: the path's)} load the symbols of any document VectorCraft opens (see document.formats), a saved symbol library included, for the library panel (Window → Symbol Libraries lists it until the app quits; a file of the user library folder, or a file with the same bytes as one there, opens as that User Defined library) → {library: id, name, count}

commands.label: Brush Libraries
commands.params: {} → {libraries: [{id, name, category: "builtIn"|"user" (User Defined: the .vectorcraft files in the user library folder, rescanned now)|"loaded" (brush.loadLibrary), count, path?}], userFolder} every brush library the library panel opens, in menu order

commands.params: {library: id or name} → {id, name, category, brushes: [{name, type}] (as brush.list)}

commands.label: Add to Brushes
commands.params: {library: id or name, name? | names?: [brush names in the library] (default: all of it), apply?: false (also apply the first one to paths, as brush.apply does), ids?|id? (the paths apply takes; default the selected ones), swatchConflict? (as edit.paste)} copy library brushes into the document's Brushes as one undo step (with the apply; named Apply Brush when no brush is added and it only applies one), with the resources their art uses (patterns, symbols, swatches, graphic styles, images). A brush the document already has (same name and definition) isn't added again; a name another brush has gets a number ("Ribbon 2"). The first one becomes the current brush → {library, names: [each brush's name in the document], added: [names added], existing: [names already there], applied: [ids of the paths it was applied to]}

commands.label: Save Brush Library…
commands.params: {path?, names?: [brush names] (default: all), name?: library name (default: the document's), user?: false (save into the user library folder, listed under User Defined)} save the document's brushes, with the resources their art uses, as a brush library: a .vectorcraft document holding only them → {path, count, library?: id when saved to the user folder}; without path or user → {dataBase64: the file's bytes, count}

commands.label: Other Library…
commands.params: {path? | data?: file text | dataBase64?, name?: file name (default: the path's)} load the brushes of any document VectorCraft opens (see document.formats; one without brushes of its own has the default ones), a saved brush library included, for the library panel (Window → Brush Libraries lists it until the app quits; a file of the user library folder, or a file with the same bytes as one there, opens as that User Defined library) → {library: id, name, count}

commands.label: Libraries
commands.params: {} → {libraries: [{id, name, graphics, colors, gradients, patterns, charStyles, paraStyles, groups} (counts)], current: the current library's id or null, folder: the library folder, or null when libraries last for the session only (the web, headless)}

commands.label: Library
commands.params: {library?: id or name (default: the current library)} → {id, name, graphics: [{id, name, width, height, thumbnail: PNG base64}], colors: [{name, hex, color, spot: ink name or null, tint: 0..1}], gradients: [{name, gradient: {gradient: {kind, stops}, angle}}], patterns: [{name, pattern: its name in the item, thumbnail: PNG base64}], charStyles: [{name, attrs}], paraStyles: [{name, attrs}], groups: [{name, items: [{kind: color|gradient|pattern|charStyle|paraStyle|graphic, item: name (graphic: id)}]}] (an item is in one group at most; the others are ungrouped)}

commands.label: Show Library
commands.params: {library: id or name} the library the Libraries panel shows, which library commands without a `library` act on → {id}

commands.label: Create New Library
commands.params: {name?: "My Library"} a new empty library (its file in the library folder), made the current one → {id, name}

commands.label: Rename Library
commands.params: {library?, name} rename a library (default: the current one) → {id, name}

commands.label: Delete Library
commands.params: {library?} delete a library (default: the current one) and its file; not undoable → null

commands.label: Add to Library
commands.params: {library?: id or name (default: the current library, made when there is none), kind: graphic|fillColor|strokeColor|fillGradient|strokeGradient|fillPattern|strokePattern|charStyle|paraStyle, ids?: objects (default: the selection), name?, color?: colour (a colour to add, instead of the selection's; #rrggbbaa and #rgba are refused), swatch?: a gradient or pattern swatch of the document (fillGradient…strokePattern: added instead of the selection's paint; with `color`, the spot swatch it is, kept as a spot colour), tint?: 0..100 (with `color` and a spot `swatch`: its %), group?: name, before?: item | after?: item (an item of the same kind)} add an item from the selection: graphic: a copy of the objects with every resource they use; fillColor/strokeColor: the first selected object's solid fill/stroke colour (else the default fill/stroke), a colour linked to a spot swatch kept as a spot colour (the swatch's name, its colour and the tint); fillGradient/strokeGradient: the first selected object's fill/stroke gradient (else the default's), without its placement or swatch links, named after its swatch, else "Gradient"; fillPattern/strokePattern: the first selected object's fill/stroke pattern (else the default's) with the resources its art uses, named after it; charStyle/paraStyle: the selected text's character/paragraph attributes (the Type tool's range, else the first selected text object). A new item goes into `group` (default: none) and, with `before` or `after`, just before or after that item in the order its kind is shown in, as dropping it among the Libraries panel's items does; an item the library already has (same kind and contents) isn't added again, nor moved → {library, kind, name, id?: graphic id, existing: bool, group?: name or null (a new item's)}

commands.label: Use Library Item
commands.params: {library?, kind, item: name (graphic: id or name), center?: [x, y] (graphic; default: the first artboard's centre), to?: fill|stroke (colors, gradients, patterns; default: the kind's), recorded?: the item as it was when used (recorded in the journal so a replay matches)} graphic: place a copy centred on `center`, its resources pasted along, selected, one undo step; colors and gradients: paint the selection (and the defaults) as paint.setFill/paint.setStroke, a gradient fitting each object; a spot color links to the document's spot swatch of its ink's name, added when the document has none of that colour (a name taken by another colour gets a number), one undo step; patterns: add the pattern and its swatch to the document (a name the document gives another pattern gets a number; the same pattern is reused) and paint the selection (and the defaults) with it, one undo step; charStyle/paraStyle: add the style to the document (a name taken by different attributes gets a number) and apply it to the selected text, one undo step → {kind, ids?, style?}

commands.label: Delete Library Item
commands.params: {library?, kind, item: name (graphic: id or name)} delete an item (out of its group too) → null

commands.label: New Library Group
commands.params: {library?, name?: "Group" (a name the library's groups have, ignoring case, gets a number), items?: [{kind, item}] (moved into it out of their groups)} a new group of items, after the others → {library, group: its name}

commands.label: Rename Library Group
commands.params: {library?, group: name, name} rename a group (another group's name, ignoring case, is an error) → {library, group: the new name}

commands.label: Delete Library Group
commands.params: {library?, group: name} delete a group: its items stay in the library, ungrouped → {library, ungrouped: how many}

commands.label: Move Library Item to Group
commands.params: {library?, kind, item: name (graphic: id or name), group?: name (null or none: out of its group), before?: item | after?: item (an item of the same kind, named as `item` is)} put an item in a group (out of the one it was in); with `before` or `after`, also move it just before or after that item in the order its kind is shown in, as dragging it in the Libraries panel does → {library, kind, item, group: name or null}

commands.label: Move Library Group
commands.params: {library?, group: name, to: index} move a group to position `to` of the library's groups (0 = first; past the end: last), as dragging its header in the Libraries panel does → {library, group, to: where it went}

commands.label: Export Library
commands.params: {library?: id or name (default: the current library), path?} write a library (its colours, gradients, patterns, styles, graphics with their art and thumbnails, and groups) as a .vclibrary file (JSON, as libraries are kept) → {path, name}; without path → {data: the file's text, name}

commands.label: Import Library
commands.params: {path? | data?: file text | dataBase64?, name?: the library's name (default: the file's)} add the library of a .vclibrary file (as library.export writes) as a new library, made the current one; a name another library has gets a number (`Brand (2)`) → {id, name, graphics, colors, gradients, patterns, charStyles, paraStyles, groups (counts)}

commands.label: Expand…
commands.params: {object?: true (symbol instances without effects (their fills' and strokes' included) and not in perspective → their art, as Break Link to Symbol places it (the instances that art holds stay instances), type → outlines, live shapes → paths, effects baked, blends → groups of their steps, repeats → groups of their instances, Intertwine groups → groups of their objects and of the parts drawn over the others (clip groups), envelopes → their distorted content, placed documents → editable copies of their art, as placing the file without link gives, its symbols, patterns, swatches and images joining the document), fill?: true (gradient fills → `gradient` art, pattern fills → their tiles in a clip group shaped like the object), stroke?: true (strokes → filled outlines, the stroked paths that baking effects leaves included), gradient?: "objects" (default: `steps` solid strips, concentric ellipses for radial gradients) | "mesh" (a gradient mesh); both in a clip group shaped like the object (freeform gradients always become a mesh shaped like it), steps?: 1..1000 (255)} one undo step; a dimension whose art an option changes, or one selected with the art it measures when that art is replaced, becomes a plain group of its art → {ids}

commands.label: Expand Options
commands.params: {} what each Expand option would change in the selection → {object, fill, stroke, gradient, appearance, symbolArt?: {fill, stroke, gradient}} (true: something to expand; gradient: a gradient fill that Fill expands, which Expand Gradient To applies to; appearance: appearance attributes Expand Appearance expands first, for which Object › Expand… is dimmed in the menus; symbolArt, when the selection holds symbol instances that Object expands: true when only their art holds it, which Fill and Stroke reach only with Object on)

commands.label: Attributes
commands.params: {overprintFill?: bool, overprintStroke?: bool (aimed as object.setOverprint's fill and stroke, item? too), showCenter?: bool (the canvas shows the selected object's centre point), imageMap?: "none"|"rectangle"|"polygon", url?: string ("" removes it; SVG, PDF and .ai export link the object), note?: string, ids?|id?, item?: appearance item index|null, target?: "object"|"contents"} set the Attributes panel's values on ids or the selection, as one undo step; a URL given joins the recent URLs (attributes.info) → {changed: objects}

commands.label: Fill Rule
commands.params: {rule: "nonZero"|"evenOdd", ids?|id?} the fill rule of the paths and compound paths in ids or the selection (groups: those inside), as one undo step → {changed}

commands.label: SVG Interactivity
commands.params: {ids?|id?} → {ids, events: [{event, script}…] in the panel's order | null (the objects' events differ), files: [the linked JavaScript files…], eventNames: [the events the panel lists…]} the SVG Interactivity panel's values for ids or the selection

commands.label: Add Event
commands.params: {event: "onclick"|"onmouseover"|… (svgInteractivity.info's eventNames), script: string (the JavaScript; "" removes the event), ids?|id?} set the JavaScript an event runs on ids or the selection, replacing the event's script where it has one, as one undo step; SVG export writes it as the event attribute → {changed: objects}

commands.label: Remove Selected Entry
commands.params: {event, ids?|id?} remove an event and its JavaScript from ids or the selection, as one undo step → {changed: objects}

commands.label: Clear Events
commands.params: {ids?|id?} remove every event from ids or the selection, as one undo step → {changed: objects}

commands.label: Add JavaScript File
commands.params: {file: path or URL (written as given, without surrounding spaces)} link a JavaScript file to the document, after the others: SVG export writes a <script xlink:href> for each linked file. A file already linked stays where it is; a document links at most 64 files → {files}

commands.label: Remove JavaScript File
commands.params: {file} unlink a JavaScript file from the document → {files}

commands.label: New Art Has Basic Appearance
commands.params: {on?: bool (omitted: toggle)} the Appearance panel option (the preference newArtBasic, on by default): on, new art takes one fill and stroke (with the Stroke panel's options); off, the whole appearance of the last selected object (every fill, stroke and effect, opacity and blend mode) → {on}
