commands.label: New Art Appearance
commands.params: {} what the next object drawn gets → {basic: New Art Has Basic Appearance, appearance: {items, effects} (the model's JSON; placed gradients relative to the unit box), opacity: 0..100, blend, graphicStyle: the style it is linked to or null, inherited: taken from the last selection}

commands.label: Color Themes
commands.params: {} the saved colour themes, in order → {themes: [{name, colors: ["#rrggbb"], keys: [colour keys, exact in each colour's model], rule?}]}

commands.label: Save Theme
commands.params: {colors: [1–5 colours] (#rrggbbaa and #rgba are refused) | color + rule (a harmony rule id or label, see color.harmony: its 5-colour theme from that base colour, base first), rule?: the rule it was made with, name?: (default "Theme N"), replace?: a saved theme's name (overwrite that theme in place, e.g. after editing it; it may be renamed), color?: one colour (as colors: [colour])} save a colour theme to the local theme library (the preferences) → {name, count: themes saved}

commands.label: Delete Theme
commands.params: {name} delete a saved colour theme → {deleted}

commands.label: Add to Swatches
commands.params: {name} add a saved theme's colours to the Swatches panel as a colour group named after it (as swatch.newGroup), as one undo step → {name: the group's, swatches: [names]}

commands.label: Export PDF
commands.params: {path?, preset?: "VectorCraft Default" (built-in or saved: pdf.preset.list), artboard? | artboards?: [i…] | range?: "1-3, 5" (1-based; default all, one page each), standard?: none|pdfA2b|pdfX1a (CMYK, grey and spot colours only: colours and images converted to output.destination or the CMYK output intent, untagged; transparency flattened with flattenerPreset; PDF 1.3)|pdfX3 (colours ICC-tagged; transparency flattened; PDF 1.3)|pdfX4 (transparency and layers kept; colours ICC-tagged; PDF 1.6 at most) (PDF/X: a /GTS_PDFX output intent, by default the CMYK profile in effect, embedded; TrimBox, Trapped, GTS_PDFXVersion, title and dates; fonts embedded or outlined), compatibility?: 1.3 (no transparency: it is flattened with flattenerPreset; images keep no see-through pixels)|1.4|1.5|1.6|1.7 (default)|2.0 (choosing a standard sets its version: 1.7 for pdfA2b, 1.6 for pdfX4, 1.3 for pdfX1a and pdfX3, which write 1.4 as 1.3 too; pdfA2b refuses 1.3), preserveEditing? (on in VectorCraft Default: the native document as an embedded file, which document.open restores; choosing a standard turns it off, a standard refuses it), thumbnails? (each page drawn as a /Thumb image, 106 px on its long side), fastWebView? (a linearised file: the first page shows while the rest downloads; it stays linearised when encrypted), viewAfterSaving? (the app opens the written file), createLayers? (each layer and sublayer but template layers as a PDF layer, an optional content group listed under its layer's: hidden layers off, non-printing ones /PrintState /OFF, locked ones locked; needs 1.5 or later; they reopen as layers; choosing pdfX1a or pdfX3 turns it off; they refuse it), includeNonPrinting? (keep layers whose Print option is off; left out by default unless createLayers), flattenerPreset?: "" (High Resolution) | high | medium | low | a saved preset (flattener.presets.list): what PDF 1.3 files flatten transparency with, flattener?: {object.flattenTransparency options over it}, compression?: {color?, gray?: {downsample: none|average|subsample|bicubic, ppi: 300, abovePpi: 450, compression: none|zip|jpeg|jpeg2000|auto, quality: minimum|low|medium|high|maximum}, mono?: {downsample, ppi: 1200, abovePpi: 1800, compression: none|ccittG3|ccittG4|zip|runLength} (black-and-white images), compressText?: true} (images above abovePpi are resampled to ppi; auto keeps JPEGs JPEG, the others lossless; JPEG needs opaque images; none, jpeg2000, CCITT and runLength are written as ZIP with a warning), marks?: {trim, registration, colorBars, pageInfo, kind: roman|japanese, weight: 0.25 (trim marks and targets), offset: 6 (pt from the artboard, at least the bleed)} (printer's marks in [Registration], every plate: trim marks, registration targets mid-side, CMYK/spot/black-tint colour bars on top, page information (title, artboard, date UTC) below), bleed?: {useDocument (the document's bleed, document.setup), top, bottom, left, right} (pt; art in the bleed is kept; a PDF/X file with no bleed on a side where the document's bleed has one comes back with a warning). Each page: TrimBox = artboard, BleedBox = artboard + bleed, MediaBox = that + the marks' room (art clipped to the BleedBox), output?: {conversion: none (default)|destination (every colour into the destination profile's model, CMYK or RGB, also colours of that model in another profile)|preserveNumbers (only colours of the other model and Lab; those in the destination's model keep their numbers) (grey stays grey; images are converted too, printer's marks are not), destination: profile name (edit.colorSettings lists them; default: the document's profile for its colour mode), profiles: none (device colours)|all|destination|taggedSource (documents assigned a profile: edit.assignProfile) (ICC-based colours: CMYK with the destination or document CMYK profile, RGB as sRGB, grey with the sRGB tone curve; PDF/A, pdfX3 and pdfX4 always, whatever profiles says), outputIntent: profile name (embedded as the catalog's /GTS_PDFX output intent; a name that isn't a profile is only named, which pdfX1a and pdfX3 allow only with a registry and pdfX4 refuses; pdfX1a needs a CMYK one), outputCondition, outputConditionId (default: outputIntent), registry, trapped (/Trapped /True; /False when an output intent is written)} (PDF/A files keep their own output intent), advanced?: {fontSubsetPercent: 100 (below 100 is accepted with a warning: fonts are always embedded as subsets), outlineText: false (type as real, selectable and searchable text in embedded subset fonts with a ToUnicode map; fonts whose licence forbids embedding, or allows only whole fonts, stay outlines with a warning; true: every glyph as an outline), overprint: preserve (overprinting fills and strokes set /OP /op true, /OPM 1; white ones knock out with document.setup discardWhiteOverprint)|discard (they knock out)}, security?: {openPassword, permissionsPassword, printing: none|low|high, changes: none|pages|forms|comments|any, copy, screenReader, plaintextMetadata}, acknowledgeLoss?: bool (write over the file the document was read from although reading it left things out), format?: "pdf"} → {path, bytes, warnings}; no path → {dataBase64, bytes, warnings}. The options apply over the preset (null keeps its value); options accepted but not applied yet come back as warnings; a standard with a PDF version it doesn't allow and a password with a standard are refused, and so is a PDF/X file that would still break its standard (transparency the flattener left, RGB in pdfX1a, a font not embedded) or a PDF 1.3 file with transparency left. document.export {format: pdf} takes the same options

commands.label: PDF Settings
commands.params: {preset?, includeDocument?: false, …options of document.exportPdf} → {settings (the preset with the options applied), presets: [name…], changed: [{option: "compression.compressText", value}] (what differs from the preset), warnings}; includeDocument also exports the active document in memory and adds its warnings (knockout groups approximated, effects left out…)

commands.label: Document Setup
commands.params: {units?: "Points"|"Inches"|"Millimeters"|…, bleed?: pt (all sides)|[top, bottom, left, right]|{top?, bottom?, left?, right?} (0–72 pt), outlineImages?: bool (show images in Outline mode), highlightSubstitutedGlyphs?: bool (Highlight Substituted Fonts is a preference: prefs.set highlightSubstitutedFonts; a highlightSubstitutedFonts key is ignored and the reply carries a warning),gridSize?: "small"|"medium"|"large", gridColors?: "Light"|"Medium"|"Dark"|"Red"|"Orange"|"Green"|"Blue"|"Purple"|[colour, colour] (transparency grid; the first is also the paper colour; #rrggbbaa and #rgba are refused), simulatePaper?: bool, flattenerPreset?: "High Resolution"|"Medium Resolution"|"Low Resolution"|a saved preset (flattener.presets.list), discardWhiteOverprint?: bool, language?: "English: USA"|"German"|"French"|… (also picks its quotes), quotes?: {double?: "“”", single?: "‘’"} (beside a language: only if they differ from the current ones), typographersQuotes?: bool (typed straight quotes become the document's quotes), superscript?: {size?: %, position?: %}, subscript?: {size?: %, position?: %}, smallCapsSize?: %, exportText?: "editable"|"appearance" (SVG text as text or as outlines), backgroundContents?: "transparent"|"white" (white: raster exports are white behind the art), …the keys of its own reply (it can be passed back; the values it only reports are ignored)} change the document setup in one undo step; no params → the current setup

commands.label: New Document Presets
commands.params: {category?: "Recent"|"Saved"|"Mobile"|"Web"|"Print"|"Film & Video"|"Art & Illustration"|"Branding"|"Social"} the New Document presets by category (Recent: the last sizes used; Saved: the user's presets) → {categories: [{name, presets: [{name, size: "1920 × 1080 px", width: pt, height: pt, units, orientation, artboards, artboardLayout: {layout, columns, spacing, rightToLeft}, bleed, backgroundContents, colorMode, rasterEffectsPpi, previewMode}]}]}; file.new {preset: name} starts from one

commands.label: Save Preset
commands.params: {name, preset?: start from this preset, …settings as file.new (default: Letter in prefs unitsGeneral)} save New Document settings as a user preset (the Saved category; same name = replace) in the preferences → {name, count}

commands.label: Delete Preset
commands.params: {name} delete a saved New Document preset → {deleted}

commands.label: Place…
commands.params: {path | name | dataBase64 (a file's path, or its name with its bytes), link?: true (a raster image keeps its file's path; a VectorCraft document at path becomes one locked placed document showing artboard `page`, linked to the file and read again when it changes (links.update; saving it in this app updates it at once), drawn as vectors in every output; so does a PDF/.ai page at path, showing its `crop` box, unless password or textAs: "outlines" is given; false: an editable copy of its art, as from dataBase64; other files are embedded), text?: {characterSet?: "unicode" (UTF-8, or UTF-16 with a byte-order mark; other bytes as the platform's 8-bit set) | "ansi" (the platform's 8-bit set), platform?: "windows" (Windows-1252) | "mac" (Mac Roman), removeLineReturns?: false (each block of lines becomes one paragraph; blank lines end paragraphs), removeParagraphReturns?: false (drop blank lines), replaceSpaces?: n (runs of n ≥ 2 spaces become a tab)} (a .txt file, placed as area type filling rect, the replaced object's bounds, or else the artboard less a 36 pt margin), template?: false (onto a new locked template layer below the current layer), replace?: false (swap the one selected object, keeping its stacking place and transform; no at/rect), at?: [x, y] centre (default: the first artboard's centre), rect?: [x, y, width, height] fit inside; aspect kept (wins over at), page?: 1 (PDF/.ai page, or a native document's artboard), crop?: "crop" (clipped to that page or artboard, default; an SVG, only when given: framed and clipped by its viewBox, else by its art's bounds) | "bounding" (the bounds of the art that shows, with its strokes and effects, as an export measures them: hidden objects and guides left out) | "art" | "trim" | "bleed" | "media" (a PDF page's boxes), password? (an encrypted PDF), dxf?: {…the DXF options of document.open} (a .dxf drawing: fit fills the artboard under at, else the first; fitted or uncentred art lands with its drawing's artboard on that artboard, else it is centred on at)} → {ids, name, format, linked, width, height, warnings}. Raster images come in at 100% of their physical size (the file's ppi, else 72); SVG, DXF, PDF/.ai, EMF/WMF (clipped to the picture's frame), EPS (clipped to its bounding box; as document.open reads it), a .ai saved without PDF compatibility (from its editing data, as document.open reads it: the art of the layers that show on artboard `page`, clipped to that artboard unless crop is "bounding") and native documents as one group, with the images, symbols, patterns, swatches and brushes they use. One undo step; selects what it placed (unless on a template layer); never touches the clipboard. A PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP image whose pixels can't be read (a file cut short) is an error, and nothing is placed

commands.label: Placed File Info
commands.params: {path | name | dataBase64 (a file's path, or its name with its bytes), page?, crop?, password?, thumbnail?: px, link?: bool, dxf?: {…} (both as file.place)} what file.place would place, without placing it → {name, format, width, height (pt at 100%), pixelWidth?, pixelHeight?, ppi?: [x, y], colorMode?: RGB|Grayscale|CMYK (raster images), warnings, thumbnailBase64?: PNG of at most `thumbnail` (≤ 512) px on its longer side}

commands.label: Image Info
commands.params: {id?} an image object (default: the one selected) → {id, name, linked, link, colorMode: RGB|Grayscale|CMYK, pixelWidth, pixelHeight, ppi: [x, y] at its placed size, width, height}

commands.label: Load Place Cursor
commands.params: {paths?: [path…], files?: [{name, dataBase64}…], link?, template?, page?, crop?, text?, dxf?, thumbnail?: px} load the place cursor (the `place` tool) with up to 100 files (as file.place reads them): a click places the current file at 100% with its top-left corner there, a drag places it at the dragged size (aspect kept), ←/→ and ↑/↓ cycle the files, Esc discards the current one; each placement is a file.place, and the previous tool returns after the last → {count, files: [{name, format, width, height, thumbnailBase64?}], skipped: [{name, error}]}

commands.label: Check Links
commands.params: {ids?: [image or placed document ids] (default: every linked image and placed document)} where each linked file is and whether it changed since it was read → {links: [{name, path, status: ok|modified|missing, ids, found?: path (found away from its path: relative to the document, or by name in its folder), preview: true (showing the low-resolution preview, not the file), refused?: why the path is not followed (another computer, a device or a URL: it counts as missing)}], missing, modified}

commands.label: Update Links
commands.params: {ids?: [image or placed document ids] (default: the linked images whose file was modified or is showing its preview, and placed documents whose file was modified)} read their linked files again; each keeps its bounds. The images and placed documents inside symbols, graph designs, patterns and opacity masks that show the same content are read again too (by default also those only that art shows); they have no ids to list. One undo step → {updated: [ids], missing: [ids]}

commands.label: Update Changed Links
commands.params: {} read again the active document's linked files that changed on disk since they were last seen (size or modification time), whatever Preferences → File Handling → Update Links says; the desktop app looks every two seconds and follows that preference. Files seen for the first time are only remembered. One undo step → {updated: [ids], ask: [], modified: []}

commands.label: Relink
commands.params: {ids?: [image or placed document ids] (default: the selected ones; with folder and nothing selected, every missing link), path | folder, scope?: selected (default: ids) | all (ids and every other object in the layers linked to the same file as one of them) | missingInFolder (with path: ids, then every other missing link whose file name is in path's folder, each to the file of its name there; names not there are in notFound; with copy, only images are looked for) | each (with paths), paths?: [{ids, path}] (with scope each, in place of ids, path and folder: each link to its own file; an id in two entries is an error), copy?: false (with path or paths, for images of a saved document: copy the file into the document's folder and link to the copy; the names Name.png, Name 2.png … Name 99.png are tried in turn until one is free, which gets the copy, or is a file with the same contents, which is used), preserve?: transforms|bounds|fileDimensions|fit|fill (how the new file takes each image's place this time, as links.placementOptions describes; default: each image's Placement Options; fit keeps the new file's aspect ratio inside the old bounds: Replace)} link images (or placed documents, each showing the same artboard or page of the new file) to the file at path, or each to the file of its link's name in folder; embedded images become linked; each keeps its bounds. One undo step → {relinked: [ids], notFound: [file names], copied?: [{from, to}], kept?: [{from, to}] (with copy)}

commands.label: Links
commands.params: {show?: all (default)|missing|modified|embedded, sort?: name|kind (file format)|status (missing, modified, ok, embedded); default: stacking order; top first} every image object and placed document in the layers, as the Links panel lists them → {links: [{id, name, linked, status: ok|modified|missing|embedded, format, pixelWidth, pixelHeight, path?, found?: path (found away from its path), page?, preview?: true (showing the saved preview), note?: said of an image past the decode allowance (shown at reduced size, or too large to draw), document?: true (a placed document: pageWidth and pageHeight in pt instead of pixels)}], missing, modified, embedded}

commands.label: Go To Link
commands.params: {id?} select image or placed document `id` (default: the first selected one); the Links panel scrolls it into view → {id, bounds: [x0, y0, x1, y1]}

commands.label: Embed Image
commands.params: {ids?: [image or placed document ids] (default: the selected linked ones)} break the links (the Links panel's Break Link): images keep the linked files' pixels in the document; a placed document becomes an editable copy of its art, as placing its file without link gives (its symbols, patterns, swatches and images joining the document). An image whose file can't be found and that shows the saved preview, or a placed document whose file can't be read or changed, stays linked: relink or update it first. One undo step → {embedded: [ids], missing: [ids]}

commands.label: Unembed
commands.params: {id?: an embedded image (default: the one selected), path?} write the image's pixels to the file at path (PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP as stored, other images as PNG; a path ending in .png/.jpg/.jpeg/.gif/.webp/.tif/.tiff/.bmp converts them) and link the image to it, keeping its bounds. One undo step → {id, path}; no path → {name, dataBase64} (nothing changes: there is no file to link to)

commands.label: Link Info
commands.params: {id?} an image's or placed document's Link Info (default: the one selected) → image.info's fields (id, name, linked, link, colorMode, pixelWidth, pixelHeight, width, height) and status: ok|modified|missing|embedded, format, ppi: [x, y] (the file's), effectivePpi: [x, y] (at its placed size), scale: [x%, y%] (of its 100% size), rotation (degrees, counter-clockwise), placement: {preserve, align, clip}; linked images also fileName, location (its folder), page?, fileSize? (bytes), modified?, created? (ms since the Unix epoch), refused? (why the path is not followed); a placed document has document: true, pageWidth and pageHeight (pt) instead of pixels, ppi and colorMode, and its scale is of its artboard's or page's 100% size

commands.label: Placement Options
commands.params: {ids?: [image or placed document ids] (default: the selected ones), preserve?: transforms|bounds (default)|fileDimensions|fit|fill, align?: topLeft|top|topRight|left|center (default)|right|bottomLeft|bottom|bottomRight (where the new art sits; not for bounds), clip?: false (clip it to the old bounds where it is larger)} how a file read again (links.relink, links.update) takes each image's place: transforms keeps its scale (relative to each file's 100% size), rotation and position; bounds stretches it into the old bounds; fileDimensions puts it at 100%, unrotated; fit and fill scale it proportionally to fit inside or cover the old bounds. Without options → {placement} of the first image; else one undo step → {ids, placement}

commands.label: Find Linked Files
commands.params: {folder?: an absolute path, ids?: [image or placed document ids] (default: the active document's missing links), maxSeconds?: 60 (1 to 600), stop?: false (true: stop the last search)} with folder: look in it and its subfolders, on separate threads, for files with the names of the linked files (in any letter case), and answer at once with the search's state (searching while it runs); without folder: the last search's state, with the files found so far. Each linked file's files come best first: same (the size and hash saved with the link), size (the saved size, where there is no saved hash or the file is larger than 1 GiB), then name. Within each kind, a file whose name has the link's letter case comes first. Then each file's folder names are compared with the saved path's, from the innermost outward up to the first one that differs, and a file with more matching names comes first; files that still tie are listed by path. Before the comparison, the saved path's parent-folder steps (.., or the empty components of a classic Mac :: run) are resolved, and . components in a slash path are skipped. A search looks for at most 1000 linked files and keeps the first 10 files of each one's name, and up to 10 that are the same file; it ends once every linked file has its same file, and searches only the folders text.findFontFiles may search, with the same maxSeconds, depth and count limits; none on the web → {id (absent while idle), state: idle|searching|done|stopped|failed, folder?, links: [{name, path, ids, files: [{path, size, match: same|size|name, caseDiffers?: true}]}], searched?: {folders, files, read}, skipped?, unreadable?, stopped?: stop|time|limit, error?, seconds?}

commands.label: PDF Presets
commands.params: {} → {presets: [{name, builtIn, supported (the writer produces its standard), description, settings (as document.pdfSettings)}]} the built-in presets (VectorCraft Default first), then the saved ones; any of these names works as `preset` wherever PDF options are taken

commands.label: Save PDF Preset
commands.params: {name?: (default: a new "PDF Preset N"), newName?: rename it, description?, preset?: the preset to start from (default: the saved preset `name`, else VectorCraft Default), …options of document.exportPdf} create or change a saved preset (built-in presets are read-only; passwords are never stored) → {name, created, settings}

commands.label: Delete PDF Preset
commands.params: {name} delete a saved preset (built-in ones stay) → {deleted: name}

commands.label: Export PDF Presets
commands.params: {names?: [preset names, built-in ones too] (default: every saved preset), path?} write the presets as a .vcpdfpresets file (JSON) → {path, count}; without path → {data: the file's text, count}

commands.label: Import PDF Presets
commands.params: {path? | data?: file text | dataBase64?, replace?: false (replace saved presets of the same names; else imported ones whose name is taken get a number)} add the presets of a .vcpdfpresets file (as pdf.preset.export writes) to the saved ones → {imported: [names]}

commands.label: Export DXF
commands.params: {path?, version?: R12|R13|R14|2000|2004|2007|2010|2013|2018 (default), unit?: mm (default; any unit name: pt, in, cm…), scale?: 1 (drawing units per unit), scaleLineweights?: false, colors?: 8|16|256|true (default; true colour needs 2004+, else 256), rasterFormat?: png (default)|jpeg (placed images, written next to the file), preserve?: appearance (default: type as outlines; strokes a CAD line can't draw as filled outlines; brush art)|editability (type as text; every stroke a line with its lineweight and dashes), alterPaths?: false (strokes a CAD line can't draw as their filled outlines, with editability too; also strokes wider than 2.11 mm, and every stroke in R13 and R14), outlineText?: false, selectedOnly?: false (the selected objects, in their layers), artboard?: 0 (the origin is its bottom-left corner), useArtboards?: true (one drawing per chosen artboard, artboards?/range?, holding the art over it: {stem}-{artboard}.dxf) | false (the origin at the art's bounds)} → {path, bytes, warnings, files?, linked?: [image files]}; no path → {dataBase64, …, linked?: [{name, dataBase64}]}. Layers become DXF layers (hidden: off; locked; non-printing: not plotted); paths become polylines and splines, fills their outlines (which laser and cutter software reads) and solid hatches. Same as document.export {format: dxf}

commands.label: Export EPS
commands.params: {path?, level?: 2|3 (default; PostScript language level: 3 writes smooth gradients and masks transparent image pixels out, 2 steps gradients and writes those pixels white), previewFormat?: none|tiffBw|tiffColor (default: a TIFF preview other apps show), transparentPreview?: true (else on white), overprints?: preserve (default)|discard, flattenerPreset?: "medium" (default; high, low or a saved preset: flattener.presets.list), flattener?: {the options of object.flattenTransparency over the preset}, embedFonts?: true (type is always written as outlines, so no fonts are needed), includeLinkedFiles?: false (the embedded document keeps linked images whole, not just their previews), thumbnails?: true (a PNG thumbnail in the file), cmykPostScript?: true (RGB documents written in CMYK), compatibleGradients?: false (stepped gradients at level 3 too), selectedOnly?: false, useArtboards?: true (one file per chosen artboard, artboards?/range?, {stem}_{artboard}.eps, the bounding box the artboard; with two or more, also the central file {stem}.eps first: the whole document, the bounding box the visible art; none when no art shows) | false (one file, the bounding box the visible art, y up from the first artboard's bottom-left corner, even when artboards are named; the default when none are named), format?: "eps", artboard?: i | artboards?: [i…] | range?: "1-3, 5" (the artboards written; naming them without useArtboards works as useArtboards: true)} → {path, bytes, warnings, files?}; no path → {dataBase64, …}. Transparency is flattened with the preset (EPS has none); the native document rides along in comments, for reopening the file as it was. Same as document.export {format: eps}

commands.label: Package
commands.params: {folder?, name?: (default: "<document> Folder"), copyLinks?: true, linksFolder?: true (the linked files go in Links/, else next to the document), relink?: true (the packaged document links to the copies), copyFonts?: true (the fonts its type uses go in Fonts/; fonts whose licence doesn't allow embedding are left out), report?: true (<document> Report.txt)} copy the saved document as it is now into folder/name as <document>.vectorcraft with its linked files and fonts; the open document doesn't change → {folder, files: [paths relative to folder/name], links, fonts (counts copied), missingLinks: [file names not found], skippedFonts: [{font, reason}], warnings: [nested files copied unchanged or cycles/depth stopped]}; no folder → the same with {name: "<name>.zip", dataBase64} (a zip of the files in <name>/) instead of folder

commands.label: Make
commands.params: {ids?} make each selected object (or ids) an object slice: its slice follows the object's bounds → {ids: the new object slices}

commands.label: Release
commands.params: {} release the selected slices: an object slice leaves its object as it was, a user slice becomes an unpainted rectangle; the objects end up selected → {ids}

commands.label: Create from Guides
commands.params: {} replace the user slices with the grid the ruler guides cut the artboards into (two vertical and two horizontal guides give 9) → {ids}

commands.label: Create from Selection
commands.params: {ids?|id?} a user slice over the visual bounds of the selected objects (or ids), selected → {id}

commands.label: Duplicate Slice
commands.params: {dx?: pt (default 10), dy?: pt (default 10)} copy the selected slices as user slices with their options, offset by dx, dy; the copies are selected → {ids}

commands.label: Combine Slices
commands.params: {} replace the two or more selected slices with one user slice over their bounds (the first one's options; object slices are released) → {id}

commands.label: Divide Slices…
commands.params: {rows?: slices down, rowHeight?: pt per slice, columns?: slices across, columnWidth?: pt per slice} cut each selected slice into a grid of user slices (evenly by count, or by size with a smaller last one; an object slice is released); the pieces are selected → {ids}

commands.label: Delete All
commands.params: {} delete every user slice and release every object slice → {count}

commands.label: Slice Options…
commands.params: {kind?: "image"|"noImage"|"htmlText" (object slices of type only), name?, url?, target?, message?, alt?: (image), text?: cell text; HTML allowed (noImage), background?: ""|"matte"|"#rrggbb" (#rrggbbaa and #rgba are refused), hAlign?: "default"|"left"|"center"|"right", vAlign?: "default"|"top"|"middle"|"baseline"|"bottom"} set the selected slices' options as one undo step; no options: read them → the first slice's {kind, name, url, target, message, alt, text, background, hAlign, vAlign, htmlText: whether HTML Text applies}

commands.label: Clip to Artboard
commands.params: {on?: bool} toggle (or set) Clip to Artboard: on, slices are clipped to the artboards and auto slices fill them; off, auto slices cover the art and the slices → {on}

commands.label: Hide Slices
commands.params: {hidden?: bool} toggle (or set) whether the canvas hides the slices (session view state); hiding deselects the slices in every open document, and showing them again leaves them deselected and does not restore the selection that was cleared; while they are hidden no command selects one (an object that is an object slice can still be selected as art) → {hidden}

commands.label: Lock Slices
commands.params: {locked?: bool} toggle (or set) the slice lock: locked slices can't be selected or edited with the Slice Selection tool; locking deselects the slices in every open document, and unlocking leaves them deselected and does not restore the selection that was cleared; while it is on no command selects one (an object that is an object slice can still be selected as art) → {locked}

commands.label: List Slices
commands.params: {} the slices as laid out, numbered left to right and top to bottom → {slices: [{number, id (null for auto slices), source: "user"|"object"|"auto", name, x, y, width, height, options, selected (selected with the Slice Selection tool or a slice command, or an object slice whose object is selected)}], clipToArtboard, hidden, locked}

commands.label: Slices
commands.params: {} select every user and object slice → {count}

commands.label: Create Slice
commands.params: {x, y, width, height} a user slice over that rectangle, selected (the Slice tool's drag) → {id}

commands.label: Set Slice Rectangle
commands.params: {id: user slice, x, y, width, height} move or resize a user slice (an object slice follows its object) → {id}

commands.label: Move Slices
commands.params: {slices?: [id…] (default: the selected slices), dx, dy} move the slices: user slices move, object slices move their objects → {ids}

commands.label: Delete Slices
commands.params: {slices?: [id…] (default: the selected slices)} delete the user slices and release the object slices (their objects stay) → {count}

commands.label: Select Slices
commands.params: {slices?: [id…] (user slice ids or ids of objects with an object slice; none: deselect the slices), toggle?: bool (Shift: add the unselected ones, drop the selected ones)} select slices as the Slice Selection tool does; the objects are deselected → {selected: [id…]}

commands.label: Print Setup
commands.params: {preset?: name ([Default] or a saved print preset, any case: print.presets.list; its settings replace the document's, as choosing it in the Print dialog does), settings?: {copies: 1 (1–999), collate: true, reverse, artboards: all|range|ignore (all the art as one page), range: "1-3, 5" (1-based, with artboards: range), skipBlank (leave out artboards with no art that prints), media: letter|legal|tabloid|a3|a4|a5|a6|b4|b5|b4 (jis)|b5 (jis)|b6 (jis)|japanese postcard|japanese double postcard|japanese envelope #3|japanese envelope #4|kaku #2|kaku #3|yonroku-ban|custom (a paper is named by its id or its dialog label, any case and spacing, so `B5 (JIS)` works; b4 and b5 stay the ISO 216 sizes, 250 × 353 and 176 × 250 mm, and the JIS sizes are b4 (jis) 257 × 364 mm, b5 (jis) 182 × 257 mm and b6 (jis) 128 × 182 mm), width, height (custom paper, 72–14400 pt), orientation: portrait|landscape|portraitFlipped|landscapeFlipped, autoRotate: true (turn the paper to each artboard; orientation ignored), transverse (the page a quarter turn on the paper), printLayers: visiblePrintable|visible|all (template layers never print), placement: {origin: topLeft|top|topRight|left|center|right|bottomLeft|bottom|bottomRight (the point of the printed area, the artboard with its bleed and marks, on the same point of the imageable area), x, y (pt, right and down)}, scaling: none|fit|custom|tileFull|tileImageable, scale: {width: 100, height: 100} (% with custom and tiling), overlap: 0 (pt between tiles), tileRange: "" (1-based tiles across then down; empty: all), margin: 0 (pt the device can't print around the paper: the imageable area is inside it), marks: {trim, registration, colorBars, pageInfo, kind: roman|japanese, weight: 0.25, offset: 6} (as document.exportPdf, at the paper's scale; page information adds the tile and the ink), bleed: {useDocument: true (the document's bleed, document.setup), top, bottom, left, right} (pt), output: {mode: composite|separations (one grey page per ink that prints), emulsion: up|down (down mirrors), image: positive|negative, spotsToProcess, inks: [{name: "Cyan"|…|a spot swatch, print: true, frequency (lpi, default 60), angle (default C 15, M 75, Y 0, K 45, spots 45)}]}, graphics: {autoFlatness: true, flatness: 1 (0.2–100), fonts: none|subset|complete}, color: {intent: perceptual|relativeColorimetric|saturation|absoluteColorimetric, preserveNumbers: true (CMYK colours keep their values), profile: "" (the printer profile, an RGB or CMYK one: composite PDF colours are converted to it with the intent, separations separate with a CMYK one; empty: as they are)}, advanced: {printAsBitmap (composite pages print as one image each, at the document's raster effects resolution), overprints: preserve|discard|simulate (composite output; preserve writes them to overprint (/OP), simulate prints them as Overprint Preview shows them; separations always keep them), flattenerPreset: "" (a flattener preset, built-in or saved: transparency is flattened before printing; empty: it prints live; PostScript defaults to medium)}, tileOrigin: {placed: false, x, y} (where the Print Tiling tool put the pages: print.tiling.set)}} store the print settings with the document, over the ones it has or the preset's (null keeps a value), as one undo step; no settings or preset → {settings} (the current ones, defaults if never set up)

commands.label: Print Preview
commands.params: {preset?: name (as print.setup's: its settings instead of the document's), settings?: {…settings of print.setup} (over the document's or the preset's)} → {pages (copies included), sheets: [{artboard (0-based; null with artboards ignored), tile? (1-based), ink? (separations), width, height (pt, the page), orientation, scale: [width %, height %], transform: [a, b, c, d, e, f] (document space → the page, pt, y down), area: [x0, y0, x1, y1] (the document region the page prints), trim: [x0, y0, x1, y1] (the artboard on the page)}] (one copy, in order), tiles: [{artboard, columns, rows, printed: [1-based tiles], tiles: [[x0, y0, x1, y1]…] (document space)}], inks: [{name, spot, print, frequency, angle}] (separations), warnings (art larger than the imageable area, type that prints in the fallback font, type that doesn't fit its frame, options not applied yet…), settings} without printing

commands.label: Print
commands.params: {preset?: name (as print.setup's: its settings instead of the document's; the saved settings stay), settings?: {…settings of print.setup} (over the document's or the preset's), includeArtboardFill?: true (each artboard's background color prints behind its art; false leaves it out), path?, format?: pdf (default: a print-ready PDF) | postscript (the default for a .ps path: a PostScript file with DSC comments, %%Pages, a page per sheet with its paper size, marks, separations with their ink and halftone screen, the fixed flatness, negatives), level?: 3|2 (the PostScript language level), flattenerPreset?: "medium" (PostScript: the preset transparency is flattened with — high, low or a saved one, see flattener.presets.list), acknowledgeLoss?: bool (with path: write over the file the document was read from although reading it left things out), forPrinter?: bool (the PDF goes to a print queue: a page whose paper is turned to landscape is written upright, the art turned a quarter anticlockwise, as a printer driver turns a landscape job; macOS prints a landscape page as it is, cut off on upright paper; paper wide in Portrait and transverse pages stay as they are)} print the document, one page per sheet of paper (per tile, per ink, per copy) → {pages, format, path, bytes, warnings}; no path → {dataBase64, bytes, pages, format, warnings}. Raster effects print at the document's raster effects resolution; a PDF leaves halftone screens and flatness to the output device

commands.label: Save Recovery Data
commands.params: {} write a recovery copy of every modified document changed since its last copy, in this app's own area of the store (the app does this every autosaveInterval minutes while autosaveRecovery is on; documents of more than 20000 objects are skipped while recoveryOffForComplex is on). Images are stored apart, each once while unchanged. A copy goes when its document is saved, reverted or closed → {saved: [{file, title, bytes, imageBytes (images written this time)}], skipped: [{title, reason}], location} (location: the recovery folder, or browser storage on the web)

commands.label: Recovery Data
commands.params: {} the recovery copies in the store → {copies: [{file ("<area>/<name>"), title, path (the document's file, if it had one), format, saved (Unix seconds or null), open (the copy of a document open here), running (kept by another VectorCraft that is running)}], location}; copies neither open nor running were left behind by a crash

commands.label: Restore Recovered Documents
commands.params: {file?} open a copy left behind by a crash (default: every one; a running VectorCraft's copies are never taken) as a new document titled "<name> [Recovered]": modified, and Save asks where to save it (suggesting its original file) → {restored: [{index, title, file, path, warnings, missingLinks, modifiedLinks, updatedLinks}], failed: [{file, error}] (damaged copies, when restoring every one; a named one fails the command)}. The copy moves to this app's area and stays until the document is saved or closed

commands.label: Discard Recovered Documents
commands.params: {file?} delete a copy left behind by a crash (default: every one; copies of open documents and of running VectorCraft apps stay) → {discarded: [file…]}

commands.label: DXF Info
commands.params: {path} or {name?, dataBase64} what a DXF drawing holds → {version (2018, R12…), units (its drawing unit: Millimeters, Inches, Unitless…), layouts: ["Model", paper layouts…], layers: [name…], unit, scale (the default ratio: 1 unit = scale drawing units, the drawing at 1:1)}; a binary DXF or a DWG answers an error saying to save it as ASCII DXF

commands.label: Save for Web
commands.params: {path?, preset?: a webExport.presets name (its settings, then these keys), format?: gif (default)|jpg|png8|png24, reduction?: perceptual|selective (default)|adaptive|web|blackWhite|gray (gif/png8, as the next five), colors?: 128 (2–256), dither?: none|diffusion (default)|pattern|noise, ditherAmount?: 100, webSnap?: 0 (0–100 %: colours that close to a web-safe one become it), lossy?: 0 (0–100, gif), colorTable?: {locked?: ["#rrggbb"…] (kept when reducing), transparent?: ["#rrggbb"…] (become transparent), webShift?: ["#rrggbb"…] (become web-safe), sort?: none|hue|luminance|popularity} (colours as the preview's colors[].source; #rrggbbaa and #rgba are refused here and in matte), transparency?: true (gif/png8/png24), matte?: white (default)|black|none|"#rrggbb" (what edges blend into; jpg and opaque png24: the background), interlaced?: false (gif/png8/png24), quality?: 60 (jpg: 0–100), progressive?: false (jpg), optimized?: true (jpg), embedProfile?: false (jpg: sRGB profile), width?: px | height?: px | percent?: 100 (the image size, proportional; width wins over height, height over percent), antiAlias?: none|art (default)|type, clipToArtboard?: true (the artboard; false: the art and the slices), artboard?: 0 (0-based), convertToSrgb?: true (PNG files say they are sRGB), metadata?: none|copyright (default)|contact|all (File Info written as PNG text, a GIF or JPEG comment), slices?: all (default)|selected|none (one image per slice: images/<slice name>.<ext>), output?: images (default)|html (an HTML page placing the image or slices, <stem>.html)} → {path, files: [path…], bytes (total), width, height, warnings: [] or [a note that an image couldn't be decoded and is missing from the image]}; no path → {files: [{name, dataBase64}], bytes, width, height, warnings} (names such as page.html, images/page_01.gif). A single image without HTML is written at path itself

commands.label: Save for Web Preview
commands.params: {…the settings of document.exportForWeb (preset?, format?…), slice?: n (1-based, from slice.list; default the whole image), kbps?: 56.6 (connection speed for the download time), image?: false (also the optimised file as dataBase64)} what Save writes for the whole image (or one slice) → {format, width, height, bytes (exactly the file's size), seconds (to download at kbps), kbps, colors?: [{color: "#rrggbb", source: "#rrggbb" (the colour the reduction made, as colorTable lists it), transparent, locked, webShifted, webSafe}] (gif/png8: the colour table in file order), mappedToTransparent?: ["#rrggbb"…], slices: images an export writes, warnings (as document.exportForWeb's), dataBase64?}

commands.label: Save for Web Settings
commands.params: {reset?: false, preset?, …the settings of document.exportForWeb} remember settings for the Save for Web dialog (it opens on them): the keys given change the remembered ones, a preset replaces them, reset goes back to the defaults; {} reads them → {settings}

commands.label: Save for Web Presets
commands.params: {} → {presets: [{name, builtIn, settings}]} the built-in presets, then the saved ones; any name works as `preset` in document.exportForWeb

commands.label: Save Save for Web Preset
commands.params: {name, newName?: rename it, preset?: start from this preset (default: the saved preset `name`, else the defaults), settings?: {…}, …the settings of document.exportForWeb} create or change a saved preset (built-in ones can't change) → {name, settings, created}

commands.label: Delete Save for Web Preset
commands.params: {name} delete a saved preset (built-in ones stay) → {deleted: name}

commands.label: Collect for Export
commands.params: {ids?: [id…] (default: the selected objects; a layer id collects the art under it, including in its sublayers), multiple?: true (an asset per object; false: one asset of them all), name?: (the asset's name, when it makes one)} collect art as assets for Window › Asset Export and Export for Screens' Assets tab, named after the object (else Asset 1, Asset 2…); art already collected as such an asset keeps it → {assets: [asset id…] (in order), added: n}. Assets follow their art: moving it moves the crop, deleting it removes it from the asset

commands.label: Remove Asset
commands.params: {assets: [asset id…]} take assets out of the Asset Export panel (their art stays) → {removed: n}

commands.label: Rename Asset
commands.params: {asset: id, name} rename an asset (its files' names)

commands.label: Assets
commands.params: {} → {assets: [{id, name, nodes: [id…], bounds: [x, y, width, height] | null (the crop: the bounds the renderer measures for what its art draws, effects included)}]} the Asset Export panel's assets, in order

commands.label: Export Assets
commands.params: {assets?: [asset id…] (default all), folder?, zip?, openLocation?, formats?, preset?, settings?, prefix?, subfolders?, antiAlias?} each asset's art alone, cropped to it, in every format row: document.exportForScreens {assets} at the document's export settings (document.exportSettings) under the ones given; with subfolders false every file goes into the folder itself, mobile and density rows too → what document.exportForScreens returns (no folder: the files, or one zip, as dataBase64). Leaves the remembered settings as they are (assets.settings.set changes them)

commands.label: Asset Export Settings
commands.params: {exportPreset?: (a preset of document.exportPresets.list: its formats or preset, its format settings over the saved ones, its prefix (none when it has none), its folders (or subfolders: rows or none) with subfolders on for rows, and antiAlias; the other keys go over it), formats?, preset?: mobile|density|"" (none), settings?, prefix?, subfolders?, antiAlias?} change the export settings the Asset Export panel and Export for Screens share (document.exportSettings; the values of document.exportForScreens; null removes one): formats replace a preset, a preset replaces the formats → {settings}. Not an undo step

commands.label: CSS Properties
commands.params: {ids?|id?: [id…] (default: the selection), units?: px|pt|mm|cm|in (default px; 1 px = 1 pt, as in SVG export), position?: false (position: absolute, left and top from the artboard's top-left), dimensions?: true (width, height), unnamed?: true (unnamed objects too, classes named after their kind; false: named objects only), rasterize?: false (art CSS can't describe as background-image: url(<class>.png), its picture, which css.export writes)} the CSS web pages style the objects with, one rule per object back to front (layers and plain groups stand for what they hold): a rectangle's or ellipse's fill as background-color or linear-/radial-gradient(), stroke as border, corners as border-radius; type's font, color, spacing and alignment; opacity, mix-blend-mode, shadows and glows (box-shadow, text-shadow), blur (filter) → {css, rules: [{id, selector, css, unsupported?: why CSS can't describe the art exactly (without rasterize it is written as its box), image?: the PNG it refers to}], skipped: n unnamed objects left out, warnings}

commands.label: Generate CSS
commands.params: {…options as css.selection} css.selection of every object in the document

commands.label: Export CSS
commands.params: {path?, scope?: selection|all (default selection; ids? picks the objects), …options as css.selection, id?: object id (default: the selection)} write the CSS (css.selection, or css.generate for all) to path and, with rasterize, each picture its rules refer to next to it (PNG of the object's visual bounds, 1 px per point) → {path, bytes, rules: n, images: [path…], warnings}; no path → {data: the CSS, name: <document>.css, rules, images: [{name, dataBase64}], warnings}; warnings are css.selection's and the pictures' as document.export gives them (an image that couldn't be decoded, type in the fallback font or that doesn't fit its frame), each once

commands.label: Print Presets
commands.params: {} → {presets: [{name, builtIn, settings (as print.setup's), changed: [{option, value}] (how it differs from [Default])}]} [Default] (the default print settings, protected) first, then the saved presets

commands.label: Save Print Preset
commands.params: {name?: (default: a new "Print Preset N"), newName?: rename it, preset?: the preset to start from (default: the saved preset `name`, else [Default]), settings?: {…settings of print.setup} (over it)} create or change a saved preset ([Default] is protected) → {name, created, settings}

commands.label: Delete Print Preset
commands.params: {name} delete a saved preset ([Default] stays) → {deleted: name}

commands.label: Export Print Presets
commands.params: {names?: [preset names, [Default] too] (default: every saved preset), path?} write the presets as a .vcprintpresets file (JSON) → {path, count}; without path → {data: the file's text, count}

commands.label: Import Print Presets
commands.params: {path? | data?: file text | dataBase64?, replace?: false (replace saved presets of the same names; else imported ones whose name is taken get a number)} add the presets of a .vcprintpresets file (as print.presets.export writes) to the saved ones → {imported: [names]}

commands.label: Show Print Tiling
commands.params: {on?: bool (default: toggle)} show the pages of the document's print settings on the canvas (each document has its own setting; the Print Tiling tool shows them too) → {on}

commands.label: Print Tiling
commands.params: {origin: [x, y] (document point: the top-left corner of the first page's imageable area), artboard? (0-based: the artboard it is measured from; default the printed artboard containing origin, its edges included, else the first; ignored with artboards: ignore)} | {reset: true} place the printed pages as the Print Tiling tool does, saved with the print settings (tileOrigin: {placed, x, y}, from the artboard's top-left corner; it replaces the placement, and tiles start there), as one undo step; reset → the placement places them again → {tileOrigin}

commands.label: Print Tiling Pages
commands.params: {settings?: {…settings of print.setup} (over the document's)} the pages as View → Show Print Tiling draws them, from print.preview's layout → {tileOrigin, pages: [{artboard (0-based; null with artboards ignored), number (1-based tile across then down, or page), printed (tiles outside tileRange don't), page: [x0, y0, x1, y1] (the paper's edge), imageable: [x0, y0, x1, y1] (inside the unprintable margin)}] (document space; every tile when tiling, else each page once)}

commands.label: List Plug-ins
commands.params: {} → {plugins: [{id, name, version, kind: "filter"|"effect"|"exporter", author, description, params (doc), paramsSchema, effect? (the effect id of a live effect: plugin.<id>), format? and extensions? (an exporter's format id, plugin.<id>, for document.export, and its file extensions), budget?: "heavy" (a filter that may compute for longer, see plugin.install's allowHeavy), size, source, permissions: [name] (what it may do: the ones its manifest lists, else the ones its kind implies; progress: it may report its progress, see Cancel and write log lines), hash (the module's SHA-256), api (the plug-in API level it was built for, 1 or 2)}], folder: the Additional Plug-ins Folder load report {folder, loaded, failed: [{file, error}]} | null}

commands.label: Plug-in Info
commands.params: {id} → plugin.list's entry plus {manifest, defaults, lastError (a live effect's last failure, null)}

commands.label: Run Plug-in
commands.params: {id, params?: {…} (the plug-in's parameters; or give them as top-level keys; missing ones take their defaults, see plugin.info), ids?: [..] (default: the selection), …the plug-in's parameters as top-level keys} run an object filter on the selected paths and compound paths (inside selected groups and layers too; hidden, locked, guide and clipping paths are left out): it may change, delete or add objects, as one undo step; the result is selected, except the objects it locked or made guides. With nothing selected it gets no objects (generators add theirs to the current layer) → {plugin, ids}

commands.label: Install Plug-in
commands.params: {path: a .wasm file (desktop) | dataBase64: the module (+ name?: shown as its source), replace?: bool (true: a plug-in with the same id is replaced), name?: file name (with dataBase64), allowHeavy?: bool (true once the user agreed to a heavy budget: a filter whose manifest asks for one, budget "heavy" in plugin.inspect, installs only with it), grant?: [permission] (the permissions the user granted: a plug-in whose manifest lists permissions, needsApproval in plugin.inspect, installs only when grant holds every one of them; the grant is recorded with the module's hash, and replacing the plug-in with one that lists no new permission needs none; with a plug-in store attached, only the grants kept there count), hash?: string (the module's SHA-256 as plugin.inspect gave it: a module with other bytes is refused)} validate and install a WebAssembly plug-in for this session → its plugin.list entry

commands.label: Inspect Plug-in
commands.params: {path: a .wasm file (desktop) | dataBase64: the module, name?: the file name shown as its source (with dataBase64)} validate a WebAssembly plug-in without installing it → the plugin.list entry it would have, plus needsApproval: bool (true when it lists permissions the user hasn't granted its id: plugin.install then needs grant)

commands.label: Remove Plug-in
commands.params: {id} uninstall a plug-in (its live effects then leave the geometry as it is) → {removed}

commands.label: Reload Plug-ins
commands.params: {path?: a folder (default: the Additional Plug-ins Folder preference)} install every *.wasm in it (desktop; a bad module is reported and skipped, and so are a heavy filter and a plug-in that lists permissions the user hasn't granted its id) → {folder, loaded: [id], failed: [{file, error}]}

commands.label: Check Script
commands.params: {path? | data?: the script's text | dataBase64?, name?: the file's name (default: the path's; with a path, only the reply's name), includes?: false (with a path: also check the files its #include lines name, inside the script's folder; not on the web)} check a script written for the reference app (.jsx, .jsxinc, .js, or a compiled .jsxbin) without running any of it → {name, kind: script|compiled|module|notText|tooLarge, needs: [language|dom|files|menuCommands|dialogs|hostOnly], lines, targets: [{value, app, instance?, version?, locale?, line, file?}], directives: [{name, value, line, form: "#"|"//@", file?}], includes: [{value, line, status: checked|missing|notFollowed|cycle|notRead|limit|unreadable, path?, file?}], features: [{id, count, lines}], dom: {members: [{path, count}], types: [{name, count}]}, menuCommands: {strings: [{value, count, lines}], dynamic}, outside: [{id: filesWritten|filesOpened|network|nativeCode|otherApps|environment|unseenCode|preferences, count, lines, modes?}], problems: [{code, line?, file?, detail?}], truncated} (file: the included file it is in; lines: at most 20 of the script's own, while counts include the included files; at most 8 MiB a file and 32 MiB in all, 64 included files 16 deep, 1,024 paths looked up for them, 1,000 entries a list, text echoed cut to 120 characters)

commands.label: Mirror & Cut
commands.params: {axis?: "vertical"|"horizontal"|"free" (vertical), from?: [x,y], to?: [x,y] (free: the axis through both; vertical/horizontal: the axis through `from`, default the selection's centre), keep?: "left"|"right"|"top"|"bottom" (the side kept; default left, or top for a horizontal-ish axis)} cut the selected paths and compound paths at the axis, reflect the kept half across it and join both halves into one closed shape (open paths are joined where they meet the axis); art wholly on the other side is deleted, as one undo step → {ids, removed}

commands.label: Line Cut
commands.params: {from: [x,y], to: [x,y]} split the selected paths and compound paths along the line through both points, extended across the art: filled shapes become their pieces on each side (holes kept), open paths split where they cross; as one undo step → {ids, removed: 0}

commands.label: Rectangle Cut
commands.params: {rect: [x, y, width, height]} or {from: [x,y], to: [x,y]} (opposite corners) crop the selected paths and compound paths to the rectangle as real geometry (not a clipping mask): filled shapes are intersected with it, open paths keep their parts inside, art wholly outside is deleted; as one undo step → {ids, removed}

commands.label: Vector Halftone…
commands.params: {shape?: "circle"|"ellipse"|"square"|"diamond"|"line" (circle), frequency?: lines per inch 1–300 (20), angle?: deg (45; CMYK: the black screen's, cyan −30°, magenta +30°, yellow −45° from it), mode?: "mono"|"cmyk" (mono), color?: mono dot colour ("#000000"; #rrggbbaa and #rgba are refused), invert?: bool (dots for light tones), clip?: true (clip the dots to the art's outline), keepOriginal?: false} the selection as vector halftone dots sized by its tone, a group of one path per screen (CMYK screens multiply), as one undo step → {id, dots, warning? (an image in the art couldn't be decoded, as object.rasterize says)}

commands.label: Perspective Grid
commands.params: {} → {grid: the model (as perspective.grid.set takes it), define: the Define Grid fields (as perspective.grid.define takes them; name is the preset only while the grid still has its fields, else "" for custom: dragging the horizon, a vanishing point or the station point makes it custom, moving a plane does not), station: {x, y, distance} (the viewer: centre of vision on the horizon, distance to the picture plane, pt), defined: false while the document uses the default grid}

commands.label: Define Perspective Grid
commands.params: {name?: preset name ("" = custom), kind?: 1|2|3, units?: unit name (points, pixels, inches, centimeters, millimeters…), scale?: [artboard, real world], gridline?: gridline every, angle?: viewing angle (0–90°), distance?: viewing distance, horizonHeight?: above the ground level, thirdVp?: [x right, y up] from the centre of vision (3-point), leftColor?, rightColor?, groundColor?: "#rrggbb", opacity?: 0–100} lengths are real-world lengths in `units` at `scale`; missing fields keep the grid's (see perspective.grid.get define). Only what changes changes: a new type, angle or distance moves the vanishing points around the station point. One undo step → the new define fields

commands.label: Perspective Grid Presets
commands.params: {} → {presets: [{builtIn, name, kind, …the perspective.grid.define fields}]} the built-in views (fitted to the first artboard, protected) first, then the saved presets

commands.label: Save Perspective Grid Preset
commands.params: {name?: (default: a new "Perspective Preset N"), newName?: rename it, preset?: the preset to start from (default: the saved preset `name`, else the document's grid), …the fields of perspective.grid.define (over it)} create or change a saved preset (Save Grid as Preset: just `name`); built-in ones are protected → {name, created, definition}

commands.label: Delete Perspective Grid Preset
commands.params: {name} delete a saved preset (built-in ones stay) → {deleted: name}

commands.label: Export Perspective Grid Presets
commands.params: {names?: [preset names, built-in ones too] (default: every saved preset), path?} write the presets as a .vcperspective file (JSON) → {path, count}; without path → {data: the file's text, count}

commands.label: Import Perspective Grid Presets
commands.params: {path? | data?: file text | dataBase64?, replace?: false (replace saved presets of the same names; else imported ones whose name is taken get a number)} add the presets of a .vcperspective file (as perspective.presets.export writes) to the saved ones → {imported: [names]}

commands.label: Perspective Grid Options
commands.params: {show?: bool, position?: topLeft|topRight|bottomLeft|bottomRight} the Plane Switching Widget: shown or not, and the corner of the document window it stays in (kept with the preferences; no params reads them) → {show, position}

commands.label: Lock Grid
commands.params: {on?: bool} (no param toggles) View › Perspective Grid › Lock Grid: the grid's widgets can't be dragged (the Plane Switching Widget still works). View state: not an undo step → {on}

commands.label: Lock Station Point
commands.params: {on?: bool} (no param toggles) dragging one vanishing point moves the other around the station point (the viewing angle turns, the viewer stays). View state: not an undo step → {on}

commands.label: Snap to Grid
commands.params: {on?: bool} (no param toggles) art drawn or moved in perspective lands on gridlines within a quarter cell (on by default). View state: not an undo step → {on}

commands.label: Show Rulers
commands.params: {on?: bool} (no param toggles) a ruler up the line where the planes meet, in the grid's units at its scale. View state: not an undo step → {on}

commands.label: Read Shortcut Set File
commands.params: {path? | data?: the file's text | dataBase64?, name?: the file's name (default: the path's)} read a shortcut set another app saved as text (.kys, starting "/Menus {") without changing anything: each entry is a block that sets /Key, with the names of the blocks around it as its section → {set: the file's name without its extension, entries: [{section: [names], name, key, modifiers, context, represent, line, target?, chord?}] (codes as the file writes them; null where the entry doesn't set one; target: what importMatches says the name stands for; chord: the shortcut its codes stand for, as Edit › Keyboard Shortcuts writes it, when importMatches decodes them, an entry without /Modifiers taking none), codes: {keys: [{value, count, key?}], modifiers: [{value, count, mods?}]} (key and mods from importMatches), unread: [{line, text}] (tokens that aren't read, at most 1000), truncated: true when a cap stopped the reading (4 MiB, 16 open blocks, 20,000 entries, 8 MiB of names over the entries and their sections; names past 1,024 bytes are cut)}. A file in another form (such as XML) is an error

commands.label: Import Matches
commands.params: {kind?: name|key|modifiers, query?: text (in the name, target or label; any case)} the matches the user confirmed when importing other apps' files (shortcut sets), kept with the preferences → [{kind, name, target, label?}] (target "": no equivalent)

commands.label: Remember Import Matches
commands.params: {matches: [{kind: name|key|modifiers, name: as the file writes it (codes in decimal), target: a command id, tool:<id> or panel:<id> (name), a key as Edit › Keyboard Shortcuts writes it (key), modifiers as it writes them, such as Cmd+Shift (modifiers), "" for no equivalent (no modifiers for kind modifiers), or null to forget the match, label?}]} remember what names and codes in another app's file stand for in VectorCraft, for later imports (at most 20,000 matches; names, targets and labels up to 1,024 bytes) → {count}

commands.label: Forget Import Matches
commands.params: {kind?: name|key|modifiers} forget the import matches, all of them or those of one kind → {removed}

commands.label: Arrange in Grid
commands.params: {layout?: "grid" (rows and columns) | "row" (one row) | "column" (one column), columns?: 1..10000 (grid; default ⌈√count⌉; never more than the count), gapX?: pt −1000000..1000000 (10), gapY?: pt −1000000..1000000 (gapX), centerOnArtboard?: false (true: the grid is centred on the artboard under the selection's centre, else the first; false: it starts at the selection's top-left)} lay the selected objects (the top-level ones) out in their stacking order from the back, left to right and top to bottom, as one undo step. Each cell is as wide as the widest object in its column and as tall as the tallest in its row, each object is centred in its cell, and everything is measured by visual bounds (strokes and effects as drawn) → {count}

commands.label: Swap Objects
commands.params: {size?: false (true: each also takes the other's width and height), scaleStrokes?: the Scale Strokes & Effects preference} swap the places (bounds centres) of the two selected objects, measured as object.setBounds measures them (Use Preview Bounds), as one undo step. Off unless exactly two objects are selected

commands.label: Replace with Top Object
commands.params: {fit?: "keep" (the copy keeps its size) | "bounds" (scaled to the replaced object's width and height) | "proportional" (scaled to fit inside them, in proportion) ("keep"), scaleStrokes?: the Scale Strokes & Effects preference, keep?: false (true: the replaced objects stay, under their copies)} put a copy of the topmost selected object centred on each of the other selected objects, in that object's place in the stacking order, as one undo step; sizes and centres are measured as object.setBounds measures them, and the copies are selected → {ids}

commands.label: Set Size of Each
commands.params: {width?: pt, height?: pt (at least one; each 0.001..1000000), proportional?: false (with only one of them given, the other follows in proportion; else it stays), reference?: 0..8 (the 9-point grid row by row from the top-left; 4, the centre: the point of each object that stays put), scaleStrokes?: the Scale Strokes & Effects preference} give each selected object (the top-level ones) that width and height, measured as object.setBounds measures them (Use Preview Bounds), as one undo step → {count}

commands.label: Group Overlapping Objects
commands.params: {} group the selected objects (the top-level ones, at most 20000) wherever their visual bounds overlap or touch, chains included (when A overlaps B and B overlaps C, all three go in one group), as one undo step. Only objects in the same layer or group are grouped together, objects that overlap nothing stay as they are, and each new group goes where its frontmost member was in the stacking order; the new groups and the objects left alone stay selected → {groups: [id…], grouped (how many objects went into groups)}

commands.label: Randomize Opacity
commands.params: {min?: % 0..100 (30), max?: % 0..100 (100; not less than min), seed?: whole number (0; the same seed, objects and range give the same opacities), ids?: [id…] (default: the selection)} give each selected object (the top-level ones) its own opacity, picked at random and evenly from min to max, as one undo step; it is the object's opacity, as the Transparency panel sets it → {count}

commands.label: Sort Objects
commands.params: {by?: "width" | "height" | "area" (width × height) | "x" (left edge) | "y" (top edge) | "opacity" (%) | "stacking" (stacking order, from the back) ("area"), apply?: one of the same ("stacking"), order?: "ascending" (small to large) | "descending" (large to small) | "random" ("ascending"), distribute?: false (true: the values step evenly from the smallest to the largest; false: the objects trade the values they have), seed?: whole number (0; the order "random" picks), scaleStrokes?: the Scale Strokes & Effects preference (width, height and area), ids?: [id…] (default: the selection)} sort the selected objects (the top-level ones, at most 20000) by the attribute `by` and give them the values of `apply` in that order, as one undo step: the first in order gets the smallest value. Sizes and places are measured and set as object.setBounds measures them (Use Preview Bounds), a width, height or area about each object's centre (an area in proportion); stacking order always trades places, and only among the objects in the same layer or group. A run that changes nothing makes no step → {count}

commands.label: Simplify Anchors (Keep Shape)…
commands.params: {tolerance?: 1..100 (20; higher removes more anchors and lets the outline move further from where it was, up to tolerance × 0.02 pt), protectCorners?: bool (false; anchors where the path turns by more than 30° stay), ids?: [id…] (default: the selection)} remove the anchors each path under the objects can do without, refitting the handles beside each so the outline keeps its shape, as one undo step; open ends stay, and locked and hidden paths are left out → {ids, before, after} anchor counts

commands.label: Health Check
commands.params: {scope?: "selection"|"document" (default: the selection, or the document while nothing is selected), kinds?: [kind…] (default: all: emptyText, strayPoints (paths of one anchor), unpainted, zeroOpacity, duplicateObjects (a path stacked on an identical one, or type on the same type within 1 pt), offArtboard, duplicateAnchors (neighbours within 0.01 pt), tinyHandles (under 0.01 pt), collinearAnchors (corners on a straight run, turning less than sine 0.005), nearPoints (anchors within 0.01 pt of other paths' anchors), nearlyClosed (ends within 0.01 pt), filledOpenPaths (filled, unstroked open paths), needlessClipGroups (an unpainted clip that clips nothing, hides everything, or is a rectangle round all its art), needlessCompounds (one path or none), needlessGroups (one member or none, nothing of their own), emptyArtboards (the document only))} find issues without changing anything; locked and hidden objects are left out → {scope, total, findings: [{kind, label, count, ids (the objects, at most 1000), artboards (indexes)}]} for the kinds found

commands.label: Show Issue
commands.params: {kind: kind (see addon.cleanup.check), scope?: "selection"|"document"} select the objects with that issue → {kind, count, ids, artboards}

commands.label: Fix All Issues
commands.params: {scope?: "selection"|"document", kinds?: [kind…] (default: all; see addon.cleanup.check)} fix the issues addon.cleanup.check finds, in up to three rounds while a round still finds some (a fix can leave issues for another kind), as one undo step: what is empty, unpainted, invisible, duplicated or off the artboards goes, anchors merge, snap or go, tiny handles retract, paths close and needless groups, compound paths and clipping groups give way to their contents → {scope, total, fixed: {kind: count}}

commands.label: Deep Ungroup…
commands.params: {includeClipGroups?: bool (false: clipping groups, and the art inside them, stay as they are; true: they are ungrouped too and their clipping paths become plain paths), ids?: [id…] (default: the selection)} ungroup every level of the groups among the objects, as one undo step; each object keeps the opacity of the groups it was in; locked and hidden groups stay whole, and locked and hidden objects stay locked or hidden and are not selected → {ids (the objects selected: those left, or with no group to take apart the selection as it was), ungrouped (groups)}

commands.label: Rejoin Path Pieces…
commands.params: {gap?: pt 0..6 (0.1), ids?: [id…] (default: the selection)} weld the open paths under the objects whose ends lie within the gap of each other back into paths: an end joins one other end, the one the path turns least to go on into, pieces may run either way, and a chain whose ends meet closes; each path takes the place and paint of its topmost piece, as one undo step → {ids, joined (paths made), removed (pieces merged into them)}

commands.label: Break Text
commands.params: {by?: "lines"|"paragraphs"|"words"|"glyphs" (lines), ids?: [id…] (default: the selection)} each horizontal point or area type object becomes point type objects, one per line, paragraph, word or glyph, each where its characters were and with their character styles, as one undo step; spaces between pieces go, a paragraph's lines stay lines (a wrapped line ends in a line break), justified lines close up, and a paragraph broken out whole keeps its bullet (not its number; other pieces have no list markers). Type on a path, vertical type, threaded type and area type whose text doesn't fit stay as they are → {ids (the pieces, selected), skipped}

commands.label: Combine Point Text
commands.params: {ids?: [id…] (default: the selection)} merge one-line horizontal point type into as few objects as it can, every glyph staying where it was: pieces turned and sheared alike whose baselines line up (within 0.4 em; the difference becomes baseline shift) join left to right, a space goes between pieces at least half a space apart, and tracking on the character before each piece keeps the spacing; each object keeps its character styles, and the leftmost piece of each run its place and paint, as one undo step → {ids (the objects made, selected), combined (pieces merged into them)}

commands.label: Join Point Text
commands.params: {ids?: [id…] (default: the selection)} join one-line horizontal point type into one point type object, as one undo step: pieces turned and sheared like the top-left one are read as lines (baselines within 0.4 em of each other), top to bottom, each line's pieces left to right with a space between them; each line becomes a paragraph, left aligned, and keeps the distance between baselines as its leading. The text keeps its character styles; the object takes the top-left piece's place and paint, and the other pieces go → {id (selected), joined (pieces merged into it), lines}

commands.label: Remove Breaks
commands.params: {kind: "line"|"paragraph", ids?: [id…]} remove the forced line breaks (line) or paragraph returns (paragraph) in the characters selected with a Type tool (after Select All in a frame of threaded text, in the text of every frame of the story), else in all the text of the selected type, as one undo step; a break between two words becomes a space, the frames of a threaded story selected all together being read as one text → {ids, removed}

commands.disabled_reason: Click in type with a Type tool to split it
commands.label: Split Text at Cursor
commands.params: {} while a Type tool edits horizontal point or area type: the text before the selected characters, they and the text after become point type objects of their own (at a cursor: before and after it), each where its characters were, as one undo step; spaces at the ends of each piece go, and editing ends with the pieces selected → {ids}

commands.label: Set Alignment, Keep Position
commands.params: {align: "left"|"center"|"right", ids?: [id…] (default: the selection)} align every paragraph of each horizontal point type object so, moving the object so its longest line stays where it is (one line: the text doesn't move), as one undo step → {ids (the objects changed)}

commands.label: Reset Text Transform
commands.params: {scale?: bool (false: the horizontal scale stays; true: it goes too, the object's and every character's), ids?: [id…] (default: the selection)} take the rotation, shear and reflection off each point type object, its size and the centre of its text staying, as one undo step → {ids (the objects changed)}

commands.label: Replace Missing Fonts…
commands.params: {font?: family (default: the default type font, Source Sans 3; any of its names)} set every character of the document's type (the type in the art of its symbols included) whose font family isn't available in `font`, in the style it has closest to the one each had, as one undo step → {runs (style runs changed), font}

commands.label: Select by Color Kind
commands.params: {kind: "spotColors" (objects painted with a spot colour swatch, solid or in a gradient's stops) | "colorEffects" (objects carrying a visible colour adjustment effect, on themselves or on a fill or stroke) | "rgbImages" | "cmykImages" | "grayImages" (embedded or linked images whose pixels are RGB, CMYK, or grayscale or 1-bit)} select those objects among the ones Select All reaches, inside groups too; locked and hidden ones are left out → {count}

commands.label: Apply as Filter
commands.params: {effect: a colour adjustment's effect id (adjust.brightnessContrast, adjust.curves, adjust.hueSaturation, adjust.levels, adjust.shiftToColor, adjust.temperatureTint, addon.color.exposure, addon.color.desaturate, addon.color.duotone or addon.color.invert), params?: {…} (as effect.apply; missing keys take the dialog defaults), fill?: true, stroke?: true, includeImages?: true, includePatterns?: true, ids?: [id…] (default: the selection)} recolour the objects and everything inside them as the live effect would draw them, but in their colours, as edit.colors.invert does (fills, strokes, type, gradient meshes, embedded images and pattern tiles), as one undo step; their effects stay. Duotone links a colour to its one tone's swatch as the live effect does → {changed}

commands.label: Print Ink Fixes
commands.params: {scope?: "selection" (the selection, or `ids`; by default, the document while nothing is selected) | "document" (every layer), inkLimit?: total ink % 1..400 (0 or left out: off), excludePureBlack?: true (black-only and grey colours keep their ink), removeWhiteOverprint?: false (white fills and strokes stop overprinting), overprintBlack?: black % 1..100 (black-only and grey fills and strokes this dark or darker overprint, as edit.colors.overprintBlack; 0 or left out: off), textOnly?: false (Overprint Black on type only), fill?: true, stroke?: true, ids?: [id…]} prepare a CMYK document's inks for print as one undo step: CMYK colours (solid, gradient stops, gradient meshes) with more total ink than inkLimit are scaled down to it (colours of spot swatches and Registration stay), white overprint is removed and black overprint set. Refused in RGB documents (File › Document Color Mode › CMYK Color first) → {changed, inkLimited: paints and meshes scaled, whiteOverprintRemoved: objects, blackOverprinted: objects}

commands.label: Find Nearest Swatch
commands.params: {library?: a swatch library's id or name (swatch.library.list: the built-in ones, and the colour books and libraries the user saved or loaded) or "document" (the document's swatches; the default), color?: colour (look this colour up, #rrggbbaa and #rgba refused; default: the selection's), fill?: true, stroke?: true (the selected objects' fills and strokes, their type's and those of the objects inside them: solid colours and gradient stops, once each, the first 100), count?: 1..50 (5), ids?: [id…] (default: the selection)} list the library's colour swatches closest to each colour, closest first, by CIEDE2000 difference (ΔE; under 1 hardly tells apart, about 2 to 3 close). Tint swatches, None and Registration aren't matched → {library, colors: [{values, hex, matches: [{name, values, hex, spot, deltaE}]}]}

commands.label: Apply Nearest Swatch
commands.params: {library?: as addon.color.nearestSwatch (default: "document"), fill?: true, stroke?: true, ids?: [id…] (default: the selection)} give each solid colour and gradient stop of the selected objects' fills and strokes (their type's and those of the objects inside them; gradient meshes too) the colour of its nearest swatch in the library, as addon.color.nearestSwatch finds it, as one undo step: a global or spot swatch's colour links to it. A library's swatches the colours take are added to the document's first, as swatch.library.add adds them (a spot colour stays spot); images and patterns keep their colours → {changed: paints changed, swatches: [the document swatches the colours took], added: [swatches added to the document]}

commands.label: Apply Fill to Stroke
commands.params: {ids?|id?, skipNone?: bool} each target's top stroke takes its own top fill, as it is (a colour in its model, a global or spot colour linked at its tint, a gradient or pattern with its placement, None); a stroke given paint at width 0 gets 1 pt, as Swap Fill and Stroke does. Type: each run's stroke takes its own fill, and while the Type tool has characters selected (no ids), only those.
