A graph's series marks and labels keep the paint when the graph is drawn again. skipNone: leave alone a target whose fill is None. A target whose stroke already has that paint is left as it is, and when nothing changes no undo step is recorded. The default stroke takes the default fill the same way → {objects}

commands.label: Apply Stroke to Fill
commands.params: {ids?|id?, skipNone?: bool} each target's top fill takes its own top stroke's paint, as addon.color.fillToStroke does the other way; the stroke itself is unchanged. The default fill takes the default stroke → {objects}

commands.label: Create Swatch Legend
commands.params: {names?: [swatch name…] (default: every colour swatch of the document, in panel order), columns?: 1..50 (4), size?: chip side in pt 8..1000 (72), gap?: pt 0..1000 (12), values?: [hex|rgb|cmyk|lab|gray…] (each at most once; default: each swatch's own colour model; spot swatches also say spot), x?, y? (the legend's top-left; default: the first artboard's, inset by `gap`)} draw a legend of colour swatches: one square chip per swatch filled with it (linked to it), labelled inside with the swatch name and the values asked for, in black on light chips and white on dark ones, as one group in one undo step; the group is selected → {id, count} (#4919)

commands.label: Contour
commands.params: {offset: pt (negative insets), corners?: "sharp"|"round"|"square" (default sharp; square cuts each corner off flat), miterLimit?: 1..500 (4; sharp corners only)} make a copy of each selected path or shape directly above it with a live Offset Path effect, or, for a selected object that already has one (a Contour), change that effect: nothing is baked (Expand Appearance bakes it) and the original is kept → {ids, created, updated}

commands.label: Save a Timestamped Copy
commands.params: {folder? (default: the document's own folder; needed for a document never saved), format?: vectorcraft|pdf|svg|svgz|ai|eps (default: the document's own, else vectorcraft), time?: Unix seconds (default: now)} write a copy of the document named <name>_YYYY-MM-DD_HH-MM.<ext> (the date and time in UTC; -2, -3… added when that name is taken) as File › Save a Copy writes it: the document keeps its path, title and modified state, and no undo step is made. Off where there is no clock (the web) → {path, format, bytes, warnings}

commands.label: Export All Open Documents
commands.params: {folder, format?: vectorcraft|pdf|svg|svgz|ai|eps (default: pdf)} write a copy of every open document, in tab order, to `folder` as File › Save a Copy writes it, each named after its document (<name>.<ext>; -2, -3… added when that name is taken, so no file is replaced), one self-contained file each with all of its art (images embedded or included, every artboard; no remembered save options apply): every document keeps its path, title and modified state, and no undo step is made. A document that can't be written is listed in `failed` and the others are still written; the active document stays active → {files: [{title, path, warnings}], failed: [{title, error}], format}

commands.label: Batch Trace Folder
commands.params: {folder, destinationFolder, preset?: name (imageTrace.presets; default: Default), expand?: false (true: trace and expand, as Make and Expand), format?: vectorcraft (default)|svg|pdf|ai|eps, includeSubdirs?: false} open each image in folder (png, jpg, tif, bmp, gif, webp, psd), select it, trace it with the preset, save it into destinationFolder as <name>.<ext> (-2, -3… added when that name is taken, so no file is replaced) and close it again, whether it traced or not; the document that was active stays active. Optional settings use their defaults only when omitted; null and values of the wrong type return an error before any image is opened. Caps: 500 images, 8 folder levels; a folder with more than 1,000 entries is refused. Not on the web (no file system) → {traced: [{path, output}], failed: [{path, error}], format} (#4921)

commands.label: New Symbols from Layers
commands.params: {layers?: [layer id…] (top-level layers; default: those highlighted in the Layers panel when two or more are, else every one), replace?: bool (false: the art stays; true: each layer's art is replaced by an instance of its symbol in the same place)} make one symbol of each layer's art as symbol.new makes one (registration in the centre), named after the layer (with a number added when a symbol has that name), as one undo step. Layers with no art are skipped, and with replace so are locked layers; with replace the instances are selected → {symbols: [name…], ids: [instance id…] (with replace), skipped: [{layer, name, reason: "empty"|"locked"}…]}

commands.label: Anchor Eraser Brush
commands.params: {points: [[x, y] | [x, y, pressure 0..1]…] (the brush's path, at most 100000 points), diameter?: pt 0.1..2500 (20; a point's pressure scales it), tolerance?: 1..100 (10; the outline may move up to tolerance × 0.02 pt), ignoreTolerance?: bool (false: every anchor under the brush that can go goes, its neighbours refitted), plain?: bool (false: true deletes them without refitting the handles beside them), ids?: [id…] (default: the selection)} remove the anchors of the paths under the objects that the brush passes over and that can go while the outline stays within the tolerance, as one undo step; open ends stay → {ids, removed}

commands.label: Extend Path
commands.params: {id, subpath?: index (0), end: "start"|"end", length?: pt (negative shortens; never all of it), to?: [x, y] (instead of length: the length that brings the end nearest this point), mode?: "straight"|"bezier" (stretch the last segment's curve, no anchor added)|"arc" (along the circle the end curves on, at most half way round) ("straight")} lengthen an open path at an end the way it runs there, or shorten it back along itself, as one undo step; with Keep Shared Points Together on, anchors coincident with an end that moves go with it → {id, length (pt)}

commands.label: Measure & Inspect
commands.params: {id, x, y, tolerance?: pt (3; how near an anchor counts as over it)} what the path reads at the point nearest (x, y): {subpath, closed, anchors, length, area (pt², an open subpath closed by a straight line), segment, t, point: [x, y], segmentLength, tangent (degrees counter-clockwise), radius (of curvature, null where straight), anchor?: {index, x, y, smooth, angle (at the anchor, null at an open end), in?: {length, angle}, out?: {length, angle}}}

commands.label: Set Anchor
commands.params: {x?, y?: pt (on the page), inLength?, outLength?: pt (0 retracts), inAngle?, outAngle?: degrees counter-clockwise} move the selected anchors (with their handles) and set their handles, as one undo step: direct-selected anchors, or every anchor of a path selected whole; a smooth anchor's other handle turns with the one set; with Keep Shared Points Together on, anchors coincident with one that moves go with it → {anchors}

commands.label: Make Smooth
commands.params: {ratio?: 0.1..0.5 (0.3905: a square's corners make a circle)} make the selected anchors smooth: a lone handle is mirrored; without handles, both stand at right angles to the bisector of the angle at the anchor, ratio × the nearer neighbour's distance long; two handles are put in line; an open end without handles aims at its neighbour's handle. One undo step → {anchors (changed)}

commands.label: Make Corner
commands.params: {retract?: bool (true: the handles go; false: they stay where they are and move apart)} make the selected anchors corners, as one undo step → {anchors (changed)}

commands.label: Equalize Handles
commands.params: {} give each selected anchor's two handles their average length (a missing one is made opposite the other), as one undo step → {anchors (changed)}

commands.label: Remove Points, Keep Shape
commands.params: {} remove the direct-selected anchors, refitting the handles beside each so the outline keeps its shape as best it can, as one undo step; open ends stay → {removed}

commands.label: Add Points to Segments…
commands.params: {count?: 1..100 (1)} add count anchors to each selected segment (a segment between two selected anchors, or every segment of a path selected whole), splitting it into pieces of equal length; the shape doesn't change. One undo step → {added}

commands.label: Close Path
commands.params: {mode?: "handles" (keep the ends' handles)|"straight" (a straight closing segment)|"smooth" (the ends made smooth), ratio?: 0.1..0.5 (0.3905, for smooth)} close the open subpaths of the selected paths, as one undo step → {closed}

commands.label: Add Points at Crossings
commands.params: {cut?: bool (false: add anchors where the paths cross; true: also cut them there), selfCrossings?: bool (false: where a path crosses itself too), ids?: [id…] (default: the selection)} where the paths under the objects cross one another, as one undo step; at most 10000 segments → {ids, crossings (anchors placed)}

commands.label: Slide Anchor Along Path
commands.params: {id, subpath?: index (0), anchor: index, t: -0.98..0.98 (where to: positive, a curve parameter on the segment after the anchor; negative, back from the end of the one before)} move an anchor along its path, the segments beside it refitted so the outline stays, as one undo step; ends of open paths don't slide; with Keep Shared Points Together on, anchors coincident with it go with it → {id, strayed (pt)}

commands.label: Divide into Dashes
commands.params: {dash?: pt 0.01..1000000 (10), gap?: pt 0..1000000 (0: the pieces touch), fit?: bool (false: exact lengths, the last piece of each run what is left; true: fit to corners and ends, every run between corners and ends holding whole dashes, all stretched or squeezed alike so it starts and ends on a dash), removeGaps?: bool (true: the gaps are left empty; false: they stay as pieces too)} cut the selected paths into separate open paths along the curve, each dash long with gap between them and keeping the path's appearance, as one undo step. Only the direct-selected segments (or those between two direct-selected anchors) are divided when there are any, the dash pattern running on across segments that follow one another; the rest of such a path stays, as pieces of its own. The pieces are selected; at most 100000 → {ids, dashes}

commands.label: Expand Dashes into Paths
commands.params: {ids?: [id…] (default: the selection)} turn the dashed stroke of each path and compound path under the objects into separate open paths, one per dash, laid out as the stroke draws them (its dash pattern, offset and Align Dashes to Corners and Path Ends), each keeping the path's appearance with the dashes off, so the gaps are real gaps: a dash running all the way round a closed path stays closed, and with a round or projecting cap a dash of no length (a dot) becomes a path on its point. The top stroke's dashes are the ones expanded; its arrowheads go, and the path's fills stay on it, below its dashes. Paths without a dashed stroke stay as they are. One undo step; the dashes are selected; at most 100000 → {ids, dashes}

commands.label: Parametric Shape
commands.params: {center: [x, y], kind?: "rectangle"|"ellipse"|"polygon" (default)|"star"|"ring"|"arrow"|"cross"|"heart"|"gear"|"bubble" (a speech bubble), width?, height?: 0.01..16384 pt (100), rotation?: degrees clockwise (0: upright), count?: 3..1000 (a polygon's sides, a star's points, a gear's teeth), a?, b?: the kind's own values (star: inner radius 0.01..1 of the outer, 0.5; ring: hole 0.01..0.99 of the size, 0.5; arrow: head length and shaft width 0.05..0.95, 0.4 and 0.4; cross: bar offset −0.9..0.9 (0, − up) and arm thickness 0.05..0.95 (1/3); heart: notch depth and point roundness 0..1 (0.4 and 0); gear: tooth height 0.01..0.9 (0.2); bubble: tail height 0.05..0.9 (0.25) and tail tip −1..1 across (−0.4)), radius?: corner radius 0..16384 pt (0; no corner rounds past the middle of a side)} draw a parametric shape with the current paint, selected, as one undo step; it stays editable with addon.pathtools.shape.set until its anchors are edited (moving, turning or scaling it keeps it) → {id, shape}

commands.label: Edit Parametric Shape
commands.params: {id, kind?, center?, width?, height?, rotation?, count?, a?, b?, radius?} change a parametric shape's numbers (as addon.pathtools.shape.create takes them; a new kind takes its own defaults for the values not given), as one undo step; with none, or the same ones, nothing changes → {id, shape (its numbers now)}

commands.label: Convert to Parametric Shape
commands.params: {ids?: [id…] (default: the selection)} make each plain closed path that is a rectangle, an ellipse or a polygon with equal sides and corners (stretched along its own axes at most) a parametric shape of the same outline, as one undo step → {ids (converted)}

commands.label: Set Corners
commands.params: {ids?: [id…] (the selection), anchors?: [index…] (of each path's outline with no corners cut; else its direct-selected anchors, or all of them), items?: [{id, anchors?}…] (instead of ids: each path with its own anchors), radius: pt 0..1000000 (drawn no larger than fits), kind?: "round"|"invertedRound"|"chamfer" (each corner's own), every?: "all"|"odd"|"even" (default all: of those anchors, only the odd- or even-numbered ones, counting each path's anchors from 1), minAngle?: degrees 0..180 (default 0), maxAngle?: degrees 0..180 (default 180; of those anchors, only the corners whose sides meet at an angle in this range: small for a sharp spike, near 180 for a shallow bend)} cut live corners at the anchors that can have one, as one undo step → {ids, corners (how many)}

commands.label: Remove Corners
commands.params: {ids?: [id…] (the selection), anchors?: [index…] (of each path's outline with no corners cut; else its direct-selected anchors, or all of them), items?: [{id, anchors?}…] (instead of ids: each path with its own anchors)} make those live corners sharp again, as one undo step → {ids, corners (how many)}

commands.label: Merge Shared Edge
commands.params: {a, b: two path ids (they needn't be selected), at: [x, y] (where), diameter?: pt 0.25..200 (20; how near `at` the edge is looked for), tolerance?: pt 0..3 (0.002; how near two anchors count as coincident), follow?: "average" (half way between the two)|"a"|"b" (keep that path's outline), ends?: bool (false: true makes an end even where the paths could merge)} where the paths touch at two coincident anchors, one each side of `at`, replace the stretches between them with one shared edge; stretches much longer one than the other (by over 10%) or leaving an end at over 120° aren't merged. Otherwise make an end there: two near anchors meet, and an anchor only one path has there is matched by a new one on the other. Each path stays closed or open; one undo step → {a, b, made: "edge"|"end"|"nothing" (merged already)}

commands.label: Keep Shared Points Together
commands.params: {enabled?: bool (default: the opposite of now)} Keep Shared Points Together: whether anchors coincident (within the Shared Edge Merge Tool's `tolerance`) with one that Slide Anchor Along Path, Extend Path or Set Anchor moves move with it, on any editable path (the `together` option of tool `sharedEdge`, kept with the preferences; off by default) → {enabled}

commands.label: Smart Pen
commands.params: {id, subpath?: index (default: the last open subpath), x, y, in?: [x, y], out?: [x, y], segment?: "straight" (the segment into the new anchor is a line: the previous anchor's handle on it goes, and the new anchor's incoming one)|"curved" (the previous anchor gets a handle on it if it has none: in line with its other handle, or with a straight segment before it)} add an anchor at the end of an open subpath of path id (default: the handles as given, the previous anchor as it is), as one undo step; the new anchor is selected → {anchor}

commands.label: Close Path
commands.params: {id, subpath?: index (default: the last open subpath), segment?: "straight"|"curved" (default: the closing segment takes the handles its ends have)} close an open subpath of two anchors or more, as one undo step

commands.label: Straight or Curved Segment
commands.params: {id, subpath?: index (0), segment: index, curved: bool} make a segment straight (its handles retracted) or curved (each end without a handle on it gets one, in line with its other handle or with a straight segment before it), as one undo step → {changed}

commands.label: Remove Points, Keep Shape
commands.params: {id, subpath?: index (0), anchor: index, plain?: bool (false: the handles beside it are refitted so the outline keeps its shape, and an open end takes its segment with it; true: it goes and the handles beside it stay as they are)} remove one anchor, as one undo step; a subpath keeps two anchors (three when closed)

commands.label: Convert Anchor Point
commands.params: {id, subpath?: index (0), anchor: index, ratio?: 0.1..0.5 (0.3905)} a smooth anchor becomes a corner with its handles where they are; any other anchor is made smooth by the auto-smooth rule (a lone handle mirrored; without handles both at right angles to the bisector of the angle at it, ratio × the nearer neighbour's distance long). One undo step → {smooth}

commands.label: Reshape Segment
commands.params: {id, subpath?: index (0), segment: index, t?: 0..1 (where it was grabbed, 0.5; held to 0.05..0.95), dx, dy: pt, mode?: "free" (both handles move, the one nearer the grab more)|"keepAngles" (each handle keeps its direction)|"symmetric" (both handles at right angles to the chord, at one length) ("free")} bend a segment so the point grabbed moves by (dx, dy); missing handles grow out of their anchors and a smooth anchor stays smooth. One undo step

commands.label: Next Segment
commands.params: {curved: bool} whether a click with the Smart Pen Tool adds a curved segment or a straight one (the tool's `next` option, kept with the preferences) → {next: "straight"|"curved"}

commands.label: Close or Join
commands.params: {} with exactly two open path ends direct-selected, join them as path.join does; else close the selected open paths keeping their ends' handles, as addon.pathtools.close does. One undo step

commands.label: Select by Artboards
commands.params: {artboards: [index…] (0-based, at least one), relation?: "overlap" (default: on at least one of them, as select.allOnArtboard takes it: the bounds overlap the artboard or the centre is on it) | "inside" (the bounds lie wholly within one of them, edges included) | "outside" (on none of them)} select those objects among the ones Select All takes (in isolation mode, the isolated container's); hidden and locked objects, objects on hidden, locked or template layers and art held by a locked artboard are left out. Bounds are geometric, a symbol instance's measured by its art → {count}

commands.label: Select by Link Status

commands.label: Text Tweaker
commands.params: {attribute?: "size" (pt 0.1..1296) | "baselineShift" (pt −1296..1296) | "rotation" (° −360..360) | "hScale" (% 1..10000) | "vScale" (% 1..10000) | "tracking" (1/1000 em −1000..10000) | "leading" (pt 0.1..5000) | "strokeWidth" (pt 0..1000) ("size"), from?: the first character's value, to?: the last character's value (each in the attribute's units and range; defaults: size 12 → 36, baselineShift 0 → 12, rotation 0 → 30, hScale and vScale 100 → 150, tracking 0 → 200, leading 12 → 36, strokeWidth 0 → 2), shape?: "straight" (an even ramp) | "ease" (slow at both ends) | "bow" (from at both ends, rising smoothly to `to` in the middle) | "spike" (from at both ends, straight up to `to` in the middle) | "random" (each character anywhere from `from` to `to`) ("straight"), seed?: whole number (0; random: the same seed and text give the same values), skipSpaces?: true (spaces and line breaks keep their values and don't count), id?, start?: byte, end?: byte (range endpoints inside a character round down to its start), ids?: [id…] (instead of id)} give the characters one character attribute letter by letter, from `from` to `to` along the shape, as the Character panel sets it, as one undo step; the text stays live and editable. The range of `id`, else the type objects in `ids`, else the text the Type tool has selected (at a caret: all its text), else every selected type object; each object gets its own ramp. Stroke weight only shows on characters with a stroke → {count (characters changed), ids}

commands.label: Release Type on a Path…
commands.params: {mode?: "both" (point type and the path) | "path" (the path only) | "text" (point type only) ("both"), keepOriginal?: false (true: the type on a path stays and the released objects go just above it), ids?: [id…], id? (instead of ids; neither: the selection)} split each type on a path among the objects (inside groups too) into point type and the path it was set on. The point type holds the same text with the same character and paragraph attributes, on one straight line whose baseline starts where the first character sat on the path; Type on a Path Options (effect, align to path, spacing, flip, brackets) don't apply to point type and are dropped. The path keeps its exact shape (open or closed, anchors and handles, the object's transform) and comes out with no fill and no stroke, in the type's layer and place in the stacking order. Other objects are left alone, and with no type on a path among them nothing changes and no undo step is made. One undo step; the released objects are selected → {ids (released, bottom to top), paths, texts}

commands.params: {open?: bool, toolbar?: name} open (true), close (false) or toggle (omitted) the All Tools drawer beside the toolbar (with `toolbar`, beside that toolbar made with New Toolbar, which shows), as the toolbar's ••• button does; while it is open, tools drag from it onto the toolbar and from the toolbar into it (Escape or a click outside closes it); returns the new state

commands.label: Toolbar: Add Tool
commands.params: {tool: id, slot?: n, place?: "before"|"after"|"group", toolbar?: name} put `tool` in the current (Basic or Advanced) toolbar (with `toolbar`, in that toolbar made with New Toolbar), moving it if it is there already: before (default) or after slot `slot` (0 = the first; omitted: at the end) in its own slot, or into that slot's group (its flyout), as dropping a tool from the Edit Toolbar drawer does; saved with the preferences; returns the toolbar's slots (lists of tool ids)

commands.label: Toolbar: Remove Tool
commands.params: {tool: id, group?: bool, toolbar?: name} take `tool` (with `group`, its whole group) out of the current toolbar (with `toolbar`, out of that toolbar made with New Toolbar; one not in it stays out), as dragging it into the Edit Toolbar drawer does; returns the toolbar's slots

commands.label: Toolbar: Reset
commands.params: {toolbar?: name} put the current (Basic or Advanced) toolbar back as it ships, undoing Edit Toolbar's changes (with `toolbar`, make that toolbar made with New Toolbar blank again); returns its slots

commands.label: New Toolbar…
commands.params: {name?: string} make a blank toolbar called `name`, of at most 200 characters (omitted: a dialog asks for the name), floating beside the Tools panel and listed under Window › Toolbars; its ••• button opens the All Tools drawer to fill it (window.editToolbar with `toolbar`); it is kept with the current workspace; returns {toolbar: name}

commands.label: Show Toolbar
commands.params: {name: string, show?: bool} show (true), hide (false) or toggle (omitted) the toolbar made with New Toolbar called `name`, as its item under Window › Toolbars does (its title bar's × hides it); shown after Tab hid the toolbars, it shows alone and the others are turned off; returns the new state

commands.label: Manage Toolbars…
commands.params: {} open the Manage Toolbars dialog, which lists the toolbars made with New Toolbar: a name typed for the selected one renames it, + copies it (none selected: makes a blank toolbar) and the trash can deletes it

commands.label: Rename Toolbar
commands.params: {name: string, to: string} give the toolbar made with New Toolbar called `name` the name `to` (not empty, at most 200 characters, not another toolbar's whatever the case), as typing a name in Manage Toolbars does; returns {toolbar: name}

commands.label: Duplicate Toolbar
commands.params: {name?: string} copy the toolbar made with New Toolbar called `name`, with its tools, as "`name` Copy" (omitted: make a blank toolbar called "Toolbar N"), as Manage Toolbars' + does; the copy shows and is kept with the current workspace; returns {toolbar: name}

commands.label: Delete Toolbar
commands.params: {name: string} delete the toolbar made with New Toolbar called `name`, and the groups torn off it, from the current workspace, as Manage Toolbars' trash can does

commands.label: List Toolbars
commands.params: {} the toolbars made with New Toolbar in the current workspace: [{name, shown, double, slots}]

commands.label: Shape Mode Buttons Make Compound Shapes
commands.params: {} toggles the Compound Shapes add-on's setting: on, the Pathfinder panel's Shape Mode buttons make a compound shape and Alt-click gives the permanent Pathfinder result; off (the default), the other way round. Members of a compound shape selected always take the mode

commands.label: Pin Bar Position
commands.params: {pinned?: bool} keep the Contextual Task Bar where it is instead of following the selection (true), let it follow the selection again from where it is (false) or toggle (omitted), as the bar's More Options menu does; returns the new state

commands.label: Reset Bar Position
commands.params: {} unpin the Contextual Task Bar and put it back under the selection

commands.label: Panels
commands.params: {} hide the panels, the toolbar and the Control bar, or show again the ones the last Tab hid (all three when none of them shows and Tab hid none); returns whether it showed them

commands.label: Panels Except Tools and Control
commands.params: {} show/hide the dock and the floating panels (hiding them closes a panel popped out of the icon column), leaving the toolbar and the Control bar as they are; returns whether the panels show

commands.label: Show Panel
commands.params: {panel: id, toggle?: bool} e.g. layers, swatches, stroke (case-insensitive; display labels like "Layers" work too); toggle (the Window menu) hides a panel that shows, and shows it again where it was

commands.label: Change Panel Layout
commands.params: {action} serialized docking action, including floating geometry, divider sizes and accordion state

commands.label: Move Panel
commands.params: {panel, anchor, zone?: tab|center|left|right|top|bottom|above|below, before?: panel, group?: bool, placement?} move a panel (with `group`, its whole group) into the group holding `anchor`: as a tab (before the `before` panel; null appends), a split beside it, or (`above` / `below`) a group of its own above or below it in its dock column or floating window; `placement` (a serialized Placement) replaces zone and before

commands.label: Activate Panel
commands.params: {panel} show and select a panel in its current group

commands.label: Close Panel
commands.params: {panel} hide a panel

commands.label: Collapse Panel Group
commands.params: {panel, collapsed?: bool} minimize the group holding a panel to its tabs (in a floating window, the window to its title bar), or restore it, as a double-click on a tab or the drag bar does; the same as window.panel.minimize {panel, minimized}. Without `collapsed` it toggles. Returns {panel, collapsed, layout}

commands.label: Float Panel
commands.params: {panel: id or "tools", x?, y?, width?, height?, group?: bool, column?: bool or n, onto?: id, above?: id, below?: id, collapsed?: bool} float a panel (with `group`, its whole group; with `column`, its whole dock column or floating window) as a floating window with its top-left corner at x, y in window points (default: inside the dock area, cascaded), as dragging its tab out does; a whole floating window keeps its rect unless given one. `onto` makes it a tab of the floating group holding that panel instead; `above` / `below` a group of its own above or below the group holding that panel, in its floating window or dock column. `collapsed` then minimizes (true) or restores (false) its window or group. A hidden panel shows first. "tools" floats the Tools panel at x, y. Returns {layout, closed, floating}

commands.label: Dock Panel
commands.params: {panel: id or "tools", anchor?: id, zone?: tab|center|left|right|top|bottom|above|below, before?: id, group?: bool, column?: bool or n, side?: Start|End, onto?: id, above?: id, below?: id, icon?: bool, collapsed?: bool} dock a panel (with `group`, its whole group): with no destination a floating panel goes back where it floated from (else joins the first dock group) and a hidden one shows where it was; with `anchor` (or `onto`) in the group holding that panel, `zone` as for window.panel.move; with `side`, as a new innermost column of that dock (`column: true` then moves its whole dock column or floating window); `column: n` with no other destination docks its group, or the whole floating window it floats in, as a new dock column at that place (1: next to the icon column, counting inwards; `true`: innermost); `icon: true` puts it in a row of its own at the end of the icon column; `above` / `below` as a group of its own above or below the group holding that panel. `collapsed` then minimizes or restores its group. "tools" docks the Tools panel at the left edge of the window. Returns {layout, closed, floating}

commands.label: Collapse Panels to Icons
commands.params: {collapsed?: bool} collapse every expanded dock column to icons (true), expand the outer dock column, Properties | Layers | Libraries (false), or toggle the outer column (omitted), as the double arrow at the top of the dock does; returns the new state

commands.label: UI Brightness
commands.params: {brightness: dark|mediumDark|mediumLight|light}

commands.label: Workspace
commands.params: {name} switch workspace (Essentials, Essentials Classic, Painting, …): the one left keeps its layout changes, and the one switched to comes back as it was left (as saved if never changed)

commands.label: Reset Essentials
commands.params: {} reset the current workspace to the way it was saved, dropping the layout changes made in it

commands.label: New Workspace…
commands.params: {name?} save the current layout

commands.label: Delete Workspace
commands.params: {name}

commands.label: Rename Workspace
commands.params: {name, to}

commands.label: New Window
commands.params: {} open another view of the current document, with its own zoom, center, rotation, artboard and Outline or Preview, as a tab of its own (titled with the view's number, "Name:2") or, when the current view floats, in a floating window; it becomes the current window; the Arrange commands treat each view as a window; file.close closes the current view and the last view closes the document; returns {index, view}

commands.label: Cascade
commands.params: {} put every open document in a floating window of its own and stack the windows from the upper left of the document area to its lower right, 30 pt apart, in tab order, each fitted to its window, the current document's in front; on the desktop each is an OS window, on the web and Wayland a window inside the app's window; returns {floating} (document indices)

commands.label: Tile
commands.params: {} show every open document and each further view of one (window.newWindow) at once, edge to edge in the document area, one pane each in a grid (columns: the square root of the number of panes, rounded up), each fitted to its pane; the current window's pane takes the tools, a click in another pane makes its window the current one; the tabs stay; windows floating come back under the tabs first; with fewer than two windows open the view stays as it is; returns {tiled, panes}

commands.label: Float in Window
commands.params: {index?, view?, at?: [x, y]} move the current window, or document `index`'s view `view` (its current view without one; it becomes the current window), out of the tab strip into a floating window of its own, fitted to it, with the window's top-left corner at `at` (main window points) or else at the next place of a cascade; dragging a document tab more than 24 pt above or below the tab strip does this at the pointer; the window holding the current document takes the tools, a click in another document's window makes its document the current one; a document already floating stays where it is; returns {floating} (document indices)

commands.label: Float All in Windows
commands.params: {} move every document under the tab strip into a floating window of its own, at the next places of a cascade; returns {floating} (document indices)

commands.label: Consolidate All Windows
commands.params: {index?, view?} show one document at a time again, under its tab, after Tile, Float in Window, Float All in Windows or Cascade; returns {tiled: false, floating: []}; with `index`, only document `index` (its view `view`, else its current view) goes back under its tab and becomes the current one, the other windows and Tile staying as they are, as when a document window is dragged by its title bar (an OS window by the tab at its top) onto the tab strip; returns {tiled, floating} (document indices)

commands.label: Next Document
commands.params: {} make the open document after the current one in tab order the current one, as a click on its tab does (after the last document it goes to the first, and from the Home screen to the first); each view window.newWindow opened is a step of its own; returns {index}, with `view` for a document with more than one view

commands.label: Previous Document
commands.params: {} make the open document before the current one in tab order the current one, as a click on its tab does (before the first document it goes to the last, and from the Home screen to the last); each view window.newWindow opened is a step of its own; returns {index}, with `view` for a document with more than one view

commands.label: Select Tool
commands.params: {tool: id} (see tools)

commands.label: Tool Option
commands.params: {key, value} | {values: {key: value…}}, tool?: id (default: the active tool) → the tool's options (`{}` reads them). The options a tool keeps (Liquify brush and tool options, Mirror & Cut, Puppet Warp, drawing tools…) last across tool switches and are saved with the preferences; another tool's are stored for when it is chosen

commands.label: Effect…
commands.params: {effect: id, index?: int (edit that applied effect in place, prefilled; OK runs effect.setParams), item?: appearance item index|null (the fill/stroke whose effects, null the object's; default: the Appearance panel's active item), aligned?: bool (index and item are rows of the first selected object's stack, which OK edits in each object where it has them, as effect.setParams does)} open the effect's dialog with live preview; without `index`, an effect already in that list first opens `effectExists` (confirm edits it, discard adds another) → {pending: "effectExists"}

commands.label: Command Dialog
commands.params: {command, label?, params} open a parameter dialog for any command

commands.label: Recolor Artwork…
commands.params: {colors?: n (an n-colour job: n rows, Scale Tints) | [colour] (new colours to assign, in order; with no art selected and no group they are the rows, and OK saves them as a new colour group, field `groupName`: the Color Guide's Edit or Apply Colors), library?: id or name; or "document" (Limit to Library; "" the first library), group?: colour group (Edit or Apply Color Group: OK rewrites the group with the new colours and recolours the selected art, if any)} open Recolor Artwork (dialog `recolor`; engine: recolor.reduce / recolor.apply)

commands.label: Crop Image
commands.params: {} show a crop box on the selected image (tool `cropImage`): it starts on the part over the image's artboard; drag its handles or inside it, then Enter or the Control bar's Apply crops the image to it (object.cropImage {rect}), Escape or Cancel leaves it as it is, both back to the Selection tool. tool.setOption {key: "rect", value: [x, y, width, height]} sets the box

commands.label: Repeat Pathfinder
commands.params: {} repeat the last successful Pathfinder panel operation, direct object.pathfinder.* command or command.batch step on the selection with current Pathfinder Options; an error until one has run

commands.label: Save as PDF…
commands.params: {} opens the Save PDF dialog; with params = document.exportPdf options written to path (asked when missing; viewAfterSaving opens the file) → {path, bytes, warnings}

commands.label: Swatch Options…
commands.params: {name} edit a swatch: Swatch Options for a colour (dialog `swatchOptions`, engine: swatch.edit) or a gradient (the same dialog with `name` only; it shows the gradient), pattern editing for a pattern

commands.label: New Swatch…
commands.params: {spot?, global?, group?: colour group name} open New Swatch for the active fill or stroke (dialog `newSwatch`, engine: swatch.new); a color opens as a spot color with `spot`, and as a global process color with `global` alone

commands.label: New Color Group…
commands.params: {swatches?: [names]} open New Color Group, from those swatches or the selected artwork (dialog `newColorGroup`, engine: swatch.newGroup)

commands.label: Color Picker…
commands.params: {stroke?: bool (default: the active proxy), artboard?: index (the picker is for that artboard's background color instead), color?: "#rrggbb"|[r,g,b]|{c,m,y,k}|{gray} (default: the proxy's color, or the artboard's color, white when it has none)} open the Color Picker (fields: hex or color, channel, webOnly, swatches); RGB, HSB and hex values use the working RGB space; OK runs paint.setFill / paint.setStroke, or artboard.setProps {index, color} for an artboard

commands.label: Sample Color from Screen
commands.params: {} or {stroke?: bool (default: the active proxy), picker?: bool (the open Color Picker instead)} show the system's color sampler (macOS; browsers with an EyeDropper) and answer at once; the color the person picks anywhere on the screen then runs paint.setFill / paint.setStroke (one undo step) or becomes the Color Picker's color (field `color`), converted from display sRGB into the working RGB space; Escape cancels it and the colors stay as they were. ui.inspect reports `screenSampler: true` until it answers. An error without a sampler, while one is open, or with `picker` and no Color Picker open

commands.label: New Brush…
commands.params: {ids?} (default: the selected art) open New Brush, what the Brushes panel's New Brush button and art dropped on the panel open (dialog `newBrush`, field `type`: calligraphic|scatter|art|bristle|pattern, Art when there is art, else Calligraphic; scatter, art and pattern need art, else OK gives the error `nothing selected`); OK opens that type's Brush Options for the new brush (dialog `brushOptions` with the fields of ui.brushOptions and `__create`; name: New <Type> Brush, numbered when taken; the `ids` given in `__ids`), whose OK runs brush.new {type, name, params, ids?} (a name another brush has gets a number) and whose Cancel adds no brush

commands.label: Brush Options…
commands.params: {name?} (default: the selected path's brush, else the current brush) open its Brush Options, what double-clicking a brush in the Brushes panel opens (dialog `brushOptions`): Calligraphic (fields name, angle −180..180, roundness 0..100, size 0..1296 pt, angleMode/roundnessMode/sizeMode: fixed|random|pressure, angleVariation/roundnessVariation/sizeVariation), Bristle (fields name, shape, size, length, density, thickness, opacity, stiffness), Scatter (fields sizeMin/sizeMax/sizeMode, spacingMin/spacingMax/spacingMode, scatterMin/scatterMax/scatterMode, rotationMin/rotationMax/rotationMode with modes fixed|random|pressure, rotationRelativeTo: page|path), Art (fields width %, scaleMode: proportional|stretch|betweenGuides, guideStart/guideEnd % of the art length, direction: leftToRight|rightToLeft|topToBottom|bottomToTop, flipAlong, flipAcross) or Pattern (fields scale %, spacing %, fit: stretch|addSpace|approximate, flipAlong, flipAcross); Scatter, Art and Pattern also colorization: none|tints|tintsAndShades|hueShift, keyColor, and tips: true opens Colorization Tips (what each method does, beside a sample of the brush painted with it), as the Tips button beside Method does; OK runs brush.options

commands.label: Graphic Style Options…
commands.params: {name?} open Graphic Style Options (dialog `graphicStyleOptions`, field `name`): for style `name` OK renames it (graphicStyle.rename); without, OK makes a new style of that name from the selection (graphicStyle.new)

commands.label: Character Style Options
commands.params: {name} open Character Style Options (dialog `charStyleOptions`); OK runs charStyle.edit with name, to and sparse attrs in one undo step; Cancel restores a live preview

commands.label: Reset Panel
commands.params: {} clear the settings of the section shown, Basic Character Formats, Advanced Character Formats, Character Color or OpenType Features, in the open Character Style Options or New Character Style dialog; available only on those sections

commands.label: New Character Style…
commands.params: {} open New Character Style (dialog `newTextStyle`, field `name`, filled in with the name charStyle.new {} would give the style), what Alt-clicking the Character Styles panel's New button opens; OK runs charStyle.new with the name and the Type tool's selected characters (else the selected type) as they were when the dialog opened; Cancel adds no style

commands.label: New Paragraph Style…
commands.params: {} open New Paragraph Style (dialog `newTextStyle`, field `name`, filled in with the name paraStyle.new {} would give the style), what Alt-clicking the Paragraph Styles panel's New button opens; OK runs paraStyle.new with the name and the paragraph of the Type tool's selection (else the selected type) as it was when the dialog opened; Cancel adds no style

commands.label: Symbol Options…
commands.params: {name?} open Symbol Options (dialog `symbolOptions`, fields `name`, `exportType`: movieClip|graphic, `registration` 0..8). Without `name` and with a selection: New Symbol (default name the first free "New Symbol"/"New Symbol N", Export Type Movie Clip, Registration centre); OK runs symbol.new {name, exportType, registration}. With `edit: true` or `name`: edit that symbol; OK runs symbol.options {name, newName?, exportType, registration}

commands.label: Tool Options…
commands.params: {tool: id} what double-clicking a tool button opens: hand → fits the artboard in the window (view.fitArtboard), zoom → 100% (view.actualSize), rotate|scale|reflect|shear → that Object › Transform dialog (dialog `rotate`, `scale`, `reflect` or `shear`; error `nothing selected` without a selection), selection|directSelection|groupSelection → the Move dialog (dialog `move`; the same error), gradient|magicWand → the Gradient or Magic Wand panel (window.panel), artboard → Artboard Options of the active artboard (dialog `artboardOptions`, fields index, name, x, y, width, height, showCenterMark, showCrossHairs; OK runs artboard.setProps, and with other artboards selected with the Artboard tool a new width or height goes to each of them too, in its `artboards` list, each resized about the reference point the form used for that size, or about its top-left corner when the size was set in the fields directly), flare → Flare Tool Options (dialog `flareOptions`, fields diameter and pathLength (pt), opacity, brightness, growth, fuzziness, longest, rayFuzziness, largest (%), rays, rings, direction (°), raysOn, ringsOn; OK runs tool.setOption {tool: "flare", values}: the next flare dragged out uses them, and a Flare click's dialog, which also has x, y and preview (on initially), previews one there and accepts it as one Undo step; Cancel rolls back the preview), lineSegment|arc|rectangularGrid|polarGrid → that tool's Tool Options, its click dialog without x and y (dialog kind = the tool id, `__toolOptions: true`; lineSegment: length (pt), angle (°), fillLine; arc: lengthX, lengthY (pt), reference (0–8), arcType: open|closed, baseAlong: x|y, slope (−100…100), fillArc; rectangularGrid: width, height (pt, the Default Size), reference (0–8), rows, columns, rowSkew, columnSkew (%), frame, fill; polarGrid: the same with concentric, radial, concentricSkew, radialSkew and compound for rows, columns, the skews and frame; OK runs tool.setOption {tool, values} and draws nothing: the next drag uses them (Fill Line, the arc's type, base, slope and fill, the grids' dividers, skews and switches) and a click's dialog opens at them), columnGraph|stackedColumnGraph|barGraph|stackedBarGraph|lineGraph|areaGraph|scatterGraph|pieGraph|radarGraph → Graph Type for the selected graph (dialog `command` running graph.setType; an error without one), typeOnPath|verticalTypeOnPath → Type on a Path Options for the selected type on a path (dialog `command` running type.pathOptions; error `nothing selected` without a selection, and the command's error when no type on a path is selected),symbolSprayer|symbolShifter|symbolScruncher|symbolSizer|symbolSpinner|symbolStainer|symbolScreener|symbolStyler → Symbolism Tools Options (dialog `symbolismOptions`, fields tool, diameter (pt), intensity and density (1–10), shared by the eight tools; OK runs tool.setOption {tool, values}), blend → Blend Options, perspectiveGrid → Perspective Grid Options, eyedropper → Eyedropper Options (dialog `eyedropperOptions`, fields sampleSize, pickUp, apply; OK runs eyedropper.setOptions), printTiling → resets the print tiling (print.tiling.set {reset: true}), warp|twirl|pucker|bloat|scallop|crystallize|wrinkle → that tool's Tool Options (dialog `liquifyOptions`, fields tool, width, height, angle, intensity %, usePressure, detail, simplify, simplifyOn, rate, complexity, horizontal %, vertical %, affectAnchors, affectIn, affectOut, showBrush; OK runs tool.setOption {tool, values}), pencil|paintbrush|smooth|blobBrush|eraser → that tool's Tool Options (dialog `freehandOptions`, fields tool and the options the tool keeps: fidelity (px for pencil and paintbrush, the same at any zoom; pt for smooth and blobBrush), fill, keepSelected (on for pencil and paintbrush, off for blobBrush), mergeOnlySelection (off), closeWithin and editWithin (px, 0 is off), livePreview (pencil, on: off draws a thin line while the stroke is drawn, and the path's fill and stroke on release), size (pt), angle (°, −180–180; 0) and roundness (%, 1–100; 100) of the eraser's tip; OK runs tool.setOption {tool, values}), livePaintSelection → Live Paint Selection Tool Options (dialog `livePaintSelectionOptions`, fields selectFills and selectStrokes (both on), color (the highlight color, #rrggbb or a layer color's name; #ff2a2a), width (the highlight's width, 1–20 px; 4); OK runs tool.setOption {tool: "livePaintSelection", values}; a color with an alpha part (#rrggbbaa or #rgba) is an error and OK changes nothing), livePaintBucket → Live Paint Bucket Options (dialog `livePaintBucketOptions`, fields paintFills (on) and paintStrokes (off), highlight (on), color (the highlight color, #rrggbb or a layer color's name; #ff2a2a), width (the face highlight's width, 1–20 px; 4; an edge's highlight is half as wide); OK runs tool.setOption {tool: "livePaintBucket", values}; a color with an alpha part (#rrggbbaa or #rgba) is an error and OK changes nothing), shapeBuilder → Shape Builder Tool Options (dialog `shapeBuilderOptions`, fields gapDetection (off), gapLength (pt, 0–72; 3), openFilledAsClosed (on), clickStrokeSplitsPath (off), pickColorFrom: artwork|swatches (artwork), cursorSwatchPreview (off), selection: freeform|straightLine (freeform), highlightFill (on), highlightStroke (on), highlightColor (#rrggbb or a layer color's name; #ff4f4f); OK runs tool.setOption {tool: "shapeBuilder", values}; a highlightColor with an alpha part (#rrggbbaa or #rgba) is an error and OK changes nothing), objectsOnPath → Objects on Path Tool Options (dialog `objectsOnPathOptions`, fields pivot (0–8, row by row from the top left; 4, the center) and rotate (°, −360–360; 0); Reset puts 4 and 0 back; Save runs tool.setOption {tool: "objectsOnPath", values}: the objects attached next use them, groups attached before keep theirs)

commands.label: Color Guide Options…
commands.params: {} open Color Guide Options (dialog `colorGuideOptions`, fields `steps` 1–20 and `amount` 0–100): OK sets the Color Guide panel's variation grid (read back with `ui.inspect`: ui.color_guide; engine: color.harmony)

commands.label: Adjust Color Balance…
commands.params: {} open Adjust Colors for the selection (dialog `colorBalance`, fields `mode` gray|rgb|cmyk|global, channels r g b / c m y k / gray / tint (global) −100..100, `convert`, `fill`, `stroke`, `preview`): previews live, OK runs edit.colors.adjustBalance as one undo step

commands.label: Saturate…
commands.params: {} open Saturate for the selection (dialog `saturate`, fields `intensity` −100..100, `preview`): previews live, OK runs edit.colors.saturate as one undo step

commands.label: Swatch Library
commands.params: {library: id or name (see swatch.library.list), or the id of a persistent panel's missing library | null (close every swatch library panel)} open the swatch library in a read-only panel of its own, floating (panel id `library:swatches:<id>`, which window.panel.* moves, docks and closes), or bring its panel forward when it is open; clicking a swatch there runs swatch.library.add with apply. ui.libraryPanel sets its view, find field and Persistent (ui.inspect: ui.library_panels) → {open: id, panel, name, count}

commands.label: Other Library…
commands.params: {path?} (default: pick a file) load a .vcswatches, .gpl, .ase or .acb (color book) library, or another document's swatches (engine: swatch.library.load), and open it in its library panel

commands.label: Library Panel Options
commands.params: {panel: a library panel's id (`library:swatches:pastels`, as window.swatchLibrary answers), library?: id or name of another library of its kind to show in the panel (Previous / Next Library; one open in a panel of its own is brought forward instead), view?: smallThumb|mediumThumb|largeThumb|smallList|largeList, showFind?: bool, persistent?: bool (reopen the panel when the app starts)} set an open library panel, or a closed persistent one's view, Show Find Field and Persistent; kept with the preferences (ui.inspect: ui.library_panels) → {panel, kind, library, view, showFind, persistent, open}

commands.label: Locate Library…
commands.params: {panel: an open library panel's id, path?} (default: pick a file) Locate Library… of a persistent library panel whose library's file is missing: load the library from the file, as Other Library… does, and show it in the panel, which keeps its view, Show Find Field and Persistent. When the file's library has a panel open already, the panel closes and that one is brought forward, made persistent when the closed one was → what ui.libraryPanel answers

commands.label: Save Swatch Library…
commands.params: {names?: [the swatches selected in the Swatches panel]} open Save Swatch Library (dialog `saveSwatchLibrary`: name, format: vcswatches|gpl|ase|css, user: save to the user library folder, selectedOnly); OK runs swatch.library.save

commands.params: {} open the 1. User Defined swatch library (swatch.library.list, category user)

commands.params: {} open the 2. User Defined swatch library

commands.params: {} open the 5. User Defined swatch library

commands.params: {} open the 7. User Defined swatch library

commands.params: {} open the 9. User Defined swatch library

commands.label: Rename Action
commands.params: {set: index, action: index, name} rename the Actions panel's action at action in set (0 is the top set) to name, with spaces trimmed from both ends; its steps, function key and color stay. An index past the last set or action, or an empty name, is an error and renames nothing → {name}

commands.label: Include Action Steps
commands.params: {set: index, action?: index, step?: index, included: bool, others?: bool} include or exclude the playback of every step in a set, every step in one action, or one step. With a step and others: true, leave that step unchanged and apply included to every other step in its action (Alt/Option-click). Invalid indexes change nothing → {set, action?, step?, included}

commands.label: New Action
commands.params: {set: index, name, key?: 0-15, cmd?, shift?, color?: red|yellow|green|blue|violet} add an action named name (spaces trimmed from both ends) after the last action of the Actions panel's set at set (0 is the top set) and start recording into it; Stop Playing/Recording (ui.action.stop) ends the recording. key 1 to 15 is the function key F1 to F15 that plays the action (0 or null: none), with cmd (Ctrl, Command on macOS) and shift; color is its Button Mode color (null or "": none), which the panel does not show. Action function keys take priority over command shortcuts and preserve the command's binding. On Windows F1, Ctrl+F4 and Ctrl+F6 cannot be used. The set becomes current and the new action is selected. The panel's Create New Action button and menu's New Action… (dialog `actionNew` with set, name, key, cmd, shift and color) run this on Record. While an action is recording, and for an index past the last set, an empty name, or a key or color that is not one of these, it is an error and nothing is added → {set, action}

commands.label: Action Options
commands.params: {set: index, action: index, name?, key?: 0-15, cmd?, shift?, color?: red|yellow|green|blue|violet} change the Actions panel's action at action in set (0 is the top set); its steps stay. name renames it (spaces trimmed from both ends), key 1 to 15 with cmd (Ctrl, Command on macOS) and shift sets the function key F1 to F15 that plays it (0 or null: none), and color sets its Button Mode color (null or "": none); a param left out keeps what the action has, and cmd or shift alone changes that modifier of its key. Action function keys take priority over command shortcuts and preserve the command's binding. The panel menu's Action Options… (dialog `actionSetOptions` with set, action, name, key, cmd, shift and color) runs this for the selected action. An index past the last set or action, an empty name, or a key or color that is not one of these is an error and changes nothing → {name, key, color}

commands.label: Play Action
commands.params: {action: name, set?: name} play the Actions panel's action named action at the speed ui.action.playbackOptions sets; set names the set to look in (default: every set). Accelerated plays it as one undoable batch → what command.batch returns. Step by Step and Pause For play its first step now and the others one at a time, each its own undo step, until the last, ui.action.stop, or a step that comes due while a different document is active than after the step before → {results: [the first step's result], pending: the steps left}. An action with a stop, at any speed, plays up to the stop and waits until ui.action.continue or ui.action.stop; at Accelerated the steps between stops are one undoable batch each → {results, pending, atStop?: true when it already waits}. A name no action has, or one that more than one action in the sets looked in has, or an action played while another is still playing step by step or with pauses, is an error and nothing plays

commands.label: Playback Options
commands.params: {speed?: accelerated|step|pause, seconds?: 1-60} set how the Actions panel plays actions: accelerated (the default) plays every step at once, step plays one step at a time and draws the window after each, and pause waits seconds (a whole number, 1 to 60, VectorCraft's own range) between steps. A param left out keeps its value; the setting is kept with the UI preferences. Any other speed or seconds is an error and changes nothing. The panel menu's Playback Options… (dialog `actionPlayback` with speed and seconds) runs this on OK → {speed, seconds}

commands.label: Begin Recording
commands.params: {set?: index} begin recording an automatically named Action N in the Actions panel's set at set (0 is the top set), by default the current set or the first set; with no sets, make Set 1. The set becomes current, and ui.action.stop adds the recorded action after that set's existing actions. An explicit invalid set or an existing recording is an error and changes nothing → {set, name}

commands.label: Stop Playing/Recording
commands.params: {} end the Actions panel's recording and keep its steps, in the action ui.action.new made for it, else in a new action after the last action of its set, as the panel's Stop Playing/Recording button does. It also ends an action playing step by step or with pauses, or one waiting at a stop, whose message box closes: the steps played stay and the rest do not run. With nothing recording or playing it changes nothing → {stopped}

commands.label: Insert Stop
commands.params: {set?: index, action?: index, step?: index, message?, allowContinue?: bool} insert a stop, at which a playing action waits and shows message. With set and action (0 is the top set or action), the stop goes into that action, after step, else after its last step; without them it goes into the recording in progress, after the steps recorded so far. message defaults to none, and allowContinue, which offers Continue in the message box, defaults to false. A stop in an action becomes the panel's selected step, and its action and set become the selected ones. An index past the last set, action or step, a param of another type, params that are not an object, or no action and no recording is an error and changes nothing. The panel menu's Insert Stop… (dialog `actionStopRecord` with message, allowContinue, set, action and step) runs this on OK → {set, action, step}, or {recording: true}

commands.label: Continue Action
commands.params: {} play on from the stop the Actions panel's playing action waits at, on the document active now, and close the stop's message box (dialog `actionStopMessage`): the next step runs at once, or at Accelerated the steps up to the next stop as one undo step. The panel's Play Current Selection runs this while an action waits. With no action waiting at a stop it is an error → {results, pending, atStop?}

commands.label: Delete Action Step
commands.params: {set: index, action: index, step: index} delete one step, a stop or a command, of the Actions panel's action at action in set (0 is the top set, action or step). The steps after it keep whether they are excluded, and no step of that action stays selected. A Record Stop dialog open on that step closes, and one open on a later step of the action follows it up. A missing or invalid index is an error and changes nothing. Undo does not bring the step back. The panel's Delete Selection runs this for the selected step → {set, action, step}

commands.label: Batch…
commands.params: {set?: index, action?: index} open Batch (dialog `actionBatch`) for the action at set/action (default: the first action of the first set); OK runs action.batch with the dialog's source, destination and overrides

commands.label: Save Actions…
commands.params: {set?: index, id?, path?} write the Actions panel's set at set (0 is the top set; default: the current set) with its actions to an action set file (.vcactions) at path, else a picked file named after the set (the web downloads it). id holds the panel's own set id, which its menu passes: the set with this id is saved wherever it is now, and set is not read. A set over 8 MiB as a file, with more than 1,000 actions or with an action of more than 10,000 steps is not written; the panel menu's Save Actions… → {path}

commands.label: Load Actions…
commands.params: {path? | data?: the file's text} read an action set file (.vcactions) at path, else a picked one, and add its set after the Actions panel's sets; a set named like one in the panel gets the next free number (Print 2), and the other sets stay. Files of another version, over 8 MiB, with more than 1,000 actions or with an action of more than 10,000 steps are refused; the panel menu's Load Actions… (disabled where there is no open dialog, the web) → {set: index, name, actions: n}

commands.label: Delete Action Sets
commands.params: {sets?: [index], ids?: [id]} delete the Actions panel's sets at these indexes (0 is the top set), with their actions (default: the current set). ids holds the panel's own set ids, which its question passes: the sets with these ids are deleted wherever they are now, sets is not read, and when one of them no longer exists nothing is deleted. The panel's Delete Selection on selected sets (Shift-click adds a range) asks first, and OK runs this. A recording into a deleted set stops and keeps nothing. An index past the last set is an error → {deleted: n}

commands.label: Duplicate Action or Action Set
commands.params: {set?: index, action?: index} copy the Actions panel's action at action in set (0 is the top set) to right after it in the same set; without action, copy set with all its actions to right after it (default: the current set). The copy is named after the original with " copy" added, a copied set gets an id of its own, and the copy is selected. The panel menu's Duplicate runs this for the selected action, else the current set. An index past the last set or action is an error → {set, action?}

commands.label: Show Package
commands.params: {folder} show a package folder (file.package's folder) in the file manager → {folder}

commands.label: Save Document Info…
commands.params: {path?, selectionOnly?, category?} write Document Info's text report (document.info {format: "text"}) to path, else a picked file (the web downloads it); with category (a document.info category id) only that category, else every category. The panel menu's Save… passes the category the panel shows and its Selection Only → {path}

commands.label: EPS Options Dialog
commands.params: {path?, useArtboards?, range?, …document.exportEps options} open EPS Options (dialog `epsOptions`: fields = these options over the ones used last); OK checks them, remembers them and writes path (else asks). Export As… → EPS opens it too

commands.label: Save for Web (Legacy)…
commands.params: {} open Save for Web (dialog `saveForWeb`: fields = the webExport.settings settings, `preset` loads a preset, __view: original|optimized|2up|4up, __zoom, __kbps; Save… remembers the settings and writes the files, Done only remembers them); with settings = document.exportForWeb, written to path, else a picked file (the web downloads the files) → {path, files, bytes}

commands.label: Preview in Browser
commands.params: {…document.exportForWeb settings} write the HTML page and its images to a temporary folder and open the page in the default browser (desktop) → {path}

commands.label: Export Selection…
commands.params: {multiple?: false} collect the selected objects as assets (assets.add: one of them all, as one image; true: one per object) and open Export for Screens on its Assets tab with them checked → {assets: [asset id…]}; document.exportSelection exports the selection in one go instead

commands.label: Copy Selected Style
commands.params: {scope?: selection|all (default selection), …css.selection options} copy the CSS of the selection (css.selection; all: css.generate) to the clipboard (CSS Properties panel) → {css, rules: n}

commands.label: Export CSS…
commands.params: {path?, scope?: selection|all (default selection), …css.selection options} css.export written to path, else a picked file (the web downloads it), with the pictures of rasterized art next to it (CSS Properties panel: Export Selected CSS…, Export All…) → {path, rules, images: [path…], warnings (css.export's; the status bar shows the first)}

commands.label: Print…
commands.params: {} open the Print dialog (dialog `print`: the print.setup settings, preset (setting it loads that print preset; Save Preset… saves them as one), printer, toFile; Print keeps the settings with the document and prints, Done (discard: true) only keeps them); with params {preset? (a print preset's name: its settings instead of the document's), settings? (over the document's or the preset's), printer? (print.printers name; "" the default), toFile?, path?, format?: pdf|postscript, level?, flattenerPreset? (as engine file.print)} print without it: the print-ready PDF (engine file.print) goes to the printer → {pages, printer, printed: true, warnings}; with toFile, a path or no printing here (no print service) it is saved as a PDF at path (else a picked file, the web downloads it) → {path, pages, printed: false, warnings}; a PostScript file (format postscript, or a .ps path) is always saved that way

commands.label: Print Preset
commands.params: {name?: a saved preset to edit | preset?: the preset a new one starts from (default [Default])} open the preset editor (dialog `printPreset`: the Print dialog's settings fields plus `name`); OK runs print.presets.save and returns to Print Presets

commands.label: Plug-in…
commands.params: {id: an object filter plug-in (plugin.list), params?: {…}} Object › Plug-ins: run the filter at once when it takes no parameters or params are given (plugin.run), else open its dialog (dialog `plugin`: a field per parameter, `__plugin` the id, live preview; OK runs plugin.run as one undo step)

commands.label: Install Plug-in…
commands.params: {path?: a .wasm file | dataBase64?: the module, name?: the file name shown as its source (with dataBase64), allowHeavy?: bool (the user agreed to its heavy budget), grant?: [permission] (the permissions the user granted it), replace?: bool, hash?: the module's SHA-256 (as plugin.install)} install a WebAssembly plug-in (plugin.install); without a path pick one (the web opens the browser's file picker; File › Open of a .wasm installs it too). A plug-in that lists permissions the user hasn't granted it asks the user first, showing its name, id, version, file SHA-256 and what each permission lets it do, and so does a filter that asks for a heavy budget: OK installs it if the file still has the SHA-256 shown, Cancel installs nothing → plugin.install's result | {pending: "confirm"} while it asks

commands.label: Cancel Plug-in Run
commands.params: {} stop every heavy filter running in the background (its progress window's Cancel): it stops at the next slice of its budget and changes nothing → {cancelled: n}

commands.label: Continue in Background
commands.params: {} close the progress window of the heavy filters running in the background; they go on, shown in the status bar → {hidden: n}

commands.label: Cancel Image Trace

commands.label: Continue in Background
commands.params: {} close the progress window of the Image Traces running in the background; they go on, shown in the status bar → {hidden: n}

commands.label: Blend Options…
commands.params: {} open Blend Options (Object › Blend › Blend Options…, the Blend tool's double-click, Alt-click and toolbar button; dialog `blendOptions`: spacing smooth|steps|distance, steps, distance (pt), orientation page|path, preview) on the selected blend's options, previewed live: OK runs object.blend.options as one undo step; with no blend selected it sets what new blends start with

commands.params: {} open Gap Options (Object › Live Paint › Gap Options…; dialog `livePaintGapOptions`: detect, size small|medium|large|custom, custom (pt), color (#rrggbb or a layer color's name), closeGaps, preview) on the selected Live Paint groups, filled in from the first; with preview on, the options apply live and the gaps found draw on the canvas in the preview color: OK runs livePaint.gapOptions as one undo step; a color with an alpha part (#rrggbbaa or #rgba) is an error and OK changes nothing, and with preview on a #rrggbbaa color is not previewed: the groups keep their own color and the gaps draw in black

commands.label: Library Folders
commands.params: {} → [{name, path, count, own, volume, selectable, label?, children}] the disks and the folders the library's photos were imported from, with photo counts (subfolders included in `count`); show one with library.source {kind: libraryFolder, path} (rows with selectable false only open)

commands.label: Remove Folder from Library
commands.params: {path, disk?: bool} — move the library photos imported from this folder (and the folders inside it) to Recently Deleted; one undo step, no file is touched. A whole disk or share (`/Volumes/nas`, `C:\`, `\\srv\share`) goes only with `disk: true`, the startup disk never → {removed}

commands.label: Set Folder Color Label
commands.params: {path, label: red|yellow|green|blue|purple|none} — give a folder of the library (one its photos were imported from, see library.folders) a colour label, or take it off (also once its photos are gone); one undo step. The label follows the folder when it is renamed or moved with folder.rename / folder.move → {path, label}

commands.label: Enable Filters
commands.params: {} — with a filter set, puts it aside and shows everything; with one put aside, brings it back as it was (stars, flag, text… together). Setting or clearing a filter while it is off forgets the one put aside → {enabled, count}

commands.label: Sort
commands.params: {key?: captureDate|importDate|editDate|fileName|rating|fileSize|random, ascending?: bool, group?: auto|none|day|month|year, seed?: u64 (the shuffle `random` gives)}

commands.label: Refresh View
commands.params: {} — show what matches now: a view that holds its photos (`library.holdView`) lets go of the ones that stopped matching a smart album's rules, Picks or the filter bar since it was opened, sorted or last refreshed

commands.label: Hold View Until Refreshed
commands.params: {on?: bool (toggles when omitted)} → {hold} — when on, an edit that makes a photo stop matching the view (a keyword given in a smart album of photos without keywords, a flag taken off in Picks, a rating under the filter bar's) keeps it in the view until `library.refresh`, Reshuffle, or another source, filter or sort; photos that start matching still appear at once, and deleting a photo or taking it out of the album or folder shown still takes it out of the view. Changing a smart album's rules is another view too. Off (the default): the view follows every edit. Kept with the library's preferences; asking for the state it already has changes nothing

commands.label: Reshuffle
commands.params: {seed?: 0..2^53-1} — sort at random; without `seed` a new shuffle each time

commands.params: {} → [{field, label, kind (text|keywords|number|date|choice|bool|album: an album id), group (field-menu submenu, null at the top level), ops: [{op, label}], choices? (ids), choiceLabels? ({id: label})}] for ruleSet rules, in menu order

commands.label: Review Import
commands.params: {paths: [file or folder (recursive)]} → {candidates: [{path, name, format, kind, width, height, fileSize, captured, duplicate?: path|content, existing?, error?, previewOnly?: why a raw can only be shown from its embedded preview}], duplicates, scanned, scanLimited: bool (the folder walk stopped at its scan limit: there may be more photos), skipped: {unreadable (folders that could not be listed), unsupported (files in the folders that are not a supported photo type, XMP sidecars not counted; a file named in paths is always tried)}} — nothing is added

commands.label: Import Photos
commands.params: {paths: [file or folder (recursive)], mode?: add|copy|move (add = reference the files in place; copy = into the library's Originals/YYYY/YYYY-MM-DD/; move = as copy, then each original and its XMP sidecars are removed from the source — only after the copy is verified (a hard link on the same volume, else copied, synced and compared byte for byte) and its catalog record is saved; commands.label: Read Focus Points in the Background

commands.label: Un-precompose
commands.params: {layer?, force?, dryRun?} → {layers, warnings}: expands the selected pre-comp layer into its composition's layers (copies, in order, with timing and position carried over). A locked pre-comp layer is refused, changing nothing. What would change the picture (the pre-comp layer has a parent, matte, effects, masks, layer styles, a non-default Scale/Rotation/Opacity, an animated transform, time remap/stretch, a blending mode, Video/Audio off, Solo/Guide on, is 3D/collapsing/adjustment, is used by another layer or named in another layer's expression; or the nested comp has cameras, lights, adjustment, 3D, collapsing, soloed or blend-mode / Preserve Transparency layers, preserves another frame rate, has another motion-blur shutter, or has Position expressions the move can't reach) is an error listing the reasons, changing nothing, unless `force`: then it unpacks anyway in one undo step, drops what the pre-comp layer carried, removes other layers' parent/matte/property links to it and lists the reasons as `warnings`. `dryRun` returns {dryRun, warnings} and changes nothing
