commands.label: Share with a join code
commands.params: {via?: "online" (default: the open file is kept on the server in Preferences, `pref.publishServer`, and the server hands out the codes) | "local" (this app hosts it for people on the same network; no server), access?: "edit" (default) | "comment" (online only: view and comment, not edit) | "view" (look only: their edits are refused): which code `code` is, server? (online: another server's address, with ?key=… when it needs its key), key? (online: the server's key, when the address has none), name? (online: the file's name there), port?, bind?: "lan" (default) | "local" (this machine only) | an IP address (local)} → the open file's session as `collab.peers` gives it: `code` is what others type to join (`collab.join {code}`, the Join field), `link` the invite link to give with it and `url` its WebSocket URL (local: the ones that go with `code`, so a view-only code's link and URL let people look only; online: your own link to the file, which edits: `share` has the link that goes with each code). Local: at once, the code carries the host's IPv4 address, port and secret (K7M2Q-…, 20 symbols), and `share` is {via, access, shared, editCode, viewCode, editLink, viewLink}: the edit and view-only ways in, each with its own secret (commentCode and commentLink null). Online: status "connecting" first; once live `code` is the server's (K7M-2QX-9TD) and `share` is {via, access, shared, editCode, viewCode, commentCode, editLink, viewLink, commentLink}: links made for others (commentCode and commentLink null from a server older than comment links) (the file's own links in `published` stay yours); `code` stays null when the server is older than join codes (give `share.editLink` / `share.viewLink` instead). Called again while shared: only switches which code `code` is (`access`). Called after `collab.stop` on a file that is still on the server: new links and codes for that same file (nothing is published twice). `collab.stop` stops sharing

commands.label: Stop live session
commands.params: {} → {ended}: the open file's session ends (a session this app hosts stops for everyone; a joined one is left). A file shared online with `collab.share` is different: its sharing stops → {ended: false, shared: false}: the links and codes others got are revoked on the server, whoever joined with them is disconnected at once (they keep their copy), and you stay in the file, which stays on the server, open only to you (`collab.share` shares it again with new codes; `collab.leave` leaves it there; `collab.manageFile {action: "remove"}` with its owner token takes it off the server)

commands.label: Join live session
commands.params: {code | link (a join code: K7M-2QX-9TD from a server, asked at the server in Preferences; a longer one for the local network; spaces, dashes and case don't matter, O reads as 0 and I or L as 1; or an invite link: figcraft://join?host=…&file=…&token=…, figcraft://join?server=ws(s)://…&file=…&token=… or ws(s)://host:port/?file=…&token=…, from a session an app hosts or a server's share link; either key takes either)} → the new session: {session, status: "connecting", …}; its file opens in a tab of its own (other files' sessions go on) and `collab.peers` tells when it's live (`sessions` lists it until then, and if it fails)

commands.label: Reconnect live session
commands.params: {} → {status}: for the open file's session when it is disconnected: a reconnect that is waiting tries now, and a session that couldn't go on (`failed`, the file open in its tab) is joined again there, what you changed since going on top (your whole version opening beside it when some of it can't). Refused when nothing was lost

commands.label: Leave live session
commands.params: {session? (a session's id from `collab.peers`'s `sessions`, e.g. a join still on its way; default: the open file's session)} → {ended}: the synced file stays open as a local copy (also how a tab stops showing a session that couldn't go on)

commands.label: Publish to server
commands.params: {server: ws://host:port/?key=… or wss://host/path/?key=… (the server's address with its key; `figcraft-server key` prints it; without a key on a server open to the public), key? (when the address has none), name? (default: the file's name)} → status "connecting": the open file is uploaded as a new file and this tab syncs through the server; `collab.peers` then has `published: {server, file, name, edit, view, owner (published without a key: the owner token, shown once), expires (seconds since 1970, or null)}` and `hosting` (the server's operator, terms and idle expiry)

commands.label: Server info
commands.params: {server: ws://host:port/ or wss://host/path/} → {open (anyone may publish without the key), operator, terms (a web address), idleDays (files published without the key are deleted after this many days unopened; null: kept), maxFileMb, expires}

commands.label: Manage published file
commands.params: {file (its id), server?, owner? (the server's address and the owner token you got when you published the file without the key; each defaults to what is recorded for one of your online files, see `collab.files`), action: links | createLink | revoke | share (others get new links and join codes) | unshare (the links and codes others got are revoked; the file stays yours on the server) | rename | remove (the file is deleted from the server and leaves your online files), access? (createLink: view (default) | comment | edit), label? (createLink), link? (revoke: a link's id), name? (rename)} → {links: [{id, access, label, created}]} | {id, access, link (a new share link, shown once)} | {shared, code, viewCode, commentCode, editLink, viewLink, commentLink} | {done}

commands.label: Report file to server operator
commands.params: {reason (a few words, at most 500 characters)} → {sent}: the file you joined on a server is reported to its operator; the session's message says when the server kept it (servers older than this app don't take reports)

commands.label: People in this file
commands.params: {} → the open file's session (each open file has its own or none): {available, canHost (false in the browser: it can only join), session (its id; null: this file isn't in a session), status: off|connecting|live|reconnecting|failed, reason?, role, me, name, color, fileName, pages, link, url, address, network, access: edit|view|comment (view: a view link or code, a server's or a local network share's, edits are refused; comment: a server's comment link, edits other than to comment threads are refused), readOnly (the open file can't be edited now: view only, comment only, or being published), published (a file you published: {server, file, name, edit, view}), code (the join code to give others, when the file was shared with `collab.share`; null otherwise or while it is on its way), share ({via: online|local, access, shared (false: a file of yours on a server that nobody else gets into now), editCode, viewCode, commentCode, editLink, viewLink, commentLink (what others join with; null when not shared)} or null), follow, syncing, document (index of the synced open document), editing (the text layer you type in: {node, layer, caret, selection}), peers: [{id, name, color, editing (theirs, same shape, or null), presence: {cursor: [page, x, y], selection, viewport: [page, x, y, w, h], editing_text}}], sessions: [{session, document (index of its open document; null for a join on its way), status, reason, role, fileName, link, peers (how many others)}] (every session of the app)}

commands.label: Remove from session

commands.params: {on? (default: toggle)} → {spotlighting}: everyone in the session follows your view and page until they move theirs

commands.params: {refresh? (true: ask each server once what became of its files, and the server in Preferences for its team list; default false: no network)} → {files: [{server, host, file (its id), name, created, opened (seconds since 1970), shared (others get in with a code now), code, viewCode, commentCode (the join codes, while shared; commentCode null from a server older than comment links), state: unknown | online | gone (the server no longer has it: removed or expired), expires, session, document (the session and open document it is in now, or null), hasOwnerToken: true}], problems: [{server, host, state: offline | unsupported (a server older than this request), reason}], max, team: {server, host, state: listed | none (the server keeps no team list) | offline, reason, web (where its browser build is, or null), files: [{file, name, updated, people, access, link (figcraft://join?server=…&file=…&team=1: joins it, no secret in it), webLink (the same in the browser build, or null)}]} or null (not asked yet)}: the files you published or shared without a server key, most recently opened first, as recorded on this computer with the preferences, and the files shared now on the server in Preferences when its operator keeps a team list (everyone who reaches it may open them; `collab.join {link}` does). Owner tokens and your own links are never in the result

commands.label: Open online file

(when files on several servers have that id)} → {session, status: "connecting", document, alreadyOpen, file, server, name}: joins the file as its owner in a tab of its own (`collab.peers` tells when it's live; `collab.share` and `collab.stop` there start and stop its sharing); a file that is open already comes to the front instead (alreadyOpen: true)

commands.label: Forget online file
commands.params: {file, server?} → {forgotten, file, server, onServer}: drops the file from the list on this computer only. The file stays on its server until it expires, and without its owner token it can't be managed from here again (`collab.manageFile {action: "remove"}` takes it off the server instead)

commands.label: Recover online file
commands.params: {path (a recovery copy of one of your online files), file, server?, session, client, seq, secret? (who the app was in the file when the copy was written, and the server's last change it had: from the note beside the copy)} → {session, status: "connecting"}: joins the file again as its owner and keeps the copy until the file arrives. Then: the server has everything in the copy → nothing more; the copy has changes of yours the server never confirmed and nothing else changed there → they are applied on top as one edit ("Recovered changes", synced to everyone); anything else changed meanwhile → the copy opens beside the file as “<name> (recovered copy)”; the file can't be joined → the copy opens as an unsaved document. The session's message says which

commands.label: Draw Table

In the app the button turns the pen on.)

commands.label: Eraser
commands.params: {"page": n, "x": pt, "y": pt} (removes the border between two cells within 4 pt of the point: cells that make one rectangle merge, including cells merged down the same rows; otherwise the border is hidden along the whole edge. In the app the button turns the eraser on.)

commands.label: Resize Table by Dragging
commands.params: {"page": n, "x": pt, "y": pt, "toX": pt, "toY": pt, "shift"?: bool, "ctrl"?: bool, "reach"?: pt} (a mouse drag in page points, 0-based page, starting on a table border or the resize handle: a column border moves (the column to its right gives or takes the difference, so the table keeps its width; with ctrl the columns right of it share it in proportion; with shift, or on the table's right edge, only the column left of it changes); the table's left edge moves a left-aligned table's indent, the first column making up the difference (a centred or right-aligned table keeps its alignment: only the first column changes); with cells of the table selected, a border of theirs moves only in their rows; a row's bottom border sets that row's height; the handle just outside the bottom-right corner scales every column and the rows on that page. `reach` (default 3) is how near the start has to be.)

commands.label: Select Table Cells by Clicking
commands.params: {"page": n, "x": pt, "y": pt, "toX"?: pt, "toY"?: pt, "reach"?: pt, "extend"?: bool, "anchorRow"?: n} (a click in page points, 0-based page, on a selection area of a table in the caret's story: just above a column selects the column, left of a row the row, along a cell's left edge inside it the cell, the move handle past the top-left corner the table; with toX/toY (a drag) every column, row or cell from there to that point; the page margin beside a table (its leading side: right for a right-to-left table) is a row area too, and `extend` (Shift+click) on one takes the rows from the selected ones' anchor, or from row `anchorRow` (0-based) when given, so a drag keeps its press's anchor. `reach` (default 3) is the column borders' resize reach, which the cell areas keep clear of.)

commands.label: Insert Row or Column by Clicking
commands.params: {"page": n, "x": pt, "y": pt, "reach"?: pt} (a click on a table's insert button: left of a row border adds a row there, above a column border a column; the new row or column is selected, as in Word)

commands.label: Move Table by Dragging
commands.params: {"page": n, "x": pt, "y": pt, "toX": pt, "toY": pt, "reach"?: pt} (a drag from the move handle past a table's top-left corner: the table floats where it's dropped, the text wrapping around it; tables in the main text only)

commands.label: AutoFit Column by Double-Clicking
commands.params: {"page": n, "x": pt, "y": pt, "reach"?: pt} (a double-click on a column border: the column left of it fits its contents and the columns right of it keep their widths, moving with the border, so the table narrows or widens (up to the right margin), as in Word)

Writes Answer, Sensitivity and Limits reports on new sheets before the model's sheet; Sensitivity and Limits need Simplex LP or GRG Nonlinear and no integer constraints, and Sensitivity a Max or Min objective. data.solver's result can be passed as is.

commands.label: Save Model
commands.params: {to: "H1" (the first cell, on the model's sheet), model?: data.solver params (default the sheet's saved model), overwrite?: false} → {range}. Writes the model down a column as formulas: =MAX(objective), =MIN(objective) or =objective=value; =COUNT(variables); one =AND(relation) per constraint (=AND(x=INT(x)) for integer, =AND((x=0)+(x=1)) for binary), which shows TRUE while it holds; and the options as an array constant {method (1 GRG Nonlinear, 2 Simplex LP, 3 Evolutionary), non-negative (1 yes, 2 no), population size, mutation rate, random seed, require bounds (1 yes, 2 no), convergence, generations without improvement, maximum evaluations, integer optimality %}, which spills into the cells to its right. Refused, with the sheet unchanged, when the model's cells, content, another formula's spilled values, merged cells or a table are in the way of the options' spill, or it would run off the sheet, and when the column would cover another formula's spilled values. A column that holds a value or a formula (a model saved there before included) is replaced only with overwrite: true; without it the command is refused ("already holds data"), as Excel asks first. One undo step.

commands.label: Load Model
commands.params: {from: "H1:H6" (a range on the active sheet; one cell reads down to the first cell without a formula; a range needs a formula in every cell up to its last formula, and may end in empty cells)} → {model}. Reads a model written by Save Model and makes it the sheet's Solver model. The model must end with its options row ({…}), which Save Model writes last; a model cut short (a cell before the options row without a formula, or the options row cleared) is refused and the sheet's model stays as it was.

commands.label: Reset All
